The proposed method shows superior performance compared to the previous state-of-the-art, with improvements in ODS, OIS, and AP of 1.1%, 4.7%, and 2.7%, respectively, and qualitatively demonstrates improved edge detection and classification performance.

articleTitle: Group-Theoretical Perspective of Tree Editing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Tree Editing Distance is a widely applied quantity for measuring the similarity between hierarchical data structures, particularly trees. This paper reinterprets the TED problem using group action theory, exploring the connection between tree editing operations and permutation groups. By formulating node insertion, deletion, and relabeling as group actions, we offer a novel perspective on tree transformations. This group-theoretic and metric-based approach provides new insights into the structure of tree similarity and introduces new possibilities for TED applications in various fields.

Author Keywords: tree editing distance permutation group group action

articleTitle: Feature Alignment in Vision Mamba to Resolve Domain Shift of Mobile Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Integrating deep learning models into mobile medical devices has led to remarkable growth in medical diagnosis and healthcare applications. In particular, the recently emerged vision mamba (ViM) has been attracting attention because it shows better accuracy than mobile-specific models and is very suitable for mobile environments where computational efficiency and memory management are important. However, there is still a lack of research on domain shift, which hinders its application in the field. To address the domain shift issue in this study, we design and integrate a squeeze and excitation layer-based auxiliary network (SEAN) into the ViM block to perform a feature alignment strategy. This enables robust performance under different domains, and in experiments on Camelyon17, a medical dataset, the proposed method achieves 0.6% and 3.2% performance improvement on ViM-Tiny and ViM-Small models, respectively. Furthermore, we show that unreliable data can be extracted using the designed SEAN, which is expected to enable more sophisticated medical diagnosis in fields where resource constraints are evident.

articleTitle: AI-Based Bitrate Selection Method for CMR-Supported Audio Codec
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: When using a codec that supports CMR (Codec Mode Request) for voice calls, the audio data receiver can request a real-time change in the encoding bitrate from the sender in order to enhance the user experience in various network environments. The bitrate selection problem has a tradeoff characteristic, and it should be considered that the selection at a particular point in time can affect the next state. Reinforcement learning is effective in solving such problems. In this paper, we propose a method of selecting an appropriate bitrate by training a reinforcement learning model using the E-MODEL, which predicts user experience of audio data, and the network statistics of the RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol) protocol. Performance evaluation was conducted by implementing AMR-WB (Adaptive Multi-Rate Wideband) application, RTP, and JBM (Jitter Buffer Management) model in the NS3 simulator environment and simulating both congested and stable network condition. The evaluation results show that the AI model outperformed the fixed bitrate approach by lowering the encoding bitrate in congested networks and increasing the encoding bitrate in stable networks as the learning progresses. This study demonstrates the possibility of improving the user experience of voice calls by selecting encoding bitrates in real-time according to network conditions through reinforcement learning.

articleTitle: CAM-Based High Efficient Weakly Supervised Multi-Object Multi-Class Detection Method
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Two approaches are available for WSOD: MIL and CAM. MIL-based methods are capable of addressing multiple targets and multiple class problems. However, these methods require the input of region proposals. In contrast, CAM-based methods are straightforward and more efficient, yet they are constrained by limited localization accuracy and are likely to be applicable only to single target classes. This study proposes a CAM-based WSOD method that is capable of addressing multi-object, multi-class tasks with high efficiency, which could prove beneficial for the development of specific consumer electronic applications, such as smart cameras and smart home devices. The proposed method was evaluated on two public datasets, demonstrating that it is significantly more efficient than the baseline method.

articleTitle: Non-Contact Sleep Stage Estimation in Adult and Infant Sleep Using Millimeter Wave Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Monitoring sleep is important from a health perspective and is of great interest to society. A sleep monitoring method that does not require wearing sensors is needed for daily use. This study investigates the performance of a non-contact sleep stage estimation system using a millimeter wave sensor and a machine learning model. This sensor emits radio waves to a subject and detects reflected waves superimposed with physiological signals. The sensor then calculates respiratory rates, body motion, and heart rates, using this information. Nine healthy adults <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({24.4\pm 6.0}\ \text{years})$</tex> and four infants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({2.4\pm 1.7}\ \text{years})$</tex> participated in the experiments. Four sleep stages were estimated from millimeter wave sensor data. Thirty different features extracted from respiratory rates, body motion, and heart rates were input into an Extremely Randomized Trees Classifier (Extra Trees classifier). As a result, the model achieved an overall accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${50.0\pm 6.4\%}$</tex> and a Kappa coefficient of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${0.26\pm 0.10}$</tex> for adult sleep. For infant sleep, the results were <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${37.5\pm 3.5\%}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.03 {\pm\ 0.07}$</tex>, respectively. The performance showed the potential for millimeter wave sensors to be used for daily measurement of sleep at home.

articleTitle: Tiny Objects Classification on Remote Sensing Image by Using Multi-Scale Crop
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Classifying tiny objects in remote sensing images (e.g., a 20x20 pixels target within a resolution 1000x1000 image) is a significant challenge. This paper adopts a fused FPN (Feature Pyramid Network) to enhance the feature extraction capability for tiny objects. Additionally, the proposed multi-scale crop method can more effectively focus on the target objects. This network architecture improves overall accuracy by 14.4%.

articleTitle: Metaverse Public Lab -1.0
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Metaverse has a high level sociability. In this study, we consider the metaverse as a society and propose Metaverse Public Lab as a space to investigate it. Different from ordinary experimental spaces, Metaverse Public Lab exists in the users' living space and aims to be an environment where data is collected naturally while users play the metaverse. As the first step of Metaverse Public Lab, we constructed a space to measure users' sense of embodiment (the sense that arises when a body's properties are felt in the same way as those of the innate body) toward an avatar. This is because avatars are essential for social interaction, and heavy users inevitably use avatars for long periods of time, so the results are expected to be different from those in normal laboratory experiments. This space is implemented on the metaverse, so that anyone can conduct experiments without coming to a physical laboratory. Many heavy users live in the metaverse, which could contribute to the collection of a lot of specific data and to the automation of experiments.

articleTitle: Numerical Formulation of Throughput Maximization for Wireless Multi-Hop Networks Using Spring Model Approximation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper discusses an algorithm for maximizing throughput in wireless multi-hop networks. Since the problem of maximizing network throughput is a combinatorial optimization problem, traditional approaches often rely on heuristics. In this paper, we formulate a method to efficiently solve the through-put maximization optimization problem by approximating the optimization problem with a mechanical spring model. The main contributions are as follows. By using an approximation based on the spring model, the problem is divided into two sub-problems: position optimization using quadratic programming and topology optimization through the minimum spanning tree. As a result, we proposed an efficient algorithm through the alternating optimization of these well-known algorithms. Additionally, by separating the problem into two optimization sub-problems guarantees algorithmic convergence. In the numerical examples, we demonstrated that the use of approximate calculations allows for real-time optimization, while also showing that the method can be flexibly applied to various network topologies.

articleTitle: Selective Classification Using Soft Labels
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Recent developments in deep learning have increased the use of artificial intelligence for extracting and evaluating information in business operations. In this context, selective classification is commonly used to meet business accuracy requirements and reduce human workload. Selective classification rejects low-confidence inference results and requires the separation of correct results from incorrect ones. To achieve this separation, it is essential to reduce the number of incorrect results that have high confidence levels. We hypothesized that the separation performance could be improved by suppressing the variations in the model outputs during the learning phase. Thus, we propose a new training method that uses a new approach of soft labels to achieve this goal. The validation experiments we conducted using the CIFAR10 dataset showed that the separation performance surpassed that of the existing methods.

articleTitle: A Linear Search Algorithm for Resource Allocation in Frequency Domain Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a linear search algorithm for resource allocation in frequency domain non-orthogonal multiple access based on the low-density signature (LDS). Although the proposed linear search enables the non-orthogonal multiple access to achieve superior transmission performance, the proposed linear search makes the resource allocation implemented with lower and fixed computational complexity. The performance of the non-orthogonal access based on the proposed linear search is evaluated by computer simulation. The proposed linear search algorithm makes the non-orthogonal multiple access achieve a gain of about 6 dB at the BER of 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> when the overloading ratio is set to 2. The complexity of the non-orthogonal access based on the proposed linear search algorithm is approximately half as much as that of the conventional low complexity resource allocation when the overloading ratio is 2, if the complexity is evaluated in terms of the number of additions.

articleTitle: Point Cloud Live Streaming System Using Scalable Point Cloud Partitioning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, point cloud streaming has attracted attention. Point cloud provides with higher reality and immersiveness. To reduce the file size of point cloud, some data compression methods such as video-based point cloud compression (V-PCC) are presented. However, most of methods are not suitable for point cloud live streaming due to the processing time of data compression. In this paper, we propose a point cloud live streaming system using scalable point cloud partitioning. The proposed method reduces file size by partitioning point cloud data into multiple layers and streams them sequentially, aiming to improve the number of rendered points and reduce playback interruptions (stalling). We implement the proposed system on actual devices and conduct performance evaluations.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Based Segmentation for Skin-Layer Visualization from Optical Coherence Tomography Images
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Changes in epidermal thickness are linked to various skin diseases, such as diabetic foot. Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT), a noninvasive imaging technology, enables detailed visualization of skin layers. This study employed a deep learning approach using the U-Net architecture to analyze OCT images, specifically focusing on the stratum corneum (SC) and epidermis (ED) layers. Utilizing a dataset of 10,000 images, the U-Net model achieved 92 % accuracy in predicting SC and 95% accuracy for ED. These results highlight the potential of this method for accurate 3D visualization of SC and ED layers, paving the way for precise assessment of skin layer thickness and its changes in medical applications.

articleTitle: Authentication Method Using Bluetooth for University Security Guards
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: On many Japanese university campuses, people can freely enter and exit during the day. However, for security reasons, only authorized people can stay at night. Therefore, security guards often patrol the campus at night. Furthermore, students do not always wear name tags when on campus, making it necessary to determine whether individuals have permission. Therefore, we propose a method that allows security guards to easily determine whether a person is authorized through the use a smartphone, Specifically, an application that uses Bluetooth low energy (BLE) is proposed to make the determination even in the dark.

articleTitle: Eye Image and EOG Signal Conversion via Autoencoders for Human-Machine Interaction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Converting between EOG signals and eye images allows for adaptive gaze-based systems, enabling real-time visualization of eye movements in healthcare and low-cost gaze-tracking in consumer electronics. This study presents a bidirectional mapping framework between eye images and electrooculography (EOG) signals, enabling intuitive and hands-free human-machine interaction (HMI). A generative autoencoder was trained over 7000 epochs to map 2-D eye images to 1-D EOG signals and back, using a 2-step decoder structure for enhanced accuracy. The training utilized a dataset of synchronized EOG and eye image data from 30 participants. Experimental results showed that the model successfully reconstructed key EOG patterns and eye images, achieving an average image correlation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.9582 (\pm 0.0068)$</tex> and EOG correlation values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.6825(\pm 0.3272)$</tex> for horizontal and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.6526 (\pm 0.3000)$</tex> for vertical signals, with minor noise noted in fine EOG details. These findings suggest that the proposed model can reliably transform between EOG signals and eye images. It has the potential to provide a promising basis for accessible, gaze-based HMI systems in consumer electronics. Future work will focus on refining detail accuracy and multimodal integration.

articleTitle: Anti-Aliased Convolutional with Data Augmentation for Speech Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this work, we propose a comprehensive framework for speech emotion recognition that combines advanced data augmentation techniques and an innovative deep learning architecture to enhance model performance. Our data augmentation strategies, including noise addition, time stretching, pitch shifting, and time shifting, significantly diversify the training dataset, leading to improved generalization and robustness against real-world variations in speech. We introduce a novel deep learning model architecture based on Anti-Aliased Convolutional (AA-Conv1D) layers, which preserves spatial hierarchies and enhances the model's ability to capture fine-grained emotional nuances in speech signals. Experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a weighted accuracy of 79.38%, which surpasses the performance of existing models, SepTr + LeRaC and EMix-NS.

articleTitle: A Particle Swarm Optimization Approach for Maximizing Bottleneck Link Capacity in Network Routing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As network technologies advance, the capacity for data transmission across networks continues to grow. Efficiently transmitting large volumes of data requires routing strategies that account for link capacity. However, conventional shortest path routing algorithms are not well-suited for high-volume data transfers. To address this, we consider the maximum bottleneck link (MBL) problem, which seeks to identify paths that avoid low-capacity links as a first step in the routing problem for efficient transfer of large amounts of data in large networks with complicated constraint. In this paper, we propose an adaptation of particle swarm optimization (PSO) to solve the MBL problem, taking advantage of the strengths of combinatorial optimization. We evaluate the feasibility and performance of the PSO method through simulations, comparing it to a Dijkstra method under various conditions. The simulation results demonstrate the validity of our approach and its superior performance compared to the conventional method.

articleTitle: Development of Optimal Insertion Path Algorithms for Radiofrequency Ablation in Tumor Surgery and AR Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The study is based on the need to develop an algorithm to identify the optimal penetration path for inaccessible lesions, for instance, brain tumors and liver cancer, using radiofrequency needles. Applying the K-D tree method, which can significantly reduce computation time compared to conventional methods, aims to decrease both surgical time and associated risks. Furthermore, integrating augmented reality (AR) technology through Head-Mounted Display(HMD) such as the HoloLens can assist surgeons in visualizing and identifying the legions more accurately and safely during actual surgical procedures. The experimental results demonstrate an improvement in precision by at least 23% compared to the baseline method.

articleTitle: Enhancing Human-Computer Interaction: An Accurate Video-Based American Sign Language Translation Model Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: American Sign Language (ASL) is the primary communication method used by individuals who cannot speak or hear well. Only about 2.8% of the United States population is proficient in ASL, making communication challenging and inconvenient for people who use ASL. To address this issue, we have developed a model that processes video data and translates ASL fingerspelling signs into English letters. We evaluated several approaches to achieve this goal, with the most effective method involving splitting the video into frames, followed by using Google's MediaPipe Library to extract information on the locations of hand landmarks in each image. The extracted points were then normalized and fed into a classification model. The models tested include Random Forest, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression. The training phase yielded accuracies of 98% for the Random Forest model, 97% for the XGBoost model, and 94% for the Logistic Regression model. However, the Logistic Regression model outperformed the other models for generalization. Our model demonstrates robust performance despite variations in hand color, camera position, background, and other potential distractions, noted as roadblocks in prior research. This work contributes to enhancing Human-Computer Interaction for individuals who use ASL.

articleTitle: Multi-Dementional Feature Engineering for Reliable Detection Method of Vehicles with Location Information Errors in Spatio-Temporal Data Retention System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The widespread adoption of IoT devices has led to increased sensor data. Among the data, we defined spatiotemporal data (STD) as data that depends on both time and space. We proposed a spatiotemporal data retention system (STD-RS) that uses vehicles to retain and utilize STD within a specific spatial area. However, in STD-RS, errors in vehicle location information can cause data to be transmitted outside the target area. Previously, we proposed a method to detect abnormal vehicles by learning the distance and received signal strength indication (RSSI) of the vehicle and then confirmed that the method can detect abnormal vehicles with an accuracy of approximately 80%. However, the previous method did not consider vehicles that cannot generate features for learning in this paper. Moreover, as the evaluation was conducted in a single (ideal) environment only, the validation of effectiveness in practical environments remains. In this study, we use the sufficiency rate of data necessary for feature generation as an evaluation metric and evaluate how the spatial and quantitative changes in the combination of features for learning impact the sufficiency rate and detection accuracy under practical environments. The simulation evaluation results revealed the factors that affected the sufficiency rate and demonstrated that using the long-term spatial variation of RSSI as a feature improves the detection accuracy in any environment.

articleTitle: A Multi-Chip-Module-Based Architecture Simulator for Scaling Vision Transformer Inference
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have achieved remarkable performance in various computer vision tasks. However, they demand significant computational and memory bandwidth, making them difficult to efficiently run on a monolithic accelerator, particularly in edge computing environments. A multi-chip module (MCM)-based architecture, which incorporates multiple accelerator modules with a chip-to-chip (C2C) interface, offers a promising solution for scaling and accelerating ViTs. Unfortunately, estimating the performance of an MCM system for ViT inference is challenging, as existing ViT acceleration simulators primarily target monolithic designs without considering C2C communication. To address this shortcoming, this paper proposes an MCM-based architecture simulator to estimate the impact of C2C bandwidth and the number of chips on latency and energy efficiency when scaling ViT inference. The experimental results show that increasing the number of chips and reducing C2C bandwidth can significantly affect performance due to C2C communication overhead. The framework helps identify optimal design configurations, balancing trade-offs within given constraints.

articleTitle: TextureMeDefect: LLM-based Synthetic Railway Defect Texture on Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Texture image generation has been studied for various applications, including gaming and entertainment. However, context-specific realistic texture generation for industrial applications, such as generating defect textures on railway components, remains unexplored. A mobile-friendly, LLM-based tool that generates fine-grained defect characteristics offers a solution to the challenge of understanding the impact of defects from actual occurrences. We introduce TextureMeDefect, an innovative tool leveraging an LLM- based AI-Inferencing engine. The tool allows users to create realistic defect textures interactively on images of railway components taken with smartphones or tablets. We conducted a multifaceted evaluation to assess the relevance of the generated texture, time, and cost in using this tool on iOS and Android platforms. We also analyzed the software usability score (SUS) across three scenarios. TextureMeDefect outperformed traditional image generation tools by generating meaningful textures faster, showcasing the potential of AI-driven mobile applications on consumer-grade devices.

articleTitle: Strategic Application of Prompt Engineering in Multi-Modal Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLM), which integrate large language models (LLMs) with vision models, aim to overcome the text-centric limitations of traditional LLMs. While models like GPT-4 and PaLM-E excel at processing text data, they face limitations in complex fields such as medical image analysis and cross-modality reasoning. MLLMs enhance understanding and reasoning by combining textual and non-linguistic data, such as images, expanding their applicability across various domains. This study proposes optimization strategies for effectively handling multimodal inputs through prompt engineering techniques. We evaluate three MLLMs–Llama-3.2, Phi-3.5, and Qwen2–VL-using datasets such as Flickr30k, NoCaps, and MSCOCO, and analyze their performance on tasks including image captioning, object recognition, and scene understanding. Furthermore, a comparison of the impact of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) and In-Context Learning (ICL) techniques on model performance shows that CoT is more effective for tasks requiring logical reasoning, while ICL enhances adaptability across diverse scenarios.

articleTitle: Automation of Node Redundancy for Stable Operation of Various Types of Blockchain Nodes
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper describes automation of node redundancy for stable operation of many types of blockchain nodes. In recent years, traditional large companies have gradually begun to consider the use of public blockchains. When using blockchain for mission-critical purposes, it is necessary to operate a large number of nodes to increase redundancy and ensure stable operation. However, as public blockchain technology is rapidly advancing and the number of types is increasing, it is difficult for many companies to efficiently operate nodes. To overcome this difficulty, Ginco Inc. developed a system on the cloud that mainly consists of three main technologies. By automatically creating a snapshot of a volume containing chain data and attaching it to a new node, Ginco Inc. reduced the time required to start up a node. Additionally, in order to prevent requests from clients from being routed to nodes with low chain block heights, Ginco Inc. implemented a function for the load balancer to grasp the block height of each node. Furthermore, when reassigning clients to nodes due to a node failure, Ginco Inc. is able to do the reassignment evenly by using consistent hashing as the mapping algorithm. Using these automatic redundancy technologies, Ginco Inc. was able to implement node services for about 30 types of blockchains with just a few infrastructure engineers. The node services have continued to operate without any large system failure for over 5 years since its launch.

articleTitle: Physical Fatigue Evaluation Using Muscle Modeling
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Physical fatigue during labor work or exercise in daily life is inevitable but harmful. Current in-lab approaches to evaluate fatigue use objective measurements like EMGs, motion capture systems, and ground reaction force to assess the fatigue level of the test subjects, while, clinically, fatigue levels are scored subjectively by participants' perceptions and might be inconsistent. In this paper, we aim to link the gap between the subjective scoring and the objective evaluation by using a three-compartment muscle model with measurements from EMG and PPG sensors. In comparison with the Borg CR-10 scale (scale from 0 to 10), the model has a mean square error of 0.91. The study presents a quantitative way for researchers in exoskeletons and human-robot interactions to evaluate the effects of their robots.

articleTitle: DFTIMP: Distributed Fake Traffic Injection from Multiple Points for Obfuscation of IoT Traffic
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in smart homes has raised user privacy concerns through various attacks by analyzing wireless communication traffic. Such attacks often use machine learning algorithms to identify device categories and working states to map them to user behavior. Traffic obfuscation such as packet padding, packet shaping, and fake traffic injection can address these kinds of user privacy inference attacks. However, such traffic obfuscation methods generally rely on a single injection device and cannot scale effectively as network size increases. To overcome this issue, we propose DFTIMP (Distributed Fake Traffic Injection from Multiple Points) for obfuscation of IoT traffic. We conducted experiments to evaluate the effectiveness of traffic obfuscation reducing the overhead of each device. Experimental results show that the proposed method reduces the overhead of individual injection devices without degrading their obfuscation effectiveness, making it suitable for application to large networks.

articleTitle: Self-Position Estimation of Moving Equipment Using a 360-Degree Camera and UAV Marker
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Industries are demanding robust communication and accurate self-positioning capabilities for autonomous machines. To address the limitations of GNSS in environments such as canyons and underground spaces, this study proposes a new self-positioning system using a 360-degree camera. By detecting pre-positioned markers with known coordinates in the captured 360-degree image, this system enables accurate self-position estimation in challenging environments where GNSS is not available.

articleTitle: Research on OLED Panel Exciter Speakers for New Sound Experiences in Vehicle Interiors
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The advancement of display and semiconductor technologies has facilitated the mass production of OLED panels. Research initiated in 2017 has led to the development of a novel sound emission system called Crystal Sound OLED (CSO), which involves directly vibrating the OLED panel to produce sound. This innovation has spurred various technological enhancements aimed at improving the sound quality of the panel speaker, achieving superior spatial sound, implementing multi-channel exciter speakers, and aligning the focus of sound with that of the screen a challenging feat in traditional LCDs. In this study introduces the application of this technology in automotive environments, enhancing the in-vehicle sound experience through the use of information devices. The proposed method utilizes the OLED panel speaker for delivering essential information to drivers, thereby ensuring more accurate voice transmission and enhancing sound quality in conjunction with the vehicle's door trim-mounted sound system. Additionally, this approach allows for a distinct and secure auditory experience both inside and outside the vehicle.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Multi-Lead ECG Monitoring for Early Cardiovascular Disease Detection and Cuffless Blood Pressure Estimation in Smart Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study introduces an AI-driven multi-lead ECG real-time monitoring system designed for cardiovascular disease detection and blood pressure estimation, integrated within the framework of smart healthcare. By utilizing deep learning techniques, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), the system accurately detects Premature Ventricular Contractions (PVCs) from multi-lead ECG signals, significantly improving diagnostic precision. Additionally, it implements a cufftess blood pressure estimation method by combining ECG and photo-plethysmography (PPG) signals through Pulse Transit Time (PTT) features. The system is deployed on the Nvidia Jetson Nano embedded platform, offering real-time processing, low power consumption, and continuous monitoring, which is ideal for remote health management. Experimental results highlight its ability to enhance early detection of cardiovascular conditions, showcasing its integration within smart healthcare systems to support personalized health management and remote monitoring.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Debanding Method Based on cGAN Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Banding artifacts, marked by the staircase-like contours in smooth areas, are mainly caused by quantization or compression algorithms and can severely degrade image quality and structure. Traditional debanding methods, such as the dithering quantization, are limited by fixed parameters and struggle with large regional artifacts. Recent techniques using conditional generative adversarial networks (cGANs) aim to address these issues across entire images. However, without proper guidance, cGANs can be disrupted by color distortions in non-flat regions, leading to unnatural colors in flat areas. To overcome this, we propose a two-stage network: first, a flat area segmentation network generates a mask for flat regions, which then guides the debanding network. This approach effectively removes banding in flat areas while avoiding unnatural colors and preserving details in non-flat regions. Our method demonstrates substantial improvements both visually and quantitatively over existing techniques.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of the LLM Models on LLM-Based Seed Generation Method for IoT Device Fuzzing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The proliferation of IoT devices has increased the need for device security measures. Recently, an method of initial seeds generation utilizing an LLM (Large Language Model) for IoT device fuzzing (LLM-based seed generation method, in short) has been proposed to reduce the cost and improve the efficiency of vulnerability detection. However, various LLMs have been released in recent years, and existing studies have not adequately evaluated their adaptability to various LLM models. In this paper, we compare the seeds generation and the associated fuzzing results by the LLM-based seed generation method among the various LLM models of Vicuna v1.5, Mistral, Phi-3, and Llama 3. Comparison experiment results show that Mistral, Phi-3, and Llama 3 detected many vulnerabilities with high conformance rates of the seed format.

articleTitle: Automatic Classification of Personal Space Using Wearable Sensor Data
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Appropriate distance between individuals is crucial for building relationships. In The Hidden Dimension [1], Edward T. Hall highlights that the right distance fosters trust, while misjudgment can undermine relationships. This study focuses on Hall's “Distance in Man” concept, aiming to classify personal space during interactions (e.g., poster sessions) using wearable sensors. We applied binary classification to Hall's four distance categories, grouping “Intimate” and “Personal” distances as “Private Distance” and “Social” and “Public” distances as “Formal Distance.” Two cases for explanatory variables were explored: one where only the Bluetooth signal strength, i.e., the Received Signal Strength Indicator (hereafter referred to as RSSI) (transmitted by the wearable sensor and received by the smartphone), and another combining RSSI with the heart rate correlation. RSSI estimates physical distance, as radio waves attenuate over space, but obstacles and interference can distort the signal. To address this, we integrated heart rate data, linked to psychological states and interpersonal distance, to classify distances reflecting communication quality. The classification accuracy using only RSSI was 0.340, while combining it with heart rate correlation improved it to 0.441. Accuracy was evaluated using Cohen's Kappa.

articleTitle: Highly Reliable Oracle Provisioning Infrastructure for Blockchain-Based Distributed Metaverse
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Blockchain that is a decentralized data management platform is attracting much attention recently. Recent advancement of blockchain technology increases the demand and supply of Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) that enable management of ownership concepts for various digital contents. Especially in the metaverse, NFT contents such as images and videos are actively used to facilitate communication within the virtual space. However, systems and technologies that link NFT content in the metaverse with metaverse platforms and generate metadata (e.g., popularity of each content) from data created through user's activities in the metaverse (e.g., user attention, conversation audio) are not realized. Therefore, our research aims to provide highly reliable data regarding the popularity and evaluation function of NFT content. To achieve the objective, we focus on extending existing oracle mechanisms and developing a system that integrates NFT content and various data generated on the metaverse platforms. The oracle technology to handle data provision and verification processes allows users within the metaverse to mutually verify reliability of the data generated through interactions with NFT content. Additionally, the proposed platform enables the use of common devices (e.g., smartphones) as wallets for the blockchain. These common devices can be used to sign transactions through short-range wireless communication when sending data to the blockchain through devices constituting the metaverse platform. This approach ensures user's involvement in data transmission procedure while simultaneously enabling mutual verification of the transmitted data through the blockchain to achieve both wallet security and data reliability.

articleTitle: A Plugin-Based Testing Tool in an Adaptive Automated Testing Infrastructure for Consumer Electronics Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Automated testing plays a crucial role in agile software development by enabling continuous quality assessment of Systems Under Test (SUTs) throughout the development lifecycle. However, implementing automated tests for embedded systems, such as digital TV receivers and smartphones, poses significant challenges. This paper introduces the Plugin-Based Testing Tool (PBTT), a flexible and scalable tool designed to facilitate test execution and provide a graphical interface for visualizing test results. The PBTT architecture supports the seamless integration of various SUTs and simplifies the development of new plugins. A plugin has been implemented to validate adaptability of PBTT, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving software quality by streamlining the testing process and enhancing result analysis.

articleTitle: Radiation Degradation Evaluation of the Dynamic Configuration Circuit on An Optically Reconfigurable Gate Array VLSI
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant was melted down by the earthquake and tsunami in 2011. The decommissioning tasks must be executed under a high radiation intensity. For the tasks, we have been developing a radiation-hardened optically reconfigurable gate array with 1 Grad total-ionizing-dose tolerance. In this device, dynamic optical parallel configuration architecture was introduced to increase the radiation tolerance. However, the radiation degradation evaluation has never been done up to now. This paper presents the first evaluation results of the dynamic optical parallel configuration circuit on an optically reconfigurable gate array VLSI.

articleTitle: Seamless Producer Consumer Execution on GPU/NPU Accelerated Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel scheme to eliminate CPU interventions when executing a neural network on multiple HW IPs, such as GPU and NPU. We delegate the role of data synchronization in CPU into GPU and NPU, so that GPU and NPU directly work together as a producer or a consumer seamlessly without CPU interventions. Experimental result shows that our scheme reduces execution time and power consumption simultaneously, so that our scheme can be effectively used for neural network execution on mobile devices.

articleTitle: A Winograd-Convolution-Based Accelerator on FPGA for Real-Time Object Detection with Effective On-Chip Buffer Access Patterns
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A convolutional neural network (CNN) based object detector typically requires billions of multiplications, making it difficult to achieve a real-time end-to-end inference on FPGA. To reduce the number of multiplications, Winograd convolution (WinoConv) appears promising in accelerating CNN-based object detectors. However, designing a generic real-time WinoConv-based accelerator on FPGA is challenging since it requires effectively executing various layers, for example, 3×3 and 1 ×1 layers with strides 1 and 2. To address the problem, this paper proposes a WinoConv-based engine on FPGA for real-time object detection with effective line buffer access patterns. Specifically, we propose a simple yet effective dataflow to process tiled input and output tensors with a stride of 2, mitigating an overhead to reorder feature maps between layers. To enable practical use of the engine, we introduce a hardware-friendly post-training quantization scheme, achieving a negligible accuracy drop, i.e., less than 1% in mean average precision (mAP) for a Tiny-YOLOv3 model on the VOC dataset. Our engine is implemented with Verilog HDL and deployed on a Xilinx Zynq ZCU106 FPGA board. The experimental results show that our engine achieves a latency of 5.134ms to inference a custom Tiny-YOLOv3 model, resulting in a throughput of 292.18 GOPS at the clock frequency of 125 MHz on a real-time video stream. The engine utilizes 1053 DSPs and 105 BRAM.

articleTitle: Fairness Issues of ABR Video Streaming Over TCP from Application and Transport Views
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: DASH video streaming is now major traffic in the current Internet. Adaptive bitrate algorithm operated in the application layer and TCP congestion control algorithm in the transport layer decides selected bitrate of each segment while affecting each other. In this paper, we discuss fairness issues of ABR over different TCP algorithms. In this paper, we especially focus on congestion window validation which has not been installed in widely used network simulator ns-3. We install it on ns-3 and our evaluation results newly reveal that TCP behavior affected by congestion window validation might be one of the reasons for unfairness between ABR bitrate selection over different TCP versions.

articleTitle: Smart Rollator Walker for Enhanced Mobility
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We introduce a new mobility aid - an intelligent rollator walker and navigation assistant - as a personal assistive device for mobility and independence of the elderly and persons with mobility and/or vision impairment. It uses simultaneous localization and mapping with object and collision detection to facilitate safe navigation in a wide range of environments including indoors, outdoors, sidewalks, beaches, etc. and is equipped with an extensive computer vision system. It is also motorized to assist a user in pushing heavy cargo across rough terrain such as dirt paths and pebble beaches.

articleTitle: Personalized Course Selection Optimization Using QAOA
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is an algorithm for solving combinatorial optimization problems (COP), which can be implemented on gate based quantum computers. However, many practical COPs such as a personalized course selection problem (PCSP) have not been solved by QAOA yet. In this paper, we solve a PCSP using QAOA by transforming the problem into a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO), and investigate the solution properties when the weight of the problem's constraint is changed. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that tuning the weight value improves the probability of obtaining optimal solutions and reduces the energy expectation value averaged over the obtained feasible solutions.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Compression for Semantic Video Communications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Deep neural network-based video coding systems are emerging to become mainstream video coding standards. However, a key challenge is the efficient transmission of neural network parameters between transmitters and receivers. We introduce a novel neural network transmission framework that integrates Versatile Video Coding (VVC) and semantic communication principles to transfer the parameters of the Deep Neural Network (DNN) between the transmitter and the receiver by exploiting the spatial correlation between the weights and biases to optimize them for each video scene. The effectiveness of the proposed network compression model was evaluated by comparing the bitrate required to transmit ten different videos with that of the state-of-the-art NNCodec. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently achieves lower bit rates while maintaining comparable video quality, outperforming NNCodec, and is a potential solution to reduce bandwidth requirements for transmission of neural network parameters in video transmission, as well as in more generalized applications.

articleTitle: Maintaining Consistency During Content Updates Using CCN Control in Peer-To-Peer Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to implement a query control function similar to Content-Centric Network (CCN) in the application layer of a pure Peer-to-Peer network to maintain the consistency of the shared content even when it is updated, and at the same time to reduce the load on the network. The effectiveness of the method is evaluated by using computer simulations.

articleTitle: Real-time Identification of Badminton Hitting Actions Using Video and Human Key Point Heat Maps
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Badminton is a fast-paced sport known for its rapid reflexes and strategic gameplay, often requiring players to execute precise and quick movements. Traditionally, analyzing badminton strokes involves manual recording and analysis, which can be time-consuming. This research addresses these challenges by leveraging key points of the human body and video data. By implementing computer vision and deep learning methods, we reduce errors in observing players' hitting actions. We designed a model to identify various badminton hitting actions using video data and key point heat maps. Initially, our study involved collecting badminton game videos and extracting key point heat maps to identify hitting ranges. Using key point detection algorithms like HRNet, we detected 17 key points in each frame. These key points were used to create heat maps, with pixel values representing the confidence of each key point. The heat maps were then fused with video data as input for the deep learning model. We employed the 3D CNN deep learning method, known for its spatio-temporal feature extraction capabilities, to develop a model for identifying badminton strategies. Through training, the model learned to extract features from the fused input data and classify shot types. After numerous iterations and optimizations, the model effectively predicted badminton actions from video clips. This approach has the potential to enhance badminton performance analysis and improvement, making it a valuable asset for the sport.

articleTitle: Semantic Communication Based Lossless Distributed Video Coding for Error Prone Channels
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Video coding is crucial for modern communications, but traditional methods with complex encoders limit their utility in many emerging consumer electronic applications. Distributed Video Coding (DVC), which shifts encoding complexity to the decoder, is a promising alternative but requires decoder feedback, limiting its practicality. We propose a semantic communication-based DVC system for lossless video coding, featuring a low-complexity semantic-based video encoder coupled with turbo channel code. The proposed codec significantly outperforms in terms of encoder complexity while maintaining better rate distortion performance at low channel signal-to-noise ratios compared to the state-of-the-art Versatile Video Coding based codec in power constrained consumer video sensors.

articleTitle: Artificial Marker-Aided Localization for Service Robots in Visually Repetitive Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) has emerged as a critical technique for enabling the autonomous capabilities of service robots. However, practical SLAM applications often face significant performance challenges in visually and geometrically repetitive environments, which impede accurate localization. To address these challenges and ensure reliable localization for service robots, this work utilizes artificial markers, specifically AprilTags and ArUco tags. This paper presents a method that strategically leverages these markers, using them in minimal quantities while maximizing their localization impact. By leveraging the Kimera-VIO and TagSLAM algorithms, the proposed approach offers several contributions: (a) consistent pose estimation through a lightweight pose-graph optimizer suitable for resource-constrained systems; (b) an efficient strategy for optimizing the placement of artificial markers within target environments; and (c) validation of the proposed method in real-world environments, including warehouses and offices, using a commercially available service robot. This approach provides a viable industrial solution for improving localization performance in commercial service robots.

articleTitle: Abnormal Behavior Detection Network System Using 3D LiDAR for Station Platforms
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Despite various countermeasures implemented by railway companies, human accidents related with railways continue to occur. The railway companies are installing platform doors on station platforms to prevent accidents that a passenger falls off the platform. However, the installation of platform doors costs up to several billion yen per station, as well as the cost of upgrading station platforms for installation. On the other hand, it is clarified that there are predictive behaviors for drunken passengers falling from platforms. By detecting this behavior, the accidents could potentially be prevented. In the existing studies, a system that tracks the movement trajectory of a human by analyzing data from 3D LiDAR sensors that can accurately measure the distance, position, and shape of the object, installed at multiple locations are proposed and developed. However, these studies focus on estimating movement trajectories and do not address abnormal behavior such as drunken behavior detection. Additionally, they do not consider real-time processing capabilities, which is a significant limitation for the critical situations. Therefore, in this study, we propose a system that detects the abnormal behaviors of human on station platform by analyzing 3D point cloud data taken by 3D LiDAR. This system observes the behavior of individuals on the platform. By extracting point cloud data corresponding to individuals, observing their movement trajectories, and analyzing them by a machine learning model for anomaly detection, the proposed system aims to identify abnormal behaviors. Furthermore, the proposed system reduces processing time by extracting only points corresponding with a human from the point cloud data observed at station platforms.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Privacy Protection Solution: Enhancing Face Obscuring Techniques with Automated Identification, Mobile Integration, and Scalable Services
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We propose a novel application aimed at protecting personal privacy. With the proliferation of various media platforms, issues related to personal portraits have emerged. To address these problems, previous applications propose methods for either Mosaic or replace it with another object. However, existing methods suffer from issues such as high time costs and unnatural rendering. To address these problems, we propose designing an automatic face identification and replacement system by combining face detection, super-resolution, and face replacement models. This approach aims to reduce processing time and enhance natural rendering. In addition to the technological advancements, we suggest expanding this system into a mobile service, allowing users to easily protect their privacy on the go. This mobile platform would provide a user-friendly interface and seamless integration with various social media and communication apps, making it accessible to a broader audience. Furthermore, we explore potential expansion opportunities, such as cloud-based processing for scalability and the development of APIs that other developers can integrate into their own applications, thereby broadening the service's reach and impact. We demonstrate that our approach is simpler and more natural compared to traditional handcrafted tasks by applying it to diverse scenarios.

articleTitle: Exploration of New Models to Enhance Treadmill Usage and Analyze Optimal Use Cases for All Age Groups
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper explores innovative models to enhance treadmill usage and analyze optimal use cases across various age groups. By investigating novel approaches and technologies, we aim to identify strategies that promote increased treadmill engagement and address the diverse needs of users across different age demographics. Machine learning applications, which have been widely used in health and fitness, are employed in this study to classify data and predict which treadmills customers are likely to purchase. The purpose of our research is to derive insights into customer behavior and predict treadmill purchases based on specific features. We explore demographics and customer behavior to uncover key factors that provide valuable insights and actionable predictions. Four machine learning models-Random Forest Classifier, Bagging Classifier, AdaBoost Classifier, and Gradient Boosting Classifier-were evaluated to determine the best-performing model for classification. Three sets of experiments were conducted: one without SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique), one with SMOTE, and one after hyperparameter tuning. Results indicate that SMOTE and hyperparameter tuning significantly improved the accuracy of our models, with an accuracy of over 80% across three of the four models after implementing SMOTE and hyperparameter tuning. The Random Forest Classifier achieved the highest accuracy at 86.7%. The study concludes that machine learning applications hold significant potential in predicting customer behavior.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition Scheme Based on Time-Series Analysis of Multi-Antenna AoA Data
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative indoor activity recognition system leveraging multi-antenna Bluetooth Angle of Arrival (AoA) data to address limitations in existing wearable, non-wearable, and signal-based recognition methods. Conventional systems often suffer from usability issues, limited location flexibility, or inadequate activity coverage. At the same time, signal-based methods such as WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) typically struggle with model adaptability across environments. Building on our previous single-antenna AoA approach, which captured azimuth and elevation angles but encountered difficulties in accurately detecting vertical movements and certain activities, this study proposes a dual-antenna solution for improved multidimensional sensing. Our system employs two AoA antenna arrays to obtain synchronized, multi-angle measurements, significantly enhancing detection accuracy with minimal added hardware. Machine learning models classify four key activities-“Falling,” “Walking,” “Lying,” and “Standing” -based on time series and statistical features, including the mean and variance from each antenna array. The system achieved a high classification accuracy of 98.3% using Ran-dom Forest models. Cross-environment testing further confirmed the model's robustness and generalizability, establishing this approach as a scalable, high-accuracy solution for real-time, location-independent activity recognition.

articleTitle: Low-Energy Zigbee Fire Detection Node: Design and Power Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Fire presents a serious risk to life and can be triggered by various factors across different environments. In some areas, the absence of fire detection systems is often due to the high initial investment costs, particularly when the need for such systems is temporary. To tackle this issue, we propose a portable fire detection system as an innovative solution. This system features sensors that monitor for fire outbreaks and alert authorities. A key challenge to its adoption is the limitation on power consumption. To mitigate this, we have developed a custom microcontroller board designed for a low-power, battery-operated portable fire detection system, which has been field-tested. A thorough power analysis of the system has been conducted, revealing a sensor battery life of 62 days. This paper details the design features and presents the findings of the power analysis performed.

articleTitle: A Study on Optimizing Field Validation Using Machine Learning of the Modem System in LTE and 5G Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In order to effectively verify the modem system with limited resources and time, it is very important to select the optimal validation location by considering various environmental variables caused in field environment of the cellular network. However, it is very difficult to consider the infinite conditions of a broad field in the human analysis. This study proposes a machine learning method designed to optimize cellular modem validation locations. The method involves training on a variety of field environments, predicting the standardized variables for each location, and subsequently comparing these similarities. Finally, the correlation coefficient by training dataset from 190 locations around the world that are being used to field verification suggested that the 32.6% locations had strong correlations and which could be optimized.

articleTitle: Optimizing Layout Transformation in Deep Neural Networks Through Data Reuse in a Vector Processor
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are widely used in various applications of consumer devices, including smartphones, which now incorporate dedicated hardware like neural processing units (NPUs) for DNN processing. Several frameworks have been developed to efficiently process DNNs on these devices. In these frameworks, DNNs are represented as computational graphs, with each node corresponding to an operation and edges indicating data dependencies. When consecutive nodes in the DNN graph have mismatched data layouts, a layout transformation is required to reorder the data for compatibility. As layout transformation is handled by a programmable vector processor in NPUs, this paper proposes a method to represent arbitrary data movements during layout transformations using a vector processor. We simplify the layout transformation of N-dimensional tensors by breaking it down into a series of one-dimensional data movements using shift vectors, which represent horizontal movements within a data array. In addition, we propose a shift vector tree, a tree structure that leverages data reuse opportunities between shift vectors to minimize data movement costs. Experiments demonstrate the reusing data between shift vectors reduces layout transformation cycles by 15% in ResNet-18 and 20% in EfficientNet-b0. Furthermore, when combined with software pipelining, it achieves an end-to-end latency speedup of 1.25 × and 1.13 ×, respectively.

articleTitle: P4-Based Buffer Management Method for Throughput Fairness Improvement with Different Congestion Control Contention
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In TCP/IP, there are various types of congestion control algorithms, such as CUBIC and Bottleneck Bandwidth and Round-trip propagation time (BBR). When flows using CUBIC and BBR share a bottleneck link, it has been reported that fairness decreases with the buffer size of the relay node on the bottleneck link. To improve fairness in these circumstances, we have previously proposed a method assigning each congestion control algorithm a separate buffer at the relay node using a programmable data plane. We have also proposed a packet scheduling method, Fair Queuing with Holding Time (FQ-HT), that allows relay nodes to send packets fairly from multiple buffers by setting an appropriate holding time. The appropriate holding time depends on the bandwidth of the bottleneck link and the buffer size of the relay node. However, if the holding time is not set appropriately, the fairness may not be improved or the total throughput may be reduced. In this paper, we propose Fair Queuing with Variable Holding Time (FQ-VHT), which automatically sets the appropriate holding time based on the difference in the number of send packets between the buffers. Emulation experiments showed that FQ-VHT can set an appropriate holding time based on network conditions.

articleTitle: Real-Time IoT Device Identification Using Traffic Pattern Mapping Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of smart homes, automatic identification of IoT devices and their behavior is becoming increasingly important for maintaining safe, secure, and comfortable smart home environments. To grasp and understand IoT devices and their behavior, various IoT device identification methods based on traffic analysis with machine learning have been proposed and realized to automatically classify IoT devices with high accuracy. We also proposed an IoT traffic analysis and device identification method based on two-stage clustering previously. However, it has not considered real-time processes in actual environments. This paper proposes a real-time IoT device identification method using a traffic pattern mapping model for smart home environments. By using the analytical results as the mapping model to assign IoT traffic patterns, which can be obtained by traffic analysis with the clustering method, we can successfully reduce the computational cost required for pattern assignment and adapt our previous method to real-time IoT device identification.

articleTitle: 3-D ESPRIT Channel Estimation Performance Analysis of IRS-Assisted Massive MIMO IoT Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This article presents a novel 3D-ESPRIT algorithm designed to estimate channel information and detect symbols in Internet of Things (IoT) systems aided by Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS). Traditional methods for symbol detection and channel estimation face challenges in complex IoT environments. The 3D-ESPRIT algorithm addresses these by utilizing an IRS model that accurately estimates channels and mitigates issues like multipath propagation and interference. Through simulations, the algorithm shows superior performance in both channel estimation and symbol detection under various conditions, including noisy environments. Its robustness, efficiency, and noise immunity make it a valuable solution for future IoT applications.

Author Keywords: 3D-Estimation of Signal Parameters via Rotational Invariance Techniques (3D-ESPRIT)

articleTitle: Development of High-Quality Saccade-Based Line Display Considering Perceptual Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A large size saccade-based line display observed at more than 15m with high-quality images considering perceptual sensitivity has been developed. To achieve high-quality performance, the flashing of 128-chip LEDs driven by high-speed LED driver ICs was controlled by PIC microcontrollers using direct memory access and SPI communication.

articleTitle: Solving Task-Select Problems Using a Quantum Annealer
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: To tackle environmental and social challenges, we face numerous tasks that need to be solved. However, due to limited time and resources, it is unrealistic to solve all tasks. Therefore, prioritizing tasks to ensure efficient handling and meeting criteria is essential. When the number of tasks is large, prioritizing the optimal combination of tasks on classical computers becomes highly time-consuming. We define this pri-oritization as a combinatorial optimization problem, termed the task-select problem, and address it using a quantum annealer. A quantum annealer is specialized hardware designed to efficiently solve combinatorial optimization problems by transforming them into Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problems. In this paper, we propose a QUBO formulation for the task-select problem. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our approach enables solving the task-select problem with up to 100 items using a real quantum annealer.

articleTitle: Extending Whisper for Korean-English Code-switching Speech Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Among various automatic speech recognition (ASR) models, Whisper is a state-of-the-art model that demonstrates robust performance across various multilingual tasks. However, Whisper shows poor performance in code-switching speech where multiple languages are used within a single sentence. To address this limitation, we propose an extended version of Whisper that utilizes a language detector model with a modified token sequence format. Unlike the original Whisper's token sequence, multiple language tokens can be assigned to one sentence using information from the language detector, which enables Whisper to effectively process code-switching speech. Our experiments on a one-hour Korean-English code-switching speech dataset showed a 1.7% reduction in the character error rate (CER) and a 0.9% reduction in the space-normalized word error rate (sWER) with only a 1.12 × higher relative time complexity compared to the original Whisper.

articleTitle: Flexible NTT/iNTT Accelerator Based on Montgomery Reduction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As the importance of data grows, so does the significance of homomorphic encryption(HE), which enables direct computations on encrypted data. However, HE presents a major challenge, with computational overhead increasing compared to plaintext operations. To address this, we developed a hardware accelerator for NTT and iNTT, which are commonly used in HE and contribute to this overhead. The accelerator implements modular arithmetic using Montgomery reduction, and pipelining is applied to improve throughput. Additionally, a mode-switching feature is introduced, allowing both NTT and iNTT operations to be performed on a single circuit. The accelerator is also designed to operate flexibly across various cryptographic strength parameters ( <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{N}$</tex> -values). The proposed accelerator achieved an average speedup of approximately 4.24 times compared to software, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing computation time in HE systems.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Estimation of Dynamic Travel Times between Points of Interest
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Due to the dynamic traffic conditions, effective estimation of travel times is crucial for the real-world travel planning service. Although APIs provide accurate travel information, the high response time poses a limitation. This paper proposes a machine learning-based method using XGBoost to predict dynamic travel times between Points of Interests (POIs). By utilizing features including latitude and longitude of locations, route direction, and departure time, the model achieves high prediction accuracy. We conducted hyper-parameter tuning using Optuna and evaluated the proposed method with POIs in Kyoto. The proposed method achieved a low RMSPE of < 6.90% and a quick response time of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 2.4\times 10^{-3} \mathrm{s}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Toward Assisting Blind Individuals in Exploring Unfamiliar Indoor Environments Using Multimodal LLM and Smartphone LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Blind individuals often face challenges accessing information about their surroundings when navigating unfamiliar indoor spaces. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence and smartphone-based sensing technology have opened up new possibilities for creating practical and cost-effective assistive solutions to enhance their environmental awareness and independence. In this paper, we investigate the integration of a cutting-edge large language model capable of processing multimodal inputs and outputs with smartphone-integrated LiDAR to assist blind travelers in scene understanding and obstacle avoidance in indoor spaces. We implement a smartphone application prototype that provides voice descriptions of user-captured photos and generates audio or vibrotactile feedback for nearby objects located in front of a smartphone camera. We present our initial findings from a preliminary study conducted with a blind expert in assistive technology, demonstrating our prototype's potential for enriching the indoor exploration experience of blind travelers. We also discuss opportunities and challenges regarding further improvements to our prototype.

articleTitle: A Light-Weight Muti-Path Vision Transformer for Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, a lightweight multi-path ViT network is proposed. To reduce computational complexity and model size, the cross-block (C-B) and cross-stage (C-S) structures are developed according to the split-and-merge strategy. In addition, Cross-shape Windows Self-Attention (CSW-SA) is also used in the first stage to decrease computational complexity. To evaluate the performance of the proposed ViT network, two image datasets, Bird-325 [1] and Brain Tumor MRI [2], were chosen for testing. As for computational complexity, FLOPs of iFormer-S and the proposed encoder are 5.9G and 1.67G, respectively. For model size, the parameters of iFormer and the proposed encoder have 18.97M and 5.22M, respectively. For image classification tasks, the accuracy, precision, recall of the proposed ViT network are at least more than 97.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> on the two datasets. The experimental results show that the proposed ViT method can not only perform good feature extraction but also outperform the existing methods in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, FLOPs, and model size.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Card Games with AR Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Regardless of the widespread use of digital games, non-digital games are still popular, because of their tactile and spatial interaction in real spaces. Recently, Augmented Reality (AR) has also been incorporated into these games. This study focuses on card games, and proposes an AR Card game that preserves the original interaction and provides digital information, consequently enhancing their entertainment value. This paper outlines the development of a game incorporating AR-based functionality into the card game “Old Maid.”

articleTitle: Proof of Authorization and Association With Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel blockchain consensus mechanism called Proof of Authorization and Association <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(PoA^{2})$</tex>, which integrates machine learning to enhance the selection of signers in blockchain transactions. By utilizing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) optimized with a custom HuberAdam optimizer, our approach dynamically selects signers based on predicted probabilities, improving the efficiency of the authorization process. Experimental results demonstrate a substantial reduction in average latency for the ML-enhanced mechanism compared to traditional non-ML approaches. Specifically, the average latency for 100 and 1000 blocks in the ML-enhanced scenario was 0.0016 and 0.0018 seconds, respectively, compared to 0.2462 and 0.2728 seconds without ML. Similarly, for signer configurations of 10, 50, and 100, the ML-based model achieved latencies of 0.0026, 0.0015, and 0.0046 seconds, respectively, while the non-ML approach exhibited much higher latencies of 0.0461, 0.2238, and 0.4766 seconds. These results underscore the efficiency and scalability of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$PoA^{2}$</tex> mechanism, showcasing its potential to enhance blockchain performance by ensuring faster transaction processing and more balanced load distribution. The study highlights the advantages of integrating machine learning in blockchain consensus mechanisms, paving the way for more robust, scalable, and high-performance decentralized systems.

articleTitle: Decentralized Knowledge Sharing Framework for Aquaponics-Based Food Production: Insights on Data Sharing and User Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Aquaponics-based food production (AFP) has been receiving increased attention among practitioners, but is still relatively unknown to the public and is not yet widely adopted in the European region. This paper explores the potential of distributed ledger technologies, the Internet of Things, and encryption methods for a secure and distributed storage of critical AFP information in the supply chain. The usage of a distributed ledger can enable a tamper-proof log of events across the supply chain, which increases trust and awareness among authorities, corporate partners, and end consumers. The findings of this study include a developed decentralized knowledge sharing framework with proposed user interface designs based on IOTA, ESP32 sensors, and an attribute-based encryption scheme to enable transparency and secure knowledge exchange among novice and prospective aquaponics farmers, thus facilitating the adoption of AFP practices in the local community. This paper presents the benefits and feasibility of the developed conceptual framework based on initial experimental results in a laboratory environment.

articleTitle: Proof of Learning Using Zero-Knowledge Proof
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Machine learning is an important technology that can be applied to various services, such as medical diagnosis and sales data analysis. However, the machine learning often involves personal information in the data used for training, and data encryption is essential to prove the learning process without losing data privacy. Garg et al. proposed a method using zero-knowledge proofs to verify whether data owned by the prover has been correctly utilized for the training on a machine learning model.
