They applied their method to federated learning, in which multiple users learn a model from their data. On the other hand, their method requires each prover to share data using Multi-Party Computation (MPC), which results in significant computational overhead for each user. Furthermore, their method does not provide a solution for the case where a malicious prover proves the data that he/she has not actually used for the training. We propose a method to prove the correctness of the procedure that one's own data was used for training without using MPC by sharing models instead of sharing the data. In our scheme, each prover's model can only be accessed by two users: the verifier and the next prover, thus reducing the computational effort required for model sharing. The data and the model used for training can be applied to zero-knowledge proofs, and the verifier can verify only the model to prove that it has been trained without disclosing the data. We prove how we can identify the malicious prover when he/she sends different models to the verification phase.

articleTitle: Investigation of Prioritized Channel Access Control to Improve Frame Collisions for TCP Flows in Wireless LANs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Currently, the number of wireless stations (STAs) connected to wireless LANs (WLANs) is increasing, and environments where multiple WLANs are densely deployed are becoming more common. Also in such environments, it is necessary to prevent the degradation of channel utilization efficiency due to frame collisions. Most data flows transferred over information networks use Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) that requires acknowledgments (ACKs) to be returned from receiver hosts to sender ones. Hence in WLANs, frequent transmission of MAC frames containing TCP ACKs from STAs receiving TCP flows increases frame collisions. This paper investigates prioritized channel access control based on IEEE 802.11e Enhanced Distributed Channel Access (EDCA) to improve channel utilization efficiency by returning TCP ACKs rapidly and reducing collisions with such TCP ACKs. The effectiveness of the proposed control is evaluated in terms of the prioritization degree of frames containing TCP ACKs from STAs over other frames.

articleTitle: Automated Evaluation of Digital TV Middleware: Using Fuzzing and Pairwise for Test Generation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Testing is paramount in evaluating digital TV (DTV) software quality while developing digital television (DTV) receivers. It is about executing tests and looking for the most effective and efficient approaches, i.e., the ones that present high coverages in short running times. However, in addition to the system software modules usually present in DTV environments' there is also the middleware element, which surely involves application programming interfaces and specific execution environments, leading to a thorough conformance evaluation. Moreover, as a complex entity, DTV middleware may require broader verification, even with scenarios going beyond what is exposed in standards. The present work addresses these aspects and introduces an automated test generation methodology using fuzzing and pairwise testing tailored for the middleware DTV Play used in the Brazilian DTV system. It speeds up testing processes, enabling quicker cycles and more thorough evaluation steps.

articleTitle: ARIS: An Artificial-Intelligence-Based Automatic Recognition and Inventory System for Surgical Instruments in Operating Rooms
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes an Automatic Recognition and Inventory System, named ARIS, which utilizes YOLOv7 as a surgical instrument recognition Artificial Intelligence (AI) model and a management information platform to promptly identify surgical instruments placed on the tray and automatically inventory the types and quantities of surgical instruments. Experimental results demonstrate that ARIS can accurately identify various types of surgical instruments, thus effectively reducing nursing manpower and enhancing surgical safety.

articleTitle: Evasion Attacks on Tree-Based Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Various machine learning algorithms exist, each maintaining different assumptions about the underlying data or the function they aim to approximate. One such class of algorithms include tree-based models, which develop decision graphs that determine model behavior. In this research, we focus on developing two attacks that target tree-based models: one attack targets single tree-based models and the other targets ensemble tree-based models. We evaluate the two proposed attack algorithms on the popular MNIST handwritten digits dataset. Evading samples generated from the testing session are analyzed through the generated perturbation from each sample. We find that the evasion attacks are largely successful in the main objectives of evading: forcing incorrect model output and maintaining the stealthiness of the attack. Additionally, we find that the proposed attack algorithms perform well in the more stricter attack setting of targeted evasion.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Algorithm for Automatically Capturing the Desired Moment in Photography
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Digital photography has become ubiquitous in daily life, driven by the widespread use of smartphones. However, capturing the desired moment remains a challenge, particularly in scenarios involving rapid or fleeting motion. To address this, the previous approach introduced a method that enables cameras to autonomously plan and capture optimal moments with minimal user interaction [3]. The approach utilizes voice or text input to describe the user's intended photographic outcome, continuously evaluating the similarity between the provided description and the live preview image in a shared vector space. The preview image with the highest similarity score is automatically selected and captured as the optimal shot. Despite the effectiveness of this method, accuracy may be affected by various distracting factors in the scene. In this paper, we propose an enhanced algorithm that significantly improves accuracy by incorporating a dynamic sliding window to compare a continuous sequence of frames against the textual description, rather than individual frames. Experimental results demonstrate that the enhanced approach provides more robust accuracy, particularly in challenging scenes with various distractions.

articleTitle: GloFANet: Global Feature Augmented Networks for Data-Efficient Soccer Field Keypoint Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Keypoint detection in soccer broadcasts is crucial for tasks such as player positioning and goal event detection. Traditional algorithms like SIFT, which ensure scale and rotation invariance, and the Hough Line Transform, effective for straight line detection, lack adaptability to perspective changes and occlusion. While deep learning models adapt better, they still lose pixel-level details needed for precise keypoint localization in complex scenes like soccer fields and sports courts. To address these issues, the High-Resolution Network has been introduced to preserve pixel-level details through multi-scale feature fusion, but it still faces significant challenges under limited data conditions. To overcome these problems, we propose a novel method, the Global Feature Augmented Network (GloFANet), which combines global and local features to guide the model in capturing critical features and improving the discriminability of hard samples. GloFANet is trained using 25,148 images from SoccerNet, along with our own annotated data, totaling 542,690 data points. Experimental results show that GloFANet achieves a mean Average Precision of 85.86% across seven types of keypoints, surpassing the 2023 SoccerNet champion by 5.96%. Notably, in detecting the center line using only 2,137 samples, our method improves performance by 20.48% over the baseline. GloFANet maintains accuracy even with limited data, demonstrating strong data efficiency.

articleTitle: Implementation of Opportunistic Federated Learning System for Heterogeneous Resource Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: High-performance mobile devices equipped with various sensors capable of executing machine learning tasks have recently become widely available. Generally, sensing data is aggregated on a central server to train machine learning models. However, this approach consumes network and computational resources due to data aggregation and model training, while also raising privacy concerns related to data sharing. Alternatively, group construction methods for distributed machines, leveraging based on the location information, have been proposed to enable collaborative learning among mobile devices. However, tasks expected to run on mobile devices are diverse, and it is necessary to consider environments where various tasks coexist. Moreover, in real-world environments, devices vary in computational per-formance, communication performance, and the data they store, making it essential to address the impact of these factors on task execution. In this paper, we propose an opportunistic federated learning system that adaptively assigns groups for executing federated learning tasks based on the status of devices. We implement the proposed system and evaluate its performance, along with its cooperative device candidate selection algorithms.

articleTitle: Region-Based Contrast Enhancement for Infrared Thermal Imaging Systems: Parameter-Wise Performance Evaluation and Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In the automotive industry, thermal imaging systems are increasingly explored for night vision applications. Building on our previous study, which introduced a region-based contrast enhancement algorithm designed to deliver consistent performance across varying driving environments, this paper focuses on a detailed performance analysis based on different parameters. Specifically, we investigate the algorithm's effectiveness using four operation bits (8, 10, 12, and 14) and four divided region (DR) parameters (4, 8, 16, and 32). Our experimental results demonstrate that the algorithm meets real-time processing requirements and performs optimally with an 8-bit operation and a DR parameter of 16. These findings indicate that this configuration provides the best balance between performance and real-time processing capabilities. Based on these results, we aim to offer users the most effective performance solutions for future night vision applications utilizing thermal imaging systems.

articleTitle: A Malware Detection and Classification System Based on Lightweight CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, the rapid growth of malware has attracted widespread attention in the academic community, prompting researchers to train more powerful models and improve accuracy by integrating various machine learning methods. However, the convolutional neural network (CNN) based malware detection model faces severe challenges during the training process. It not only requires efficient hardware equipment, but also requires a long training time and the size of the generated model. It is also large and difficult to apply to devices with limited computing resources. In response to this problem, this study proposes a method that aims to reduce the size of the CNN model while maintaining a high accuracy rate, thus reducing the training time cost and the required storage space. This method first tests the combination of convolution kernel size (Kernel Size) and convolution kernel number (Filter Number) by establishing a two-layer convolution base layer to find the combination with better performance, and builds a model architecture based on it. Batch normalization and dropout regularization are also added to make the model more stable and generalizable. Second, the hyperparameters of the model are adjusted to find the hyperparameter combination that can make the model proposed in this study perform best. Finally, the data enhancement method is used to generate three different data sets for testing. Finally, the lightweight CNN model proposed in this study achieved an accuracy of 98.86%.

articleTitle: The More Halving Advances, the More Rational Double Spending Attack is
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Several blockchains, such as Bitcoin, feature an event known as a “halving,” where the reward obtained by miners for mining a block is halved at regular intervals. As halving progresses, the reward for newly issued cryptocurrency per block will decrease, potentially making double-spending attacks more profitable than mining honestly. A double spending attack involves an attacker creating a longer chain to overwrite a transaction that has been included in the main chain, thereby reusing the transaction. This attack was introduced in the Bitcoin paper by Satoshi Nakamoto, the originator of the blockchain concept. However, there has not been sufficient quantitative analysis of double-spending attacks following a halving. This study employs a simulator to calculate the profits from double spending attacks under various parameters in the context of halving. The results show that, 20 years from now, conducting a double spending attack could be more profitable than regular Bitcoin mining if the attacker controls more than 10% of the hash rate. This poses a significant challenge to the foundation of Bitcoin. Furthermore, this research analyzes the causes of this situation and reveals that the resale value ratio of the goods purchased with the transactions used in the double spending attack has a significant impact on the economic rationality of the attacks.

articleTitle: Exploring the Implementation of Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems in the Logistics Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems (ASRS) significantly enhance the efficiency of warehousing storage management within the logistics industry, thereby increasing operational profitability. By utilizing ASRS, logistics operators can minimize operational error and improve the overall efficiency of warehouse operations. This advancement improves warehousing storage management and reduces labor and operational costs. This study investigates logistics operators' satisfaction with ASRS using the Task-Technology Fit (TTF) model, offering valuable insights for discussion and implementation in logistics.

articleTitle: Real-Time Recursive Point Cloud Prediction for Interpolating Anomalous Frames
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Physical attacks that target light detection and ranging (LiDAR) sensors have become a significant threat to the security and reliability of LiDAR-based systems, particularly in autonomous driving and digital twin applications. These attacks selectively manipulate or remove point cloud data, thereby undermining the functionality of safety-critical systems. In this study, we propose a recursive point cloud prediction mechanism that anticipates future frames based on past data, enabling real-time interpolation of anomalous frames. The proposed mechanism predicts five future frames based on the preceding five frames and replaces compromised frames with interpolated predictions, thereby ensuring data continuity. Furthermore, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach using a major dataset, showing that it can maintain data integrity even during physical attacks.

articleTitle: An Integrated Data Analytic Platform for Internet of Things Products
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The use of big data for business solutions has become a standard practice in many companies. We have developed an integrated data analytic platform which collects, integrate, and accumulate a large amount of operating data from a wide variety of electrical products on a cloud-based system. We are aiming to gain insights for development of new functions, create new services, and improve the efficiency of maintenance work by analyzing the data. Many papers have been published which discuss requirements, functions, or configuration models to manage Internet of Things (IoT) data on clouds. This paper focuses on the utilization of the data analytic platform in actual business. The target data are operating data of various electrical products shipped to the market. Users of the system include people who are not experts in data analysis, such as product developers, solution developers, and quality control department personnel. The system is required to provide an environment which can deal with a variety of data in a unified format for users with different duties. In this paper, we introduce the architecture of the integrated data analytic platform, utilization of the data, effects of the introduction of the system, and feedback from the users.

articleTitle: Anomalous Sound Analysis Technology for Factories That Reduces Network Load
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: When anomalous sounds occur from machinery, it is almost always necessary to take measures such as stopping the factory line, which often results in significant losses. For this reason, anomalous sounds analysis is important in factories. In recent years, anomalous sound analysis using machine learning has been proposed. When using supervised learning, it is said that it is possible to make nearly 100% accurate judgments. There are many machines in a factory, and it is normal for there to be multiple factories. This means that a large amount of data needs to be collected and learning needs to continue. Collecting a large amount of voice data increases the network load. This paper describes the results of an investigation into compression methods for compressing and transmitting voice data. The conditions for compression are that machine learning can be performed using compressed data and that anomalous sounds can be identified by using machine learning.

articleTitle: An Implementation of Naming Rule Checking Function and its Applications to Java Programming Codes
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Currently, a lot of universities are offering Java programming courses for teaching the first-step object-oriented programming language. For novice students, to master writing readable codes using proper names for variables, classes, and methods is crucial in Java programming, to improve under-standability and maintainability. In this paper, we consider four naming rules to write a readable code and implement the naming rule checking function to check whether the given code follows them. For evaluations, we applied the proposal to 2, 908 source codes submitted in Java programming courses from students in Okayama University, Japan, Malang State Polytechnic, Indonesia, and Yamaguchi University, Japan. The results confirm the effectiveness of the proposal.

articleTitle: Fast-Neutron Soft-Error Tolerance of a Radiation-Hardened Repairable Field Programmable Gate Array
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Radiation-hardened very large scale integrations (VLSIs) are required for nuclear power plants, particularly for decommissioning operations. Nevertheless, the totalionizing-dose tolerance of current radiation-hardened VLSIs remains insufficient. Even if a space-grade VLSI were used, the totalionizing-dose tolerance would be only 1–20 kGy, implying their life-time as about 1–20 hr under the intense radiation of 1000 Sv/h around the melted nuclear fuel of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant. This paper presents a new radiation-hardened field programmable gate array (RHFPGA) incorpo-rating a triple-modular redundant configuration function. The RHFPGA sustained a 7.3 MGy total ionizing dose: 365-7,300 times higher than those of existing space-grade VLSIs. How-ever, during decommissioning operations, recriticality presents an important concern. This paper explains evaluation of the soft-error tolerance of RHFPGAs against a 15.0 MeV high-energy neutron beam. No soft error occurred on RHFPGAs.

articleTitle: An Improved 3D Systolic Architecture Design Using A Combination of Sub-Array Partitioning and Hierarchical Stacking Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Systolic arrays have been widely utilized to ac-celerate neural network training, particularly in convolutional neural networks (CNNs), where convolution operations are well-suited for acceleration using systolic arrays. This study demon-strates that mapping systolic arrays onto three-dimensional circuit structures, as opposed to traditional two-dimensional structures, achieves high throughput through large-scale parallel computation, effectively accelerating common convolutional layer operations. Conventional large-scale systolic arrays often suffer from long computation cycles; thus, this paper adopted two acceleration methods to significantly reduce computation time: sub-array partitioning acceleration and hierarchical stacking acceleration. In this work, we implemented systolic sub-arrays in a 3D scheme through Through-Silicon Vias (TSVs) and presented a 2.5D floorplan using EDA layout tools. By leveraging the three-dimensional structure, we achieved a significant reduction in inference latency for matrix operations by utilizing a three-dimensional structure. Compared to standard implementations, this design improved computational efficiency by factors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.577 \times$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16\times 16$</tex> matrices and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$11.43\times$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$256\times 256$</tex> matrices, resulting in superior performance and throughput. This innovative approach highlights the substantial potential of 3D systolic arrays in accelerating systems that rely on rapid matrix multiplication, including AI inference and cryptographic algorithms.

articleTitle: Development of a Radiation-Hardened JTAG Interface for Optically Reconfigurable Gate Arrays
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A radiation-hardened optically reconfigurable gate array that is a type of field programmable gate arrays and has over 1Grad total-ionizing-dose tolerance has been developed. Since the optically reconfigurable gate array allows its transistors to be broken by radiation, the total-ionizing-dose tolerance could drastically be increased. However, while the optically reconfigurable gate array works under a radiation environment, since a lot of transistors on the radiation-hardened optically reconfigurable gate array are broken by radiation, a test function must be implemented to find out any defect region. In a sense, Joint Test Action Group (JTAG) interface is very useful for optically reconfigurable gate arrays. However, current JTAG interfaces are highly vulnerable to strong radiation such as the decommissioning task of nuclear power plants. The weakness of JTAG interfaces is caused by serial transfer architecture. Therefore, in order to improve the radiation-tolerance of JTAG interfaces, we have developed a triple-modular redundant JTAG interface. This paper presents the triple-modular redundant JTAG interface design and the experimental results that the triple-modular redundant JTAG interface was implemented onto a DE1-SOC FPGA board and was used for monitoring a radiation-hardened optically reconfigurable gate array.

articleTitle: Cognitive Radio Sensor Networks for Visually Impaired Individuals for smart healthcare applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Individuals with visual impairments encounter significant difficulties in navigating and interacting with their surroundings. Cognitive radio sensor networks (CRSNs) have become a highly promising approach for assisting these individuals by providing real-time environmental data. Using recent developments in machine learning and wireless communications, this study introduces an AI-based approach to CRSNs for visually impaired individuals. A network of cognitive radio sensors is employed in the proposed system to gather and process surroundings data. This data is subsequently analyzed using artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms to provide useful information to the visually impaired user. The work presents an analysis of the system design along with it's features, and assessment of the proposed solution. The results highlight the significant improvement in the quality of life for visually impaired individuals.

articleTitle: Entanglement-Reusable Dynamic Routing for Quantum Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As a novel form of network structure, quantum networks can be considered nodes equipped with limited quantum memory units connected via lossy optical links. To fully unleash the potentials of quantum networks in applications such as distributed quantum computing, quantum key distribution, etc., an efficient quantum routing mechanism is vital for discovering multiple path solutions that deliver overall higher communication opportunities. Existing quantum routing algorithms focus on the “contention-free” strategy, which may result in restricted throughput gains. In this paper, we propose a novel metric called reusable factor to evaluate the probability that the reserved quantum resources for a candidate path can still offer available channels for other potential available paths even after path assignments. Further, a new Entanglement-Reusable Dynamic Routing Algorithm (ERDRA) is proposed to enable the multiple assignment of quantum entanglement. Simulation results demonstrate that Erdra achieves solid performance gains over state-of-the-art algorithms under various network settings.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence-Based Polyp Detection And Measurement Add-On System For Endoscopy
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The intelligent medical assistive system has emerged as a topic of considerable interest within the research community in recent years. The implementation of such a system has the potential to significantly reduce the workload of medical personnel while simultaneously enhancing the quality of medical treatment. The automated detection of endoscopic images through computer vision technology represents a significant aspect of the development of intelligent medical assistive systems. In this study, we propose the integration of artificial intelligence-based automated detection and measurement technology into a medical assistive system. The system is capable of detecting polyps in endoscopic images and measuring their sizes simultaneously, as well as calculating the distance to any region of interest in endoscopic images. The detection and measurement performance of the proposed system has been evaluated using self-collected real-world endoscopy images. To demonstrate the clinical unmet need that the proposed system addresses, it was deployed to an edge computing device and integrated with actual endoscopic equipment, which confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Partial Super Resolution Using Cross Attention
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We propose the task of partial super-resolution and introduce two methods for the task, PartialHAT and Partial- DRCT. Partial super-resolution is the task of enhancing the resolution of a specific region of an image. For this task, we incorporated cross attention and a novel loss function into the existing super-resolution models, HAT and DRCT. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms the original methods, HAT and DRCT, in terms of PSNR. Additionally, we conducted experiments by altering the hyperparameter values of the loss function. Our source code is available at https://github.com/msdsm/partial-super-resolution.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Shooting Method for Biometric Authentication in External Auditory Canal
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: With the advancement of information technology, biometric authentication is being used in a variety of situations. It is known that images from external auditory canal contain features that can be used to identify individuals, but because experiments were conducted using ideal images, the robustness of this in real environments was unknown. In recent years, image processing has been applied to the image data obtained, assuming a real usage environment, and the impact of this on recognition accuracy has been evaluated. It has been confirmed that recognition accuracy decreases as the light source becomes stronger due to its influence. In this study, a jig was created that can capture images of external auditory canal using an LED light source, and captured images of the left and right external auditory canal for the same person over several days, and used images obtained from the actual video data to confirm the impact on overall recognition accuracy. We obtained results equivalent to those of robustness evaluations that applied image processing.

articleTitle: YOLOv8-WS: Improved YOLOv8n for Traffic Sign Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Deep learning huge data for traffic sign detection is a highly attractive approach for autonomous driving. You only look once (YOLO) family of deep learning networks is an appealing candidate for high-precision object classification. In this paper, we improve the YOLOv8n model by incorporating the shuffle attention (SA) mechanism into the YOLOv8n model's ‘head’ architecture and the spatial pyramid pooling full connection spatial pyramid convolution (SPPFCSPC) technique into the YOLOv8n model's ‘backbone’ architecture. We call this new model as YOLOv8-WS. We use the image synthesis method by Torres et al. to automatically annotate dataset of Taiwan traffic signs. Experimental results show that, under the same 70 epochs, YOLOv8-WS achieves a precision of 0.983, which is equivalent to a 0.004 improvement over that of the YOLOv8n model. The improvements for recall rate and mAP50 are 0.008 and 0.001, respectively.

articleTitle: Visualization of Flow Fields Around Drones Using Intermittent Smoke
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study presents a method for visualizing the flow fields around multiple drones intended for gas leak detection in disaster areas, using intermittently generated smoke and image processing. As a preliminary step before conducting experiments with multiple drones, we focused on enhancing visualization performance. An experimental setup was constructed to conduct visualization experiments indoors. This setup is installed in a dark room, where a smoke generator is connected to a duct to create the flow path. Smoke is generated intermittently from the smoke device, and the cross-section of the flow path is extracted using a sheet laser. A transparent panel separates the interior and exterior of the duct, allowing for external image capture with a camera. Optical flow image processing is applied to the captured images, achieving visualization of the entire flow path.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of Data Cleaning for Improving Road Damage Detection Through Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The WHO predicts that by 2030 road accidents will be the 5th leading cause of death. Globally, road accidents account for 1.25 million casualties each year, and road defects cause 34% of these casualties. The road survey process in many countries have several challenges, one of which is detection using cameras that do not have a recognition system. In this study, a model with YOLOS architecture based on Vision Transformer trained on the RDD2022 dataset successfully recognizes road damage well, as indicated by the number of objects detected, bounding box on accurate objects, and the ability to recognize objects with inconsistent shadow and light inference. This research uses assessment parameters such as Average Precision (AP) and Average Recall (AR) to determine the overall performance of the model. The model achieves the highest AP value at Intersection of Union (IoU) 0.5, 0.75, and 0.5-0.95, worth 62.1%, 37.1%, and 36.2% respectively, and the highest AR value in Large, Medium, and Small Areas, worth 42.1%, 60.3%, and 75.4% respectively. The supplementary material can be found through this link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LzkI2e_IORE.

articleTitle: Low Parameters UNet for Energy-Efficient Cloud Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Applying cloud detection algorithms to edge devices using semantic segmentation poses significant challenges due to the high computational complexity and power consumption. This paper proposes a parameter reduction method that combines linear channel pruning and adaptive pruning techniques to effectively compress the large UNet model. Linear channel pruning efficiently reduces model redundancy, while adaptive pruning further enhances the model's sparsity. This approach not only maintains performance comparable to the original UNet in terms of Intersection over Union (IoU) and other key metrics, but also significantly reduces the model's parameter count, thereby lowering DRAM access power consumption. Experimental results show that the first and second stages of parameter reduction decreased the model's parameter count by 98.5% and 70.3%, respectively, while reducing memory access by 67.5% and 65%, respectively.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Next Generation DTTB Using Asynchronous Time-Domain LDM
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: For the achievement of 4K and 8K terrestrial Ultra High Definition Television (UHDTV) broadcasting, research in the physical layer is being conducted all over the world to realize technology that achieves high transmission efficiency. Currently, the frequency band allocated to terrestrial broad-casting is strained, and there are no extra bandwidth avail-able to introduce next-generation Digital Terrestrial Television Broadcasting (DTTB, same meaning as Advanced ISDB- T). In Japan, Integrated Services Digital Broadcasting-Terrestrial (ISDB-T) is used for terrestrial broadcasting. To introduce the next-generation DTTB while broadcasting ISDB-T, the Layered Division Multiplexing (LDM) method has been proposed. LDM enables ISDB-T and Advanced ISDB-T to communicate in the same frequency band in Time-Domain or Frequency-Domain. In this study, we propose using Asynchronous Time-Domain LDM with a larger number of FFT size, which the size is only acces-sible in the Time-Domain. The result shows that communication accuracy against noise was improved over Frequency-Domain LDM (FLDM) or previous study of Time-Domain (TLDM). This enables next-generation DTTB using TLDM instead of FLDM to transmit signals with different FFT clocks and higher bit rates for 4K and 8K TV services. The results are simulated in the Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) channel.

articleTitle: Enhancing DDoS Attack Detection in SDN with a Stacked Model Framework Utilizing Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Software Defined Networking enhances network management and security through centralized control, vital for the growth of consumer electronics. With the rise of smart devices and IoT systems, the demand for scalable network management has intensified. While SDN streamlines network operations and supports essential technologies, it remains vulnerable to DDoS attacks that can disrupt these services. However, SDN environments are vulnerable to Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, posing significant risks to operational integrity. This paper analyzes the performance of various machine learning models at the individual level, providing insights into their effectiveness in detecting DDoS attacks. Based on these findings, a hybrid model is introduced, utilizing stacking techniques with a Deep Neural Network (DNN) as the meta-learner. The hybrid approach achieves a remarkable accuracy of 99.09%. The results underscore the crucial role of machine learning, particularly deep learning methodologies, in safeguarding SDN networks against cyber threats. As reliance on complex networked systems in consumer electronics increases, enhancing the security of SDN environments becomes essential for maintaining seamless operations.

articleTitle: A Landslide Remote Monitoring System Using Solar-Cell-Operated Low-Power Wireless Sensor Networks and Cloud Service
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this study, we propose practical technologies for achieving battery-less operation and maintenance-free solutions, such as eliminating the need for battery replacement, in a landslide remote monitoring system using wireless sensor networks. Additionally, we propose a low-cost system capable of remotely monitoring landslides by leveraging a commercial cloud service. This paper details the development and evaluation of the prototype we propose.

articleTitle: Innovative Hinge Design for Tablet PCs Based on User Needs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study explores the development and evaluation of an innovative hinge design for 360-degree rotating laptops (tablet PCs) tailored to business environments. Emphasizing user experience (UX) alongside traditional metrics of functionality and durability, this research underscores the pivotal role of UX in business-oriented devices. By conducting user observations and technical analyses, we identified hinge-related challenges and proposed a novel two-step torque hinge design. This design was implemented in a market-released product, enabling the collection of real-world user feedback. Results indicated notable improvements in user satisfaction, highlighting the significance of UX-focused design in business tablet PCs. This study demonstrates that prioritizing UX can drive innovation in mature product designs, resulting in significant improvements.

articleTitle: Briefing of Text-to-Speech Trends Toward Zero-Shot Multi-Speaker Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper reviews advancements in Text-to-Speech (TTS) systems and focuses on the evolution from single-speaker systems to Zero-Shot Multi-Speaker TTS (ZS-TTS) systems. Traditional single-speaker TTS models require retraining whenever a new speaker is introduced, which limits scalability. Multi-speaker models address this issue but rely on large amounts of data and computational resources. ZS-TTS is a recent innovation that synthesizes natural speech for unseen speakers using only a few seconds of reference audio and eliminates the need for additional fine-tuning. In this paper, we introduce important methods such as speaker embedding, GAN-based models, and transformers, explaining how these approaches improve efficiency and voice quality. It also examines the challenges of inference speed and model scalability, especially in edge computing environments, and suggests potential directions for future research in TTS.

articleTitle: Strength Assessment Procedure using Grid Strength Impedance Metric with PSCAD
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: With the growing integration of inverter-based renewable energy sources, modern power systems face increasing challenges in maintaining grid strength across a wide frequency spectrum. Traditional indices, such as the short circuit ratio (SCR), primarily assess grid strength at the fundamental frequency, which is inadequate for evaluating the impact of dynamic, power electronics-based devices such as inverters on grid stability. This limitation poses significant risks to the performance and reliability of consumer electronics, which depend on a stable and robust grid connection for seamless operation across various frequencies. This paper proposes a comprehensive procedure to assess grid robustness using the grid strength impedance metric (GSIM), which analyzes system stability across all frequency ranges, particularly in the context of consumer electronics integration. Through detailed PSCAD-based simulations of the Jeju Island power grid, we extract frequency-dependent impedances and evaluate grid strength both with and without the connection of Grid-Following (GFL) inverters. The results demonstrate that while grid strength is high at the fundamental frequency, potential instability arises at higher frequencies, especially when inverter output is at its peak. These findings underscore the importance of robust, frequency-wide analysis to ensure the reliable operation of consumer electronics in modern power systems.

articleTitle: Convolutional Inception v4 for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis Using Multi-Plane MRI Data
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Deep learning approaches have demonstrated encouraging results in the classification of Alzheimer's disease (AD); yet high accuracy, fast processing speed, and cross-population generalizability are necessary for medical environments to be successful. In this work, we used cognitively normal controls that differ in age and gender, as well as structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) scans from AD patients to construct a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based method for the classification of Alzheimer's Disease. The experiment used slices of the sMRI images taken from ADNI of T1-weighted images that underwent the process of slicing the images and fed to the model in the Coronal, sagittal and axial plane to obtain the model accuracy and other parameters; plotted the confusion matrix. The obtained accuracy is 91%, and sensitivity and specificity as 94% and 89% respectively.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Rule Based Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Reinforcement learning is a crucial technology for implementing intelligent service scenarios by optimizing reward functions to learn similar action. However, reward functions designed by humans often lead to significant errors when imitating action. To address this issue, methods for reward estimation and behavior generation through inverse reinforcement learning have been explored. Nevertheless, Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning(GAIL) can suffer from decreased learning speed and performance in uncertain environments with limited information. We propose designing the Generator of GAIL based on fuzzy rules, aiming for faster and more efficient action generation. This approach focuses on improving the algorithm's learning speed and preventing performance degradation in uncertain environments. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing algorithms in terms of stability and performance.

articleTitle: Dynamic Lighting for Enhanced Sense of Depth in 2D Mid-air Image
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study aims to enhance the realism of two-dimensional (2D) mid-air images. While a 2D light source is often used to create these images owing to its affordability, high resolution, and ease of implementation, it presents challenges in eliciting a depth perception similar to that of 3D mid-air images. Aligning the lighting environments of real space with mid-air images enhances optical consistency, affecting the perception of presence and shape. Therefore, we introduced dynamic lighting in real space, achieving optical and temporal consistency, which enhances the sense of depth in 2D mid-air images. Additionally, a psychophysical experiment suggested that dynamic lighting increases depth perception, offering an enhanced sense of depth in 2D mid-air images compared to that of traditional static lighting.

articleTitle: Spatial Media Applications by Use of Aerial Display Based on Aerial Imaging by Retro-Reflection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Aerial display, which shows an information screen floating in mid-air, is a new field of electronic display technologies. Since the aerial display enables us to implement non-contact touch operations, social implementations of the aerial display have rapidly increased after the pandemic of COVID-19. This paper introduces the definition of the aerial display with its international standardization. Then, we show the principle of aerial imaging by retro-reflection (AIRR) and typical AIRR optical systems. Furthermore, we report applications of the aerial displays as spatial media, including aerial newspaper installed for the general public, opera, noh, and theaters.

articleTitle: A Sequential Perturbation Framework for Solving Laplacian Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the iterative solution of a sequence of graph Laplacian systems by leveraging the (relative) continuity of the generalized inverse operator. Our primary objective is to extend traditional matrix perturbation techniques specifically to the context of graph Laplacian systems. We achieve this by modeling the evolution of these systems starting from a given initial graph Laplacian and applying a series of systematic updates. We propose a novel framework that formulates an iterative method for solving the targeted graph Laplacian system based on the solutions of simpler, earlier Laplacian systems. By establishing a relationship between the solutions of two Laplacian systems, we derive a recursive formula that enables efficient computation of the updated solutions. This approach not only enhances computational efficiency but also maintains accuracy, as it utilizes the inherent structure of the graph Laplacian, including its positive semi-definiteness and the zero-mean condition of the right-hand side.

articleTitle: Novel Multi-Scan LiDAR System for Enhanced Shadow Removal
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In autonomous driving, sensor data is critical for ensuring safety in dynamic road environments. The conventional LiDAR systems face challenges when obstacles create shadow zones leading to incomplete mapping and potential detection failures. This paper presents a novel LiDAR system employing beam-splitting technology to minimize shadow regions in 3D mapping. Through multi-angle scanning, the proposed system effectively eliminates shadow regions, ensuring continuous detection in complex driving environments. Prototype testing demonstrates a reduction in shadow-induced detection errors achieving measurement accuracy within 3%. The research highlights the viability of this technology for safer autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Driver Drowsiness Detection System to Prevent Accidents Using Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Drowsiness is a critical factor contributing to numerous road accidents worldwide. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) conservatively estimates that 1,000,000 police-reported crashes are the direct results of driver fatigue each year. Implementing a drowsiness alarm or a drowsiness detection system can effectively mitigate these causes. Drowsiness detection systems continuously monitor the driver's state and trigger an alarm if signs of drowsiness are identified. The objective of this project is to design and implement a system for detecting driver drowsiness. It employs image processing to determine if the driver is experiencing fatigue or drowsiness. Through this image processing approach, we identify the driver's eyes and monitor how long they remain closed. If the eyes are shut for more than 3 seconds, the system includes a speaker that activates an alert. This alert serves to notify and awaken the driver, thus helping prevent accidents. Additionally, the system is connected to an electric motor, which plays the car engine role, and it reduces the motor speed if the driver does not promptly respond to the alarm.

articleTitle: Pose-Guided Person Image Synthesis with Hybrid Appearance Encoding
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Despite significant advancements in pose-guided image synthesis techniques using diffusion models, many results still appear unrealistic and unnatural due to insufficient semantic understanding of the input person images by the synthesis models. This paper introduces an enhanced deep neural network for pose-guided person image synthesis. The proposed network integrates both global and local information by employing Swin Transformers and a CNN-based Fourier convolution block during the encoding process of a person image. This approach generates more natural and refined images across various poses and appearances. Furthermore, we improve the appearance encoding process by utilizing VQ-VAE (Vector Quantized Variational AutoEncoder) to compress appearance information. Our method demonstrates outstanding results in preserving details and reducing overfitting. Additionally, the generated images can be effectively used as training data for applications such as object detection, object re-identification, and abnormal behavior analysis.

articleTitle: Enhancing AI Backend Network with Dynamic Load Balancing Using Open Source Network Operation System SONiC
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper evaluates dynamic load balancing (DLB) with the open-source network operating system SONiC to enhance AI backend networks. Our experiments demonstrate that DLB significantly improves network utilization, reducing link imbalance by as much as 26% in undersubscribed topologies and increasing bandwidth by up to 25% in all2all operations. By optimizing load distribution, DLB provides a critical advantage for AI-driven environments. The findings suggest that further exploration of DLB in diverse network configurations could maximize its benefits, contributing to a more efficient and reliable AI infrastructure.

articleTitle: Exploring Pedestrian Responses to eHMIs in Virtual Reality: Balancing Efficiency and Safety in Interactions with Automated Buses
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Automated buses, which have the potential to enhance public mobility, are being deployed globally. However, due to their non-human driving style and lack of traditional driver communication cues (e.g., eye contact and gestures), these vehicles can pose traffic hazards. This study aims to explore pedestrians' information needs regarding external human-machine interfaces (eHMI) when encountering automated buses in ambiguous situations, such as un-signalized intersections. In a virtual reality (VR) experiment, 32 participants navigated a residential area under four eHMI conditions: (1) no eHMI; (2) eHMI indicating the bus is autonomous; (3) eHMI displaying the bus's intent; and (4) eHMI displaying right of way. Participants' crossing behaviors and responses to questionnaires were collected to assess the impact of eHMI on pedestrian-bus interactions. Results showed that eHMI indicating either the bus's intent or priority reduced pedestrians' hesitation and increased their perceived safety. However, eHMI displaying the bus's intent also fostered pedestrian dependence on the interface, potentially leading to risky behaviors. These findings highlight the need for clear, effective eHMI designs and call for further research to fully assess their impact on pedestrian safety.

articleTitle: A Method of Detecting Port Bay Numbers and Optimizing Effects Under Various Weather Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Ports are transportation hubs located along coasts, rivers, lakes, and reservoirs, with water and land transport facilities that allow ships to enter, exit, and berth safely. The port bay numbers are located on the land side of the port and are rectangular frames of specific sizes designated by port management, containing unique codes. These codes identify where containers are stacked under various weather conditions. Therefore, the ability to quickly and accurately recognize bay numbers in all weather conditions has become a significant issue affecting work efficiency, especially in rainy ports. However, collecting images of bay numbers during rainy days is not permitted due to safety restrictions. In this article, we first generate images of rainy scenes based on images collected in sunny weather. We then compare two detection algorithms and select the one with a smaller decrease in detection metrics but fewer model parameters. Finally, we incorporate an attention mechanism into the chosen algorithm to optimize and enhance target detection performance across various weather scenarios.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Based Detection Mechanism for Deepfake Image
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The widespread availability of digital smart devices and the rapid growth of multimedia content on social media platforms have created an environment conducive to the manip-ulation of images and videos through advanced machine learning algorithms, notably in the form of deepfakes. These AI -generated multimedia deceptions pose a significant challenge to the verification and integrity of digital media, particularly as they are employed to spread disinformation across social channels. In our current “post-truth” era, deepfakes have emerged as powerful tools for distorting reality, capable of manipulating public opinion, defaming individuals, and even influencing critical events like elections. Deepfakes, categorized into various types such as face-swap, lip-synching, puppet-master, face synthesis and attribute manipulation, and audio deepfakes, present multifaceted threats. Face-swap deepfakes target public figures, distorting scenarios to damage reputations or create false narratives. Puppet-master techniques aim to replicate a person's expressions or entire body movements for deceptive purposes. Therefore, this is the need for an hour to find out about the originality and authenticity of the images. In this research paper, we used convolutional Neural Network and found 92.67% accuracy.

articleTitle: Multi-Object Tracking System Based on StrongV7 Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-object tracking system based on StrongV7 Neural Network. This research focuses on object detection and optimization of object frame generation for multiple target-tracking neural networks. The proposed StrongV7 network architecture that combines the advantages of YOLOv7 in object detection and the characteristics of StrongSORT in multiple target identical object tracking to make the generation of object frames more lightweight and efficient.

articleTitle: Implementation of Key Based Secure Centralized Database On The Cloud
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Implementation of the secure database management system requires to achieve confidentiality from the triad of CIA (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability). Confidentiality becomes more valuable when data is available on cloud. The main concern is forestalling cloud administrators, database administrators, and software developers to get plain data that resides in the database. Whereas encryption is the fundamental tool that may be used to ensure data confidentiality by picking the popular encryption methods such as AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256. In this study, we demonstrated our approach on Land Record Management Information System (LRMIS). After implementing the proposed methodology, technical persons are prohibited to get confidential data.

articleTitle: Smart Warehouse Safety: Computer Vision for Forklift Driver Monitoring in Warehouse Setting
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Safety for forklifts and warehouse workers must be prioritized. Our study introduces a computer vision-based solution for promptly recognizing unsafe behaviors in real time using deep learning and pose estimation. The primary goal is to identify unsafe actions of forklift drivers, enhance workplace safety, and help managers spot dangerous trends or patterns early on. The research will integrate Convolutional Neural Networks and Pose Estimation. Specifically, we will use the “You Only Look Once” architecture version 8 of the CNN model for object detection to identify forklift drivers. Subsequently, the YOLO version 8 pose will detect and estimate forklift driver body joints. Our findings indicate that this approach achieves a detection accuracy rate of over 91 percent and an f1 score of the pose estimation model exceeding 0.96. Importantly, the potential of our solution is not limited to forklift safety in warehouses. Future work will focus on adapting the model to different warehouse settings and other high-risk industries, demonstrating the versatility and wide-ranging applicability of our research.

articleTitle: Fall Risk Prediction in Older Adults via Deep Learning on Point Cloud Sequences
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In an aging society, the number of falls among older adults is increasing, and the number of older adults who fall, fracture bones, or require nursing care to prevent these injuries has become a social problem. Since falls are more likely to occur and lead to more serious injuries with aging, it is important to detect the increased risk of falls at an early stage and take countermeasures to reduce the number of falls. Therefore, it is desired to develop a monitoring system for older adults that includes fall risk estimation. In this paper, we focus on standing up and sitting down, which are activities of daily living, and propose a technique for predicting fall risks based on time-series data of 3D point clouds taken during these activities. We aimed to achieve a higher estimation accuracy than binary classification of fall risks by indirectly estimating the risk of falling by the regression of time taken to conduct the Timed Up and Go test (the TUG score). The score was estimated with a mean absolute error of 0.86.

articleTitle: Generation of Similar Sounds Using GPTs in a Sound Effects Synthesis System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Nowadays, the market size for services such as gaming and video streaming has been expanding, and along with this, the demand for essential sound effects in content production is also increasing. Additionally, audio generation AI, such as Diff-Sound, has emerged in response to this growing demand. However, these AI systems face challenges when tasked with generating content based on prompts that contain multiple events. In this study, we propose a method for improving the generation of sound effects by utilizing GPTs to preprocess prompts containing multiple events, based on a system used in previous research. This preprocessing technique involves using GPTs to decompose prompts with multiple events into simpler, single-event components. As a result, the generated sound effects are improved through this process.

articleTitle: Quantum Hybrid Support Vector Machines for Stress Detection in Older Adults
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Stress can increase the possibility of cognitive impairment and decrease the quality of life in older adults. Smart healthcare can deploy quantum machine learning to enable preventive and diagnostic support. This work introduces a unique technique to address stress detection as an anomaly detection problem that uses quantum hybrid support vector machines. With the help of a wearable smartwatch, we mapped baseline sensor reading as normal data and stressed sensor reading as anomaly data using cortisol concentration as the ground truth. We have used quantum computing techniques to explore the complex feature spaces with kernel-based preprocessing. We illustrate the usefulness of our method by doing experimental validation on 40 older adults with the help of the TSST protocol. Our findings highlight that using a limited number of features, quantum machine learning provides improved accuracy compared to classical methods. We also observed that the recall value using quantum machine learning is higher compared to the classical method. The higher recall value illustrates the potential of quantum machine learning in healthcare, as missing anomalies could result in delayed diagnostics or treatment.

articleTitle: On-Device Neural Architecture Search
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach to near-sensor computing, in which a lightweight Neural Architecture Search (NAS) is performed directly on the deployment device to find the best tiny neural architecture for analyzing the real-time data acquired through sensors. This new adaptation capability can be particularly useful in the case of human-machine interfaces for which the neural network analyzing the biometrical data can be re-designed each time the user changes, after a guided data collection procedure, fighting the typical data variations between individuals on a new level. To implement the proposed approach a new NAS has been designed and then validated on the Italian Sign Language dataset (ISL), a collection of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals of the signs of the Italian alphabet, using several embedded systems. Moreover, further validation on the Case Western Reserve University dataset (CWRU), a benchmark for intelligent fault diagnosis, is presented to suggest another possible application of the proposed approach. When run on a Raspberry Pi 4, the proposed NAS performs beyond the state of the art proposing a tiny neural architecture having 0.63 times less RAM occupancy and 5.96 percentage points of more accuracy in the case of the ISL dataset; and 0.44 times less RAM occupancy and 0.2 percentage points of more accuracy in the case of the CWRU dataset.

articleTitle: Secure and Reliable 6G Communications with BCH-Based GLDPC and Kyber
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Channel coding in sixth-generation (6G) networks must attain exceptionally low bit error rate (BER), typically in the range of 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> to 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>, to ensure the requisite level of reliability. While fifth-generation (5G) New Radio (NR) coding techniques have made substantial progress, the inherent limitations of the low error floor impede the attainment of such stringent BER targets. Compared to the low-density parity check (LDPC) codes employed in 5G communications, generalized low-density parity check (GLDPC) codes offer a more advantageous tradeoff between computational complexity and error correction performance in 6G networks. GLDPC codes enhance traditional LDPC structures by incorporating more complex local decoding units within their check nodes. When coupled with cryptographic techniques, GLDPC codes can establish a robust information security framework. In this paper, we propose a new security-based GLDPC that uses a number of BCH matrices for the GLDPC decoding process combined with the Kyber algorithm (BCH-based KyGLDPC) before transmitting data to increase reli-ability and solve the security problem against quantum computer attacks. The system's performance is assessed using both image data and data encrypted prior to transmission in a white additive Gaussian noise environment. The results indicate that the system provides strong error correction and data security.

articleTitle: A Study of Style Transfer Based on Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Style transfer, the blending of content from one image with the style of another, has advanced significantly through two primary approaches: neural network-based methods like Neural Style Transfer and recent text-to-image diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion. In particular, inversion-based methods like Textual Inversion, DreamBooth, and Custom Diffusion further enhance the process by embedding new styles from reference images. This paper evaluates the performance of these methods in style transfer using two datasets-paintings of “Edward Hopper” from the WikiArt dataset and the Peanuts Comic Strip dataset-and explores the impact of the number of reference style images used during training. Our study highlights the current capabilities and future potential of diffusion-based style transfer.

articleTitle: Lightweight Calculation of Region Estimation for Data Indication by Augmented Reality in Road Space
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for accelerating the calculation time of estimating regions where data can be safely indicated via augmented reality in road spaces. It is necessary to estimate whether the data can be indicated safely for each small region of road users' view image. Our method estimates the regions by extracting CNN-based features and performing classification via machine learning-based classifiers. Our method accelerates the calculation time by extracting features from the entire images instead of region by region. This study contributes to the data indication to road users via AR devices in the terminal computing environments.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of RL Based End-to-End Learning Technology for Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As autonomous driving technology is being researched as a core technology for the future automotive industry, there has been rapid advancement in related sensors, components, platforms, and artificial intelligence technologies. The core technology of autonomous driving, based on such hardware and platforms, lies in AI-driven software, with various studies being conducted in this field. In particular, key technologies for advancing autonomous driving include the mechanism of interaction among modules: the perception module that recognizes the ego vehicle's situation from multiple sensor inputs, the decision module that plans driving strategies based on the recognized situation, and the control module that operates physical components such as acceleration and steering based on the driving plan. This also includes the orchestration technology for feedback control in response to changing environments. This paper focuses on E2E (End-to-End Learning), an integrated control module encompassing perception, decision, and control modules, specifically investigating the performance of reinforcement learning in the control section. The research places particular emphasis on evaluating end-to-end learning performance using the CARLA online simulator (Car Learning to Act). It examines the neural network structure of TCP (Trajectory-guided Control Prediction) and trains and validates it under identical conditions. The results show an increase in performance when comparing a simple reinforcement learning model to the original: Driving Score improved by 4.81%, Route Completion by 1.91%, and Infraction Penalty remained at 0.0%.

articleTitle: Emergency Vehicle Siren Direction Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The siren identification of emergency rescue vehicles is important, but if it can also identify the direction, its application will be even wider. This paper proposes that three types of siren positions can be determined for emergency rescue vehicles: cars coming from the front, cars coming from behind, and ambient sounds. The proposed method is compared with the other four methods. The emergency vehicle siren in the paper is presented with the sound of an ambulance. In the test, experiments were performed with different sound intensities and different signal-to-noise ratios. The results presented in the experiments show that the proposed method CNN+BiLSTM has the highest accuracy.

articleTitle: Voltage-Boosting Rectenna with Enhanced Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A voltage boosting rectenna with high efficiency using circularly polarized microstrip patch antenna with reduced surface waves is proposed. A rectenna operating at 5.8 GHz has been designed using two zero bias Schottky diodes with high detection sensitivity for rectifying device as well as voltage booster. In order to minimize surface waves, two microstrip circular patch antennas with shorting pins are used.

articleTitle: Video Transfer Method Suitable for Object Detection in the Cloud
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a video transfer method which is suitable for object detection in the cloud. It reduces the effects of video codecs by applying an averaging filter before video coding. An evaluation using the VisDrone2019 dataset, the YOLOv3 inference model, and the H.264 video codec shows that the proposed method improves the mAP by up to 7.2 % compared to the conventional method. Additionally, it can reduce the bitrates by approximately 20 % in some sequences while maintaining the detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Implementation of Smart Garbage Detection System Using Camera-Based Low-Power Edge AI Device
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In Japan, garbage collection sites are shared by multiple households, and garbage disposal rules are set by local governments. When garbage is disposed of outside the specified times or after collection, it remains at the site for extended periods, causing issues like bad odors and landscape deterioration. This paper implements a garbage detection system using a low-power edge AI device equipped with a camera. Verification experiments with a prototype system confirmed that MobileNetV2, a machine learning method, achieves higher detection accuracy than Mixture of Gaussian, a background subtraction method.

articleTitle: Hashgraph-Based Model Parameter Management for Reliable and Secure Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Deep learning networks have rapidly developed across various fields, with several high-performing models already being applied in real-world applications. However, even with identical network architectures, variations in parameter values can lead to significantly different outputs, making the security of these parameters crucial for maintaining network performance. Despite their importance, limited research has focused on securing deep learning network parameters. In recent years, distributed ledger technologies, such as blockchain and hashgraph, have been extensively studied. Their applications extend beyond cryptocurrencies to include public services, voting, supply chains, and insurance. This paper proposes a novel approach to enhancing the security of deep learning network parameters by leveraging Hedera Hashgraph, providing a more secure foundation for their deployment and commercialization. With the security offered by hashgraph, model parameters are safely stored, ensuring the reliability and trustworthiness of deep learning systems. Additionally, when these stored parameters are used for further training, such as in transfer learning, the results are expected to be reliable. We demonstrate that our proposed system secures the parameters effectively, guaranteeing both security and reliability in deep learning.

articleTitle: Mutual Information Reduction Techniques and its Applications in Feature Engineering
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Feature engineering is a vital aspect of machine learning model development, as it involves selecting and transforming relevant data features to improve predictive accuracy. Traditional feature selection methods focus on maximizing mutual information (MI) between features and the target variable. In contrast, this paper introduces novel mutual information reduction techniques aimed at minimizing redundant information between features. By reducing mutual information among features, these methods enhance feature selection and creation, allowing machine learning models to benefit from less correlated and more informative variables. We provide examples and an implementation to demonstrate how mutual information reduction improves model performance, particularly in classification tasks. Additionally, the integration of Weight of Evidence (WOE) transformation further boosts predictive power by capturing the unique information from each feature.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Prompt-Engineering Techniques for Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the performance of three large language models (LLMs) - Llama3, Gemma2, and Mistral - using various combinations of prompt engineering techniques, focusing on the TruthfulQA and Winogrande datasets. In TruthfulQA, which emphasizes evaluating the truthfulness and cognitive errors of language models, the Chain of Thought (CoT) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques demonstrated superior performance. On the other hand, in Wino-grande, which assesses contextual reasoning abilities based on common-sense knowledge, CoT and In-Context Learning (ICL) were found to be effective. The performance analysis by model revealed that Llama3 exhibited the most significant improvement when prompt engineering techniques were applied. Meanwhile, Gemma2 achieved the highest overall performance across all evaluation metrics. This study highlights the importance of selecting appropriate prompt engineering techniques tailored to each model to maximize LLM performance, demonstrating that effective combinations of techniques can substantially enhance the models' reasoning abilities and accuracy.

articleTitle: SCENEDERELLA: Text-Driven 3D Scene Generation for Realistic Artboard
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As global media and Video-on-Demand (VOD) markets expand, efficiently producing high-quality 3D scenes has become a key challenge. Our study named SCENEDERELLA generates 3D scenes useful for the film industry using simple text prompts. Since traditional diffusion models create fantastic images, they have limitations in generating scenes truly desired by real-world users. However, fine-tuning the clip encoder of the diffusion model enables the production of realistic 2D scenes for users. Once the initial 2D scenes align with the user's conceptual expectations, we construct 3D scenes using a depth estimator and 3D Gaussian Splatting. The study successfully demonstrates the generation of 3D movie scenes based on various movie scripts. Our method overcomes the limitations of traditional physical set production and offers a new approach that enables the rapid creation of diverse scenes. Additionally, it can be used as a pre-visualization video to attract investment in movies and dramas. Our approach is expected to introduce a new paradigm in content production, with film, gaming, and advertising. Additional results and interactive demos are available at our project website.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Generative High-Fidelity One Shot Transfer for Virtual Kimono Try-on with Identity Loss Variation and Proposal for 3D Face Mesh Shape Loss
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study aims to realize the transfer of face shape while preserving the hairstyle through the improvement of the Generative High-fidelity One Shot Transfer (GHOST) of the face swapping model, and to apply it to the virtual try-on for kimono. This “face shape” refers to the contour and skeleton of the entire face, as well as specific features such as the forehead, cheekbones, nose, and chin. However, transferring facial shape is a challenge for face swapping models. Therefore, we considered that the shape of the SOURCE face could be retained by increasing the weight of Identity Loss, which is responsible for reproducing the features of the source face. In this study, we tested the effect on face shape retention by adjusting the weights of Identity Loss. As a result, there was no change in facial shape, but the lighting and brightness of the face changed, and naturalness was lost. These results suggest that it is difficult to accurately transfer the face shape only by adjusting Identity Loss. To address these issues, this study proposes the introduction of Shape Loss using 3D meshes. This approach is expected to be able to accurately transfer facial shapes and reproduce lighting and brightness naturally.

articleTitle: Integrative Human-Computer Interaction System Using Eyes and Facial Movement
