publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study investigates the possible improvement of communication systems for individuals with motor impairments, such as ALS, by the incorporation of real-time facial movement detection and eye tracking. We propose a system that combines webcam-based facial movement identification with an eye-tracking virtual keyboard, enabling users to customize input methods according to their physical ability. Seven healthy participants evaluated the system while seated in a single position. We evaluated essential criteria like input velocity, accuracy, and user comfort, and integrated a feature to gauge pain severity through facial expressions to enhance emergency situation prediction. The research demonstrate that participants exhibited varied preferences for facial characteristics, with improved performance noted when employing their preferred landmarks rather than non-preferred ones. This study implies that, when implemented for patients in an incomplete locked-in state, the system may increase communication and provide a customized solution aligned with each individual's preferences. The findings demonstrate that the use of real-time facial movement detection alongside eye-tracking enhances communication for individuals with severe motor impairments, providing a more efficient, customized, and practical alternative to traditional approaches.

articleTitle: Development of High Density 3D NAND Flash Memory Using New Scaling Technologies for AI Semiconductor
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Scaling technology of 3D NAND flash is recently required to implement large-capacity memory and high performance due to recent demand of AI semiconductors. However, it is suffering from the critical issues such as cell current, cell to cell interference and retention characteristics. In this paper, the new methods that enable for device scaling and performance were introduced.

articleTitle: An Improved Vision Transformer Architecture-Based Computer Recognition Platform for Lilium Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Lilies are popular in the global flower market, but consumers often lack information about specific varieties. To address this issue, this paper proposes a computer recognition platform based on the Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture. The proposed platform uses an improved vision transformer (ViT) architecture to classify different types of lilies, allowing consumers to access information and names of various Lilium species. The experimental results show that the proposed lily classification model achieved a 96.4% accuracy rate in classifying six lily species.

articleTitle: A Combined Method of Overhearing-Based Multicast and BitTorrent with Cooperative Group for Local Content Distribution within Wireless LAN
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: To address increasing demand for content distribution within a wireless LAN, this paper proposes a combined method of overhearing-based multicast and BitTorrent, which is designed to compensate for each other's weaknesses in wireless content distribution: overhearing-based multicast supports BitTorrent by distributing data to many nodes in a traffic-efficient manner, and BitTorrent provides nodes with the ability to download data pieces from multiple nodes in parallel and to retransmit data piece not received by overhearing. This paper also proposes to make nodes in the wireless LAN into a “cooperative group” for the more efficient use of wireless resources. Simulation results demonstrated that the proposed method can accelerate content distribution even when there is radio interference from another wireless LAN.

articleTitle: Autonomous Hardware-Trojan Generation Method Using Reinforcement Learning for Random Forest-Based Hardware-Trojan Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, the risk of inserting malicious circuits called hardware Trojan (HT) in the IC design process has become a serious concern. Although machine learning methods are effective in detecting HTs, their performance is not guaranteed for more difficult HTs. In order to make practical use of HT detection methods, they must be able to adapt to the daily updates of hard-to-detect HTs, and it is quite necessary to efficiently generate them. In this paper, we propose an autonomous HT generation method using reinforcement learning for random forest-based HT detection. The proposed method uses reinforcement learning to generate HTs efficiently and autonomously. The reinforcement learning algorithm used repeatedly generates new HTs and observes the HT detection accuracy, and learns a policy for modifying parameters during HT composition in order to minimize the HT detection accuracy. From the evaluation experiments, we confirmed that the proposed method generates HTs that are difficult to detect.

articleTitle: InstaSight: Leveraging AI to See Beyond Sight for Blind Users on Social Media
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study introduces “InstaSight,” a system enabling visually impaired individuals to engage with social media focused on visual content. InstaSight integrates a Single Board Computer, head-mounted webcam, and Bluetooth headset for seamless voice interactions. By utilizing the APIs of social media, speech recognition, and Large Language Models (LLMs), users can post photos and videos with voice-to-text captions and listen to comments converted from text or images. This system fosters social engagement, helping blind users connect and share experiences, improving their psychological well-being.

articleTitle: Enhancing ASR Performance through OCR Word Frequency Analysis: Theoretical Foundations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As the interest in large language models grows, the importance of accuracy in automatic speech recognition has become more pronounced. This is especially true for lectures that include specialized terminology. In such cases, the success rate of traditional ASR models tends to be low, presenting a significant challenge. A method using the word frequency difference approach has been proposed to improve ASR performance for specialized terminology. We investigated this proposal through experiments and data analysis to determine if it effectively addresses the issue. In addition, we introduced the power law as the theoretical foundation for the relative frequency methodology mentioned in this approach.

articleTitle: Outage Probability of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Assisted NOMA Cooperative System over Mixed FSO/RF Links
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) dual-hop free space optical (FSO)/radio frequency (RF) relaying communication system is presented where reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) with phase error and hybrid automatic repeat request (H-ARQ) protocols are considered on the RF link. The FSO link is subjected to Gamma-Gamma distributions with pointing errors while the RF link follows Nakagamim distributions. To quantify the system performance, the exact outage probability expressions for the near and far users are obtained. Under the same conditions, the results reveal the superiority of NOMA over orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and the accuracy of the results are validated via the Monte-Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: Searching Candidate Sequences for RNA Aptamers Using Quantum Computation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Addressing the problems of increasing time and cost for drug discovery is becoming more and more important. RiboNucleic Acid (RNA) aptamers have recently attracted attention as an emerging class of medium-molecule pharmaceuticals. However, searching the candidate sequences with conventional computers within a realistic timeframe is difficult due to the large search space. To overcome this problem, we employ Ising machines such as annealing quantum computers, which solve combinatorial optimization problems formulated as Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problems. In this study, we formulated the aptamer-sequence search problem as a QUBO problem based on the Systematic Evolution of Ligands by EXponential enrichment (SELEX) experimental data. We demonstrated that candidate RNA sequences were generated from a real Ising machine experiment and that those sequences can bind to the target protein. We concluded that our method is an efficient way to discover aptamers.

articleTitle: Thermal Management for In-Vehicle Emergency Call Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Given the life-saving significance of an automatic emergency call system for vehicles, it is imperative that it operates reliably under extreme environmental conditions such as high external temperatures. However, traditional thermal mitigation strategies from a System on Chip (SoC) perspective, where external cooling methods are not available, have primarily focused on reducing dynamic power by limiting the CPU clock frequency and this approach is insufficient for extremely high temperature situations. To address this issue, this paper examines the effects of managing static power in addition to dynamic power. It also expands the scope of power management from a SoC perspective to a product perspective, proposing an integrated thermal management solution. This solution has the potential for widespread application across various embedded systems where external cooling methods are not available.

articleTitle: A Crux on Audio-Visual Emotion Recognition in the Wild with Fusion Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper introduces recent advancements in emotion recognition using multimodal approaches, with a particular focus on real-world data. The primary challenge in this domain is accurately analyzing emotions in uncontrolled environments, where factors such as occlusion, illumination, and noise complicate data interpretation. To address these issues, we review studies that utilize various fusion techniques-such as early fusion, intermediate fusion, and late fusion-to effectively combine multiple modalities. Additionally, we conducted experiments using real-world dataset to evaluate performance and uncovered key limitations, including contextual mismatches and challenges in integrating diverse modalities. These findings highlight the importance of developing robust fusion strategies for real-world emotion recognition systems. Future work should focus on optimizing fusion strategies and enhancing model robustness to better handle the complexities of real-world data, and advance the field of Human-Computer Interaction.

articleTitle: Delta-ICM: Entropy Modeling with Delta Function for Learned Image Compression
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Image Coding for Machines (ICM) is becoming more important as research in computer vision progresses. ICM is a vital research field that pursues the use of images for image recognition models, facilitating efficient image transmission and storage. Demand and required performance for recognition models are rapidly growing within consumers. To meet these needs, exchanging image data between consumer devices and cloud AI using ICM technology could be one possible solution. In ICM, various image compression methods have adopted Learned Image Compression (LIC). LIC includes an entropy model for estimating the bitrate of latent features, and the design of this model significantly affects its performance. Typically, LIC methods assume that the distribution of latent features follows a normal distribution. This assumption is effective for compressing images intended for human vision. However, employing an entropy model based on normal distribution is inefficient in ICM due to the limitation of image parts that require precise decoding. To address this, we propose Delta-ICM, which uses a probability distribution based on a delta function. Assuming the delta distribution as a distribution of latent features reduces the entropy of image portions unnecessary for machines. We compress the remaining portions using an entropy model based on normal distribution, similar to existing methods. Delta-ICM selects between the entropy model based on the delta distribution and the one based on the normal distribution for each latent feature. Our method outperforms existing ICM methods in image compression performance aimed at machines.

articleTitle: Innovative Indoor Positioning System Based on Infrared Light Technology and SVR Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This work presents an indoor positioning system based on infrared (IR) cameras. The system gathers identity (ID) and 3D position information from an IR tag placed on the tracking target. Compared to other positioning methods, the proposed system offers precise positioning capability without high costs or privacy concerns. The system utilizes a two-stage Support Vector Regression (SVR) model to estimate the height of the IR tag in the real world and calculate the coordinates for positioning. Experimental results indicate that the proposed two-stage SVR model can effectively track the target's movement with an average 3D positioning error of 10.1 cm and achieve 100% accuracy in ID recognition.

articleTitle: A Crowdsourcing-Based Walk Test Approach to Evaluate Mobile Network Quality
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this study, we present a novel crowdsourcing-based approach to evaluate mobile network quality at Cheikh Anta DIOP University, located in Dakar, Senegal. Traditional methods of assessing network performance often require significant resources and infrastructure. By leveraging the power of crowdsourcing through a mobile application, we collected real-time data on network quality from various locations within the university campus. This approach enabled us to gather extensive data on signal strength, coverage, bandwidth and other metrics. The collected data was analyzed to generate comprehensive coverage maps and performance curves, highlighting areas of strong and weak network performance. Our results provide valuable insights for network operators of Senegal and university administrators to enhance network services and improve user experience. This approach demonstrates the efficacy of crowd-sourcing in conducting large-scale network quality assessments in educational environments.

articleTitle: Collecting Restaurant Information and Urban Analysis for Foreign Tourists to Realise Smart City
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In order to realise a smart city for foreign tourists, it is necessary to suggest which areas have an attractive concentration of restaurants. For this purpose, a survey was conducted in Tokyo using private gourmet information websites to investigate areas with a high concentration of restaurants for foreign tourists. By incorporating this method into smart city applications, foreign tourists can smoothly enjoy food culture.

articleTitle: Motion Classification by Utilizing Machine Learning for Acceleration Data
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, professional athletes have utilized motion analysis to improve their performance and skill. However, since devices and systems used in motion analysis are very expensive, it is impossible for an athlete who does not have enough budget to use them. In this paper, we propose a motion analysis system using an inexpensive accelerometer controlled by Arduino and machine learning. The target motion in this work is bat swing in baseball. The acceleration from the target motion is measured and used to train a neural network. Users of this system can classify their motion into experienced one and inexperienced one, and then will be able to know the quality of their swing motion.

articleTitle: Network Support for Distribution Transparency
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Assemble Computing which support distribution transparency from network level is proposed. Assemble Computing removes distinction between local and remote accesses and consequently provides the framework to support large-scale disaggregated computing.

articleTitle: An SRAM-Based PUF with High Native-Stability Using Alternative Configuration Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) is used in cryptography to generate secure keys for secure communication. Therefore, a PUF's stability in key generation is a serious concern. This work presents a novel alternative configuration architecture on SRAM-based PUF with enhancement-enhancement(EE)-structure bit cells to increase its native stability further while retaining low area overhead. Each PUF bit cell comes with an extra pair of load transistors that can act as a second entropy source if the original pair proves unstable. The design was fabricated with 180nm CMOS process. Measurements yielded two orders of magnitude Bit Error Rate (BER) improvement, from 0.765% before any stabilization methods to 0.00612% after reconfiguration and masking. The chip functions under 20 to 70°C while consuming 15.3pJ/bit given a 1.8V supply.

articleTitle: A Spatio-Temporal Recurrent Alignment for Video Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The proliferation of high resolution displays has made the demand for high-quality and computationally appropriate video super-resolution increase. Achieving top-notch video super-resolution boils down to effectively using information between frames. Yet, many current deep learning-based methods depend on complex network structures, such as bidirectional optical flow estimation, modulated deformable convolution, and cross-frame attention-based transformers. This paper introduces a practical video super-resolution method that leverages deep prior restoration information through the learning of spatio-temporal recurrent alignment. The features of our approach enable us to achieve excellent performance without the need for an expensive motion compensation stage. The algorithm's appeal for video super-resolution applications lies in its attractive combination of superior performance and reduced computational load. Our experimental results show the effectiveness and efficiency of video super-resolution, especially in real-world scenarios with diverse degradation types and complex motion compensation requirements.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Intra-Picture Coding Tools of Versatile Video Coding (VVC) Standard for 8K Video Resolution
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Versatile Video Coding (VVC), standardized in 2022 as ITU-T Recommendation H.266, ISO/IEC 23090–3 and MPEG-I Part3, is the latest block-based hybrid video coding standard which claims to fulfill all the requirements of todays and tomorrow's video applications. VVC defines more tools to increase compression efficiency while maintaining the same level of quality. The tradeoff is the computational complexity. H.266/VVC, especially the intra-coding loop, is computationally very complex due to its nature of iteratively trying all possible QTMT partitioning tree alternatives with all options of compression technologies. In this paper, we focus on the intra-coding loop of VVC for 8K video and study the effects of technologies like MTS, LFNST, MIP etc. on the compression efficiency (bits), quality (Y-PSNR), and computational complexity (runtime). By switching off all those optional technologies, we observe 46.07% runtime gain with only 5.00% increase in bitrate, and 0.0423 dB decrease in Y-PSNR on average. Since this is a remarkable gain in complexity with a limited effect on efficiency and quality, this tradeoff can be taken into consideration for many 8K applications utilizing VVC.

articleTitle: Speech Emotion Recognition Using Weighted Score Fusion for Low Resource Consumer Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Deep learning techniques have significantly advanced machine performance in tasks traditionally dominated by human expertise. One such task is speech emotion recognition (SER), a crucial component of affective computing. Given the inherent complexity of recognizing emotions, even for humans, there is a persistent demand for models that are both robust and accurate, yet less complex for deployment on low-resource devices. Despite notable progress in SER systems, achieving high performance with low-parameter models remains a challenge. In this paper, we introduce a transformer-based multilayer SER model (TBWSC model) that employs a weight score configuration (WSC) across shallow, intermediate, and high-level learned features. This approach enhances SER performance by utilizing a transformer encoder to capture detailed acoustic feature representations, reducing the need for a deep network. Our model achieves significant improvements with just three layers, compared to traditional deep architectures. Additionally, we performed a comprehensive evaluation of our proposed TBWSC SER model to highlight the benefits of weighted fusion and complexity reduction. The model was tested on multiple datasets, including the emotional German speech dataset (EMODB), the Surrey audio-visual expressed emotion (SAVEE) database, and the Toronto emotional speech set (TESS). These datasets encompass emotional states such as happiness, sadness, neutrality, and anger. Our TBWSC model demonstrated superior performance, achieving an average accuracy of 81.82% on EMODB, 82.22% on SAVEE, and 99.65% on TESS. These results underscore the effectiveness of our weighted feature fusion approach and the potential for deploying efficient SER systems in low resource consumer devices.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a Clock Distribution Method using Switching Matrices and a Two-Phase Clock Signal on an FPGA
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Very large-scale Integrations (VLSIs) are vulnerable to radiation, and VLSIs used in high radiation environments such as space environment and nuclear power plants have a short lifetime. Therefore, we are developing radiation-hardened optically reconfigurable gate arrays. Conventional optically reconfigurable gate array VLSIs have a weak point in clock distribution. This problem can be solved by a new clock distribution exploiting reconfigurable switching matrices. However, in this case, the clock skew increases. Therefore, to solve this problem, this paper proposes a new clock distribution method using a two-phase clock signal and switching matrices on an optically reconfigurable gate array VLSI. The proposed clock distribution method has been demonstrated on a Cyclone V FPGA by using a 4-bit counter circuit. This paper presents the demonstration results.

articleTitle: IoT Mobile Application for Alzheimer's Disease Caregivers
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Caring for a friend or family member diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease poses significant challenges due to the necessity for continuous supervision, attentive care, and support. Given the exorbitant expenses associated with professional nursing care, many families with limited financial resources find themselves relying on the unpaid assistance of friends and relatives to fulfill these caregiving responsibilities. Consequently, there is pressing demand for cost-effective health monitoring solutions and systems geared towards enhancing the quality of life for both patients and caregivers alike. This paper addresses this critical need through the development of an iOS mobile application. The application seamlessly integrates various Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, strategically designed to alleviate the burdens of caregiving. Central to its functionality, the application encompasses four key features: medication management, visual short-term memory assessment, facial recognition, and patient location tracking.

articleTitle: A Federated Learning Approach for Telerehabilitation Outcome Prediction in Parkinson's Disease
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this study, we propose a telerehabilitation system designed to remotely monitor patients and analyze data collected from wearable devices throughout a 12-week physical exercise program. The system, developed under the RAPIDO project, utilizes a multiple linear regression federated learning (MLRFL) approach to predict patients' rehabilitation outcomes while preserving data privacy. In particular, federated learning allows decentralized data analysis, ensuring that sensitive patient data remains on local devices while only model updates are shared. Preliminary results of the MLRFL compared to a centralized learning architecture show similar prediction performance while adding all the federated learning advantages, thus making it a promising approach.

articleTitle: Quantitative Reliability Assessment for 3D LiDAR Point Cloud Data Frames
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Digital twin technology plays a crucial role in realizing advanced mobility services such as autonomous driving; however, it is at risk because of potential tampering with three-dimensional (3D) point cloud data collected by Light Detection And Ranging (LiDAR) systems. This paper proposes a method to detect tampering in 3D point cloud data based on LiDAR scan line characteristics and to estimate a reliability score for each frame. Specifically, our method detects lost regions by calculating the angular differences between adjacent collected points and then applies a sigmoid function to the number of detected missing points to assign a reliability score. In experiments using the proposed method, we evaluated the reliability of tampered data, including consecutive and random data losses, and confirmed that the consecutive data loss resulted in a lower reliability score. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the data integrity for digital twins. The method holds promise for providing reliable 3D point cloud data in future implementations.

articleTitle: The Intelligent Systems of Skin Thickness in Measured by Optical Coherence Tomography
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study investigates the intelligent systems to evaluate walking interventions on skin thickness using Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT). The walking durations of 10 and 20 min were conducted with participants wearing insoles providing 160 mmHg air pressure. Skin thickness in the stratum corneum (SC) and epidermis (ED) was measured at four-foot regions: the big toe (T1), first metatarsal (M1), second metatarsal (M2), and heel (HL). Results revealed a significant decrease in SC at HL after 20 min of walking. This finding suggests that prolonged walking with air-pressure insoles may reduce mechanical stress at HL and could contribute to preventing and managing diabetic foot ulcers.

articleTitle: Preliminary Evaluation of Spatial Features for Real-Time Importance Estimation in Point Cloud
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: City digital twins enable artificial intelligence (AI)-empowered services in smart cities by leveraging city-scale point cloud data. However, real-time collection and utilization of point cloud for AI tasks incur significant communication and computational costs. A key strategy is to estimate important regions within real-time point cloud frames that contributes to specific AI tasks. This study introduces a spatial feature extraction method for real-time importance estimation between point cloud frames. The proposed method can calculate importance values in parallel for each voxel based on the difference in a spatial feature between past and current frames. Furthermore, experiments conducted with an actual device demonstrate the effectiveness of the model, including an analysis of the estimation results and real-time performance when applying various spatial features.

articleTitle: Security Architecture for Heterogeneous Chiplet-Based Mobile SoC
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Chiplet technology is increasingly being incorporated into System-on-Chips (SoCs), yet security considerations are often overlooked. This paper explores the security challenges specific to mobile SoCs constructed with heterogeneous chiplet technology and proposes a robust security architecture to address these risks. Using Android mobile systems as a case study, we propose an optimized architecture based on threat modeling and vulnerability categorization across various security scenarios. The proposed architecture is designed to maintain the existing security level of mobile SoCs by effectively partitioning IPs to minimize security threats without significantly increasing costs.

articleTitle: Content Prefetching Method for Scalable Video Streaming in IPFS
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a prefetching method for Interplanetary File System (IPFS) video streaming with scalable video coding. In the proposed method, the IPFS/HTTP gateway prefetches video segments that it predicts the client will play next from other gateways. This reduces the download time of video segments for the client, and improves the quality of the video segments. We evaluate the playback quality on a Docker network and show that the proposed method improves the average playback bitrate of the video. We also show that the proposed prefetching algorithm does not generate unnecessary traffic for the inter-gateway network, and that the video segments requested by the client are correctly prefetched by the gateway.

articleTitle: AI-Enabled Speech Monitoring for Dysarthria Detection in Consumer Electronics
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Speech is essential in human communication, and recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled new applications for voice data, particularly in health monitoring. Building on this progress, a home-based health detection system that utilizes voice signals provides an accessible method for users to independently identify and respond to conditions such as dysarthria, without the need for hospital or clinic visits. In this study, we developed and evaluated convolutional neural network (CNN) models to classify audio data from both healthy individuals and individuals with dysarthria. The dataset comprised command-based speech samples, which were segmented into sentence-specific input. Preprocessing steps included segmentation, downsampling, and feature extraction tailored for CNN input. The models exhibited high potential in distinguishing between normal and dysarthric states, with the most effective model achieving an f1-score of 96.18±4.7% and an accuracy of 96.01±5.02%. Furthermore, sentence structure and composition significantly influenced model performance, with specific sentences demonstrating higher classification accuracy. These findings suggest that AI-driven speech analysis may support detecting and managing specific health conditions in non-clinical environments. However, further work is needed to address data imbalance and sentence variability limitations. Future research could expand on real-world applications, particularly in settings with limited traditional health monitoring.

articleTitle: Energy-Conscious Image Enhancement for Dimmed Displays: Balancing Visual Quality and Power Efficiency for Consumer Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Display-enabled devices are an integral part of daily life, making power consumption a critical factor for consumers who rely on these gadgets for prolonged, uninterrupted use. Ensuring high visual quality while minimizing energy use is essential for enhancing the consumer experience. In this paper, we propose a method that leverages the concept of Just-Noticeable-Difference (JND) to optimize image luminance, thereby improving visual quality without increasing power consumption. Subjective evaluations confirmed that our approach significantly enhances the quality of dimmed images while maintaining or reducing energy consumption compared to state-of-the-art techniques, offering consumers both better performance and greater energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Robotic System Integrated with Object Classification and Gripping Pose Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This research leverages the Robot Operating System (ROS) to develop a software system that integrates an industrial computer, a six-axis robotic arm, a depth camera, and an adaptive gripper through ROS's distributed architecture. The objective is to devise a recognition and grasping strategy without CAD model matching by fusing 2D and 3D point cloud data. A deep learning network identifies target objects and determines optimal six degrees of freedom (6DoF) grasp poses. The robotic arm is controlled using inverse kinematics to grasp and sort four objects randomly positioned in the workspace, resulting in an 86% success rate and showcasing the system's efficacy.

articleTitle: Toward Scalable Heterogeneous Controller System for Various Quantum Computer by Using Multiple FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a control system capable of supporting various qubit platforms by combining control units with different specifications with a lightweight and common interface. To realize quantum computers, several qubit platforms, such as superconducting qubits, neutral atoms, ion traps, and semi-conductor quantum dots, are being researched. Each platform requires different microwave frequencies, channel numbers, intensities, and time scales for control. However, building individual control systems for each platform is not practical from a development cost perspective. Therefore, the standardization of control systems is desired. In practice, common languages and libraries for pulse control software are being developed as both commercial products and open-source projects. However, no widely adopted standardization methods currently exist for the control layer of electrical signals responsible for qubit manipulation. This paper first organizes the challenges in standardizing the control layer of electrical signals. It then proposes an architecture to address these challenges, featuring Ethernet-based unit inter-connections, a synchronization system based on time and pulses, and a lightweight and flexible waveform generation method. The proposed approach allows for practical cost adaptation to various types of qubits by connecting electronic circuits with specifications required for the target qubit platform.

articleTitle: BioMAS: A Wear-Free Biomechanical Motion Assessor for Physical Self-Training
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Physical training is essential for enhancing human health and aesthetics, playing a crucial role in daily life. However, individuals lacking expertise may face challenges in performing exercises correctly, which increases the risk of injury due to improper posture. To promote efficient physical self-training for individuals, we propose BioMAS, a novel motion assessor which captures and evaluates the performers motion through biomechanical analysis. BioMAS maximizes the performer's convenience by eliminating the need for wearable devices and instead utilizing video sensors for motion estimation. The proposed assessor first estimates human motion from multi-view RGB videos by leveraging deep learning and biomechanical models. From the estimated motion, biomechanical metric scores for balance, stability, and neutrality are provided for motion assessment. To validate the effectiveness of BioMAS, we developed the BioPT dataset, which includes biomechancial motion sequences paired with RGB videos on major weightlifting motion. Experimental results show that the estimated biomechanical motion from BioMAS has a joint error of approximately 53.2 mm compared to ground-truth human motion. Furthermore, we show that the proposed biomechanical metric scores exhibit a high correlation (≥ 80%) with the subjective scores evaluated by experts, confirming the efficacy of BioMAS for pyhsical self-training.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Random Access Approach for RIS-Aided Direct Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Satellite communication can provide seamless communication to handheld and high-throughput devices in remote areas, mountain areas or the ocean where cellular networks are unavailable or limited. These low-power devices may generate different types of traffic which requires various resources such as bandwidth or time slot according to their generated data. Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) are flexible and can be deployed to any environment to enhance transmission with low energy consumption. In this work, we propose a RIS-aided direct satellite network (RADSN) and a hybrid random access approach (HRA) to increase network throughput and support direct transmission for low-power devices. HRA consists of grant-free random access (GFRA) for single-packet users via direct satellite link and grant-based random access (GBRA) for multiple-packet users via RIS-aided link. By allocating preambles to different groups of users, our proposed protocol guarantees the fairness of successful preamble transmission probability. The simulation results show that our hybrid random access protocol can increase the total data rate for RIS-aided satellite communication with different types of users.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Cam-Lidar Fusion-Based BEV Segmentation in Weather and Day/Night Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Autonomous driving technology has been rapidly evolving as it becomes a core technology in the future automotive industry, driven by advancements in related sensors, components, platforms, and artificial intelligence technologies. This paper addresses Sensor Fusion-based BEV (Bird's Eye View) Segmentation, which has recently emerged as a major issue in autonomous driving technology. In this study, we analyzed the performance of Cam-Lidar Fusion BEV Segmentation and Cam-Only BEV Segmentation under different weather and time conditions, comparing them using various backbones and two different models. The experimental results were evaluated using mIoU. The best performance was achieved by the Cam-Lidar model, which reached 60.0%, whereas the Cam-Only model achieved 42.4%. On average, the Cam-Lidar model outperformed the Cam-Only model by 27.0%, with differences of 27.0%, 32.3%, and 26.9% under day, night, and rain conditions, respectively. The particularly low performance observed in the night environment is attributed to the Cam-Only model's average performance of 7.6% in detecting crosswalks during nighttime. Given this low performance, which is inadequate for autonomous driving, it is necessary to develop models that utilize LiDAR or RADAR to ensure accurate localization in low-light environments.

articleTitle: Virtual Reality Environment: Detecting and Inducing Emotions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) provides an innovative platform for investigating the verbal and non-verbal keys in emotion induction, as emotion plays a vital role in human interactions. However, the accurate identification of facial emotions in VR has been challenging. This paper introduces a novel approach to enhancing emotions in a VR immersive environment. Our proposed study leverages a Convolutional Neural Network approach to accurately identify real-time emotion detection with emotion induction within a VR environment during virtual health consultations. The proposed system was evaluated against existing methods, demonstrating superior performance in detecting and alleviating negative emotions such as sadness and frustration.

articleTitle: Practical Autostereoscopic 3D Display Using a Parallax Barrier With High Image Quality and Wide Viewing Area
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We have developed and commercialized a glasses-free 3D display with high image quality and a wide viewing range by solving the problem of screen darkness associated with the parallax barrier method. The eye tracking enabled us to determine which pixel was visible to which eye of the user at any given time, thus increasing the aperture ratio of the barrier. Our method is suitable for commercialization because it has a simple hardware structure and requires little image processing, and we have commercialized it. We have also implemented and commercialized a live 3D system without the need for special glasses using our 3D display.

articleTitle: An Architecture for Configuring HTML Applications That Run on Consumer Electronics Products
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The consumer electronics area is characterized by devices that operate on domestic premises. Among them, we can find digital TV (DTV) receivers, which currently present the ability to execute hypertext markup language (HTML) content through HTML version 5 (HTML5) engines. Indeed, such a resource may also be used to extend their capacities by sending new features encoded in an HTML (web) application, without software updates or changes. However, such a software enhancement must still be encoded, which is often done manually or partially automated with fixed and restricted templates. This work addresses this issue and proposes a methodology for dynamic HTML content creation based on three elements: Basic HTML container, JavaScript engine, and Orchestrator. To validate our proposal, we have used it to enhance an existing template-based feature that creates photo albums for presentation on DTV receivers, thus providing a free editing mode. As a result, presentations became richer and more flexible, created with an application that presents a lower memory footprint promptly and readily shows what you get.

articleTitle: GoodGPT: Counseling-Chat
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this study, we introduced GoodGPT, a korean generative neural network system designed to enhance counseling interactions by combining retrieval-augmented generation with advanced safeguard mechanisms. By leveraging a database of real counseling records and employing Dense Passage Retrieval, GoodGPT effectively retrieves contextually relevant information to inform its generative processes. This approach not only improves the relevance and appropriateness of the generated responses but also aligns them with professional counseling fields.

articleTitle: UMAP and Tree Physiology Optimization for Effective Water Quality Management in Consumer Electronics
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Leveraging UMAP for feature selection and Tree Physiology Optimization (TPO) for hyperparameter tuning, we proposed model for efficient water quality control in consumer electronics. We balanced the data with SMOTE from a Kaggle water quality dataset and using UMAP to find important characteristics. The TPO method then was used to maximize the parameters of the deep learning model. With an eye on few false positives, our algorithm was very accurate in spotting clean water. Still, the confusion matrix shows that there are difficulties precisely identifying dangerous water.

articleTitle: Leveraging Visual Language Information for Enhanced Person Re-Identification: A Robust Framework for Real-World Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Recently, performance improvements through vision-language learning have gained significant attention in the field of image re-identification (ReID). In particular, the CLIP-ReID [1] achieved enhanced visual representations by introducing learnable text token sets for each identity. However, existing approaches have not fully exploited fine-grained part-specific features of the human body, which are crucial when applying person re-identification technology in real-world scenarios where partial occlusions or other factors might affect accuracy. To address this limitation, we propose a novel framework that incorporates body part-specific learnable text tokens, leveraging visual language information related to specific body regions. This approach is essential for mitigating the impact of occlusions and enhancing the robustness of ReID systems in practical settings. The process of applying visual language information through CLIP-ReID involves several stages. First, body part regions are identified and segmented within the image. Next, visual features specific to these regions are extracted and mapped to corresponding text tokens that describe these features in natural language. Finally, these text tokens are integrated with the image features to create a more comprehensive representation that captures both visual and semantic aspects, improving the discrimination of individuals based on specific anatomical features. Experimental results not only using the MSMT17 [2] and Market-1501 [3] datasets but also from a real-world scenario involving 11 CCTV cameras installed on the campus of Chung-Ang University demonstrated that the proposed method significantly outperformed existing models. This confirms the effectiveness of vision-language learning that utilizes segmented body part information in the image re-identification task.

articleTitle: Power Consumption Analysis in LCD and AMOLED Display Technologies for Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: When analyzing the battery consumption of mobile devices, one of the primary components considered is the display, which presents distinct consumption characteristics depending on the screen technology used. Furthermore, developing energy-efficient display technologies is critical, as they are a substantial source of smartphone battery consumption. In this study, we consider a comparative analysis between smartphones with two display technologies, Liquid Crystal Display (LCD) and Dynamic Active Matrix Organic Light-Emitting Diode (AMOLED), employed in modern mobile devices. The results showed a considerable energy saving for the Dynamic AMOLED compared to PLS TFT LCD technology, with reductions of up to 72.49%.

IEEE Keywords: Active matrix organic light emitting diodes

articleTitle: Integrated Path Tracking and Control Algorithm for Autonomous Driving of a 1/10 Scale Vehicle Using Low-Cost Cameras
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, key technologies are proposed to achieve Level 5 autonomous driving, and the feasibility of these technologies is discussed. The proposed technologies focus on environmental perception using cameras, decision-making, and driving control. While it is common to use LiDAR and radar for perceiving various driving environments, only cameras are utilized in this research to reduce the number of sensors and simulate the process similar to human driving. A combination of path following and optimal controllers is employed to ensure basic driving on roads using the information collected from the cameras. Before applying the proposed algorithm to a full-scale vehicle, it is tested on a 1/10 scale miniature car to verify its performance. Additionally, participation in the ICCE Design Competition 2025 is planned to evaluate the effectiveness of the algorithm in a real-world driving environment.

articleTitle: GOLD: Green Optimization of Language Models Serving on Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: With the growing integration of language models into embedded devices, enhancing energy efficiency while maintaining target performance is essential. This paper presents GOLD, a policy that enhances on-device language model inference using DVFS and power management via reinforcement learning. GOLD optimizes energy use, extending battery life by up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.39\times$</tex> and increasing performance by 4%. This solution supports sustainable AI for energy-limited environments, meeting the rising demand for LLM on the device.

articleTitle: Vehicle Platooning Based on Second-Order Pinning Consensus Control and Its Cyber Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a control method of vehicle platoons based on pinning consensus control and its cyber attack detection. One of the control problems in multi-agent systems is the consensus problem, in which the state of each agent is matched through communications. Pinning control is a method of adding external control inputs to pre-specified agents called pinning agents. It can accomplish setting the state of an agent to a value other than its initial average value or speeding up the rate at which it converges. Model Predictive Control (MPC), a method of obtaining control inputs by solving a finite-time optimal control problem at each discrete time, is applied. Using pinning consensus control and MPC, we consider vehicle group control, in which multiple vehicles are controlled as a single group. In addition, a method for detecting cyber attacks on pinning agents is also proposed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Hardware-Trojan Detection by Ensemble Learning Model for Circuits Inserted with a Trojan by an Automated Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: During the design and manufacturing stages of IoT devices, there is a risk of Hardware Trojans (HTs) being inserted into circuits due to the intervention of outside companies. One method for effectively detecting HTs from gate-level netlists is to use an ensemble learning model. In this paper, we use four ensemble learning models: Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, and evaluate the accuracy of HT detection by adding a new Trojan circuit generated using an automatic HT generation framework as a netlist for training and evaluation. We also use SMOTE, ADASYN, and Borderline-SMOTE as oversampling methods used in training, and evaluate the HT detection accuracy when the hyperparameters of each method are optimized.

articleTitle: HomeBud: A Smart IoT Watering System for Indoor Plants
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Indoor plants are known to benefit their owners in a variety of ways. Plants can serve useful functions within the home, such as herbs for cooking or various plants for insect repelling, or increase one's mental health by lowering stress levels. Unfortunately, caring for plants can be difficult for people who have busy schedules, lack experience in plant care, or have health complications or disabilities. This paper explores a way to automate plant care-taking while being space, time, and cost-efficient. The system runs on an Arduino Uno R4 which automates the plant watering process and uses a grow light in order to ensure that the plant is getting the appropriate amount of light every day. This system can be controlled using an app, which allows for monitoring as well as setting target soil moisture and daily light amounts, which can be tailored for the plant being cared for. Novice users may not know exactly how much water or light their plants may need, so the companion app also include presets for common plants. This system will enable more people to take better care of plants, allowing more people to reap the benefits of keeping indoor plants, even if their lifestyle makes it otherwise difficult.

articleTitle: Automated Classification of Multi-Class Brain Tumor with Lightweight CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Classification of brain tumors is crucial for accurate diagnosis because different types of tumors have different treatment requirements. Through precise classification, doctors can develop more effective treatment plans, improving patient survival rates. However, current deep-learning models utilized for brain tumor classification typically exhibit large parameter sizes and high computational complexity. Therefore, we proposed a lightweight deep learning model named PatchBT-Net to reduce computational complexity and maintain accuracy. PatchBT-Net mainly includes technologies such as patch stems and channel attention blocks, which can effectively classify brain tumors in MRI data. PatchBT-Net uses 99.98% fewer parameters than the pre-trained VGG16 model and achieves 97.55% accuracy on the CE-MRI dataset.

articleTitle: Efficient Task Scheduling Using Constrains Programming
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a constraint programming algorithm designed for efficient task scheduling in Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) operations, specifically for aircraft engines. By leveraging historical data from Korean Air's MRO maintenance logs, the proposed method achieves optimal scheduling performance by minimizing total maintenance days and maximizing resource utilization. Experimental results reveal an average utilization rate of 99.34%, with some cases reaching 100%. Furthermore, this study explores the potential application of the algorithm in consumer electronics manufacturing, emphasizing its adaptability to various industrial environments. The findings highlight the algorithm's ability to optimize resource allocation, reduce operational downtime, and enhance scheduling efficiency, paving the way for broader industrial applications.

articleTitle: Using Integrated Chips in IoT for Health to Monitor Non-Contact Heart Rate Variability
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, the Internet of Health Things (IoHT) components have been increasingly used, allowing entire circuit modules to achieve circuit simplification and miniaturization. These components are characterized by their lightweight and low power consumption. Therefore, we use a BMD101 commercial module as the front-end circuit for measuring non-contact electrocardiogram signals, significantly reducing the volume and power consumption compared to the original discrete circuits. Although the measurement method does not require direct contact with the human body, we still aim to place the electrodes as close to the body surface as possible. The electrodes are made of conductive fabric and polymer foam, which are flexible and easily conform to the body, thereby obtaining a better signal-to-noise ratio for electrocardiogram signals and accurate HRV parameters.

articleTitle: Advanced Teeth Instance Segmentation Using Contextual Spatial Attention and Deeper Mask Head
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Dental image analysis has advanced significantly with deep learning, yet achieving accurate teeth segmentation remains challenging, particularly with complex structures like adjacent or small teeth. This paper introduces Segmentation based on Contextual Spatial Attention Block (Seg-CSAB), a novel framework that integrates the CSAB with dilated convolutions to enhance feature extraction while maintaining high spatial resolution and an increased receptive field. Unlike traditional segmentation models, which often lose spatial information and compromise the representation of small structures due to downsampling, Seg-CSAB effectively captures fine-grained spatial details and contextual relationships between teeth, improving the understanding of smaller tooth structures and adjacent teeth. Additionally, Seg-CSAB features a deeper mask head with three additional convolutional layers (3 ×3) before the transposed convolution and final convolution layer, refining segmentation output and enhancing boundary delineation. It outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, including Yolov8 and Mask R-CNN, in comprehensive segmentation, both qualitatively and quantitatively, offering substantial improvements in dental image analysis and treatment planning.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-based Core Assignment in TCP Transmission for SDM-OPS Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The amount of traffic in the network is increasing due to the emergence of various video-based applications and cloud-based services. Space-division multiplexing optical packet switching (SDM-OPS) network using multi-core fiber exists as a technology to cope with the increase in traffic volume. However, as the network load increases, packet loss increases rapidly due to optical packet collisions and optical signal degradation, and as a result, communication quality deteriorates. Therefore, it is necessary to predict in advance which spatial/frequency channels are likely to cause packet loss before the network load increases, and to control the amount of traffic by adaptively exploiting those channels. In this paper, we focus on TCP-based packet transmission in SDM-OPS network using multi-core fiber, and investigate the performance of control mechanisms for predicting the number of packet losses in the near future (within 1[s]) using time series analysis and multiple machine learning methods.

articleTitle: Colorization Quality Assessment with CLIP
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Automatic colorization of grayscale images defies simple evaluation by quantitative metrics because there can be multiple equally good but different “truths,” making consistent evaluation challenging. To address this problem, we propose an evaluation model for image colorization that utilizes prompt learning, with novel components Color-Query Cross Attention Block and addition of Positive and Negative input images, based on the prior knowledge CLIP possesses. This complements conventional metrics by evaluating naturalness of the colorization based on the scene content.

articleTitle: Robust TDOA Estimation Using Kernel Density Estimation for Noisy Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In various applications, the importance of localization has increased significantly. In this study, we propose a method combining a filter bank and kernel density estimation (KDE) for robust localization even in noisy disaster environments. The proposed technique applies a filter bank to the input signal to separate it into multiple frequency bands, allowing for the analysis of signal characteristics within each band. Subsequently, generalized cross correlation with phase transform (GCC-PHAT) is calculated for the signals in each separated frequency band. KDE is then applied to the computed GCC-PHAT to estimate the probability density function and determine the time difference of arrival (TDOA) values. Finally, the TDOA results are used to determine a final TDOA, and the coordinates where hyperbolas most closely intersect are estimated as the sound source's location. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional techniques in noisy environments and is a robust solution for sound source localization in complex real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Reduced Bfloat Mode Switching on Precision Modulated Shading for Mobile GPU
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to reduce GPU power consumption while maintaining image quality when using Precision Modulated Shading (PMS). PMS saves power by dynamically adjusting precision based on the sensitivity of instructions. We introduce enhanced PMS logic to solve image corruption issues by employing a heuristic algorithm that considers branch instructions to make accurate decisions. To further mitigate the overhead associated with switching Bfloat modes in the microarchitecture, a more aggressive mode heuristic algorithm is proposed. When applied to the Aztec High GPU benchmark, our algorithm achieved an average PSNR of 52.47 dB and a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>inimum PSNR of 47.4 dB. Moreover, GPU power consumption decreased by 1.99%, and FPS/Watt performance improved by 2.51 %.

articleTitle: Proposal for Enhancing Manufacturing Efficiency with Generative AI and Surveillance Cameras
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a system aimed at maximizing the productivity of small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises by improving operational efficiency through advanced image analysis. The system utilizes surveillance cameras to meticulously examine the spatial arrangement and activities of equipment and workers. Object detection and random forest techniques are employed to perform action recognition and distinguish tasks based on these actions. The extracted images are analyzed with GPT-4o to provide suggestions for task improvement. This system is particularly tested on inspection tasks and effectively guides improvements through detailed image analysis.

articleTitle: Open Source Metaverse Platform System for Educational Engagements and Research Activities Using Layered Multicast Method
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper introduce “chutvrc,” a web-based open-source metaverse platform system software designed to enhance educational engagements and research activities operable on various consumer devices. As a successor to Mozilla Hubs, chutvrc aims for high extensibility and customizability, specifically tailored to meet the needs of educational institutions and research communities. It is designed to be accessible from various devices and display environments, including VR equipment, PCs, smartphones, and tablets, ensuring broad interconnectivity and interoperability within the metaverse. A unique feature of chutvrc is its layered multicast teaching/speaking functionality, which allows for seamless educational sessions across multiple virtual rooms, enhancing the collaborative and interactive experience for educators and learners. Fully open source, chutvrc includes the client, server, protocol, and component software, benefiting educators and researchers by preserving all components of the virtual environment. This comprehensive open-source approach supports research replication and the management of 3D research data, enabling reanalysis and further contributing to the academic and research community.

articleTitle: A Verification System of AR Information Provision for Drivers Using Virtual Reality Driving Simulator
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Providing information to drivers is expected to promote the early detection of pedestrians. To develop an effective system for this purpose, we constructed a Virtual Reality Driving Simulator (VRDS) that replicates dangerous situations, such as potential collisions between vehicles and pedestrians. The system uses a simple augmented reality (AR) icon to notify drivers of crossing pedestrians. Additionally, it offers a controlled environment for testing Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) functions under development, which are difficult to evaluate on real roads. In this study, we focus on right turns at signalized intersections, where accidents frequently occur, and verify the effectiveness of the proposed system in such scenarios.

articleTitle: Design of Smart Farm Service Architecture Based-On Microservice
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: With the rapid advancements in IoT, big data, and AI technologies, smart farm and agriculture have emerged as a key solution for improving productivity and maintaining optimal crop growth environments, leading to various ongoing studies. As part of this research, this paper proposes a microservice-based smart agriculture framework that integrates cloud and edge computing. The framework consists of cloud, edge, controller, and device entities, each playing a crucial role in ensuring efficient environmental control and real-time decision-making for crop growth. By incorporating edge computing, the proposed service architecture mitigates issues related to network latency and failures, thereby enhancing system stability and responsiveness. Moreover, the service management module, present in both cloud and edge entities, enables flexible service scalability and version control while ensuring seamless operation even during network outages. Through the implementation of a testbed, we validated the system's operational procedures and demonstrated that the edge-enabled architecture reduces response times by approximately 40% in high-latency network conditions. This study highlights the potential of edge computing in smart agriculture and lays the groundwork for future research focusing on comprehensive performance evaluations and high-availability service monitoring in various environments.

articleTitle: A Multi-CAM Based Robust Interpretations Framework in Medical Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Recently, methods for interpreting the decision of deep learning models have been actively used in medical imaging. Still, some studies provide interpretations based solely on a singular method, such as GradCAM. This approach has the limitation to reduce reliability by providing only fragmentary information about model predictions. In this study, we propose a framework that multi-interpretations of model results to improve the reliability of deep learning based diagnostic assistance systems. We combined several CAM based methods and deep learning model and analyzed the differences in interpretation based on the CAM methods. The results show that the same image has different interpretations depending on the CAM, which means that multiple interpretations through a combination of appropriate CAM and deep learning models are essential. Consequently, the proposed framework can improve diagnostic reliability and increase the usability of AI-based diagnostic assistance systems by providing multiple interpretations of model predictions.

articleTitle: A Modular IQ Baseband Digitizer for Post-Fabrication Testing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Advances in modern semiconductor ICs require sophisticated test solutions during the post-fabrication testing phase. Compared to a fixed logic test instrument, a synthetic test instrument is more programmable to handle increasingly challenging test requirements. Among synthetic instruments, a digitizer plays an important role in many high-speed and high-precision applications. In this work, we design a baseband digitizer for high-volumn postfabrication testing applications. The proposed digitizer is designed to analyze intermediate frequency (IF) signals in real time from a DUT to measure gain, IM2, IM3, phase noise, and noise figure. The digitizer hardware was manufactured on a 20-layer printed circuit board (PCB) with discrete components. The functionality of the proposed digitizer was verified in capturing and displaying the spectrum of an input sample. The mismatch between in-phase and quadrature channels was characterized by computing the digitizer's image rejection ratio (IMRR). The results show that the digitizer has an intrinsic IMRR of 57.4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{dBc}$</tex> with a magnitude imbalance of 0.0173 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{dB}$</tex> and a phase imbalance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.1^{\circ}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Explainability of Large Language Models for Ethical Decision Making
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The innate ethical decision-making capabilities of large language models (LLMs) has been previously assessed in the literature using a classification-based workflow. An analysis performed for morally unambiguous scenarios indicated strong alignment between LLM and human ethical judgement. This paper proposes an enhanced explainability-based workflow for exploring the ethical decision-making capabilities of LLMs. In addition to producing binary labels indicating moral acceptability, models are prompted to produce justifications for their decisions. We propose and verify an approach for assessing similarity in the produced justifications across prompting style using latent semantic analysis. We demonstrate that justifications produced for identical moral scenarios are considerably more similar than those produced for arbitrary scenario combinations. We also show that variability in the similarity of justifications produced across prompting styles is negligible as expected for the morally unambiguous scenarios considered.

articleTitle: Toward Enhancing 6G Security and Resilience with Blockchain: A Case Study on Mitigating SUCI Replay Attacks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Security/resilience is one of the four overarching aspects of 6G requirements. To enhance resilience, one potential technology that can be integrated into the network is blockchain. By leveraging synchronized and distributed peers participating in the blockchain network, blockchain technology mitigates single points of failure and provides enhanced resilience. To demonstrate the potential application of blockchain in 6G networks, we analyzed the SUCI(Subscription Concealed Identifier) replay attack reported by the 3GPP(3rd Generation Partnership Project) and proposed a blockchain-based solution to address this issue. Using an open-source 5G project, we implemented and tested the feasibility of integrating blockchain into the network, showcasing its potential to enhance security and resilience in next-generation communication systems.

articleTitle: A Fully Digital Neuromorphic AI Processor for Industrial and Consumer Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study introduces a fully digital neuromorphic AI processor architecture specifically developed for diverse scientific fields, with a particular emphasis on deep learning applications. The suggested design utilizes Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) to accurately mimic biological neural processes, while also providing scalability and flexibility through the use of fully digital circuits. The main characteristics consist of scalable parallel neuron arrays, adjustable neuron model implementation, and learning algorithms. The design includes temporal information-based weight calculations with a Winner-Takes-All (WTA) mechanism to enhance bio-plausibility. This adaptable and efficient framework holds potential for enhancing data processing and analysis in various scientific areas.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Behavioral Biometric Authentication for Heterogeneous Actions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Authentication methods based on behavioral characteristics identify individual user behavior patterns and utilize them for user authentication. Compared to traditional methods like passwords and biometrics, this approach offers a more natural and convenient authentication experience. Behavioral biometrics are expected to find applications in areas like ID proofing and surveillance. Authentication methods using accelerometers can directly capture user movements but require users to constantly carry devices, limiting their use in surveillance scenarios. On the other hand, gait recognition based on their walking patterns from general video sequences has gained significant attention. Gait recognition is considered highly distinctive due to subtle variations based on individual physique and physical traits. However, focusing solely on gait presents challenges in static scenarios. We propose a novel method that decomposes the entire skeleton into parts and calculates feature values for each part. Then, it merges the features based on their joint visibility. The proposed method demonstrated higher accuracy compared to a baseline method using full-body features, based on proof-of-concept experiments using the MMAct and CASIA-B datasets.

articleTitle: A Proposed LLM-Based Supported Treatment Framework for Intracerebral Hemorrhage
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study proposed a large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent chatbot system to assist inexperienced clinicians during the interhospital transfer of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) patients. This framework utilizes LLM trained on medical guidelines, real clinical case data, and Q&A datasets to offer real-time case responses. The approach could support medical staff in making decisions using the chatbot system during the interhospital transfer in medically underserved areas. To examine the feasibility of this study, the actual clinical scenarios based on the ICH prompt were assessed by three neurosurgeons. As a result, the overall performance of the chatbot received positive evaluations. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed LLM-based chatbot framework to support medical staff in clinical practice.

articleTitle: Shoe-Based PDR System for Two-Dimensional Tracking
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The most famous absolute self-positioning is GPS (Global Positioning System). However, GPS cannot be used in indoor and underground environments. Thus, relative positioning methods such as sensor-based pedestrian dead reckoning (PDR) are required. The visually impaired has difficulty using navigation devices using visual information, such as smartphones, and it is necessary to develop navigation devices using non-visual information. In this paper, we propose a highly accurate two-dimensional PDR using Ashirase device, a shoe-based wearable sensor. This sensor provides non-visual navigation aids through the underfoot vibrations and has an accurate position estimation as the sensor is strongly attached to the shoe. The proposed method obtained a low estimation error <0.2% walking in straight lines and <1.2% walking in circles.

articleTitle: A Performance Evaluation of Zeek-Based Intrusion Detection in Agricultural IoT Security
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As agricultural networks become more connected, they face increased risks from cyber threats that can compromise the security of farming operations. In a previous study, we explored the potential of Zeek, an open-source Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS), in securing IoT devices within agricultural scenarios. This initial work, conducted in a Raspberry Pi virtual environment, showed promise in detecting cyber threats through offline analysis of pcap files. However, the dynamic and unpredictable nature of active farming environments necessitates a more comprehensive evaluation of security solutions that cannot be fully captured in offline experiments alone. This paper extends our prior work by investigating Zeek's implementation under both offline and real-time conditions, addressing the need for a more thorough understanding of its performance in dynamic agricultural case studies. We deploy Zeek in a virtual environment, providing a controlled and isolated testing platform for our experiments. For offline analysis, we utilize pcap files from the Stratosphere laboratory dataset, containing a mix of genuine and malicious traffic. Then, real-time analysis is conducted using various network tools to simulate live attack scenarios. The study specifically examines Zeek's effectiveness in identifying and mitigating two critical types of cyber threats relevant to IoT agriculture: unauthorized access attempts and distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks.

articleTitle: Assessment Device for the Stability of Osseointegration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The study aims to develop and justify a hand-held stability assessment device for osseointegration prostheses. Four types of probes based on electromagnetic actuation and detection mechanisms are designed and implemented. A dual-core microcontroller is employed to actuate implant structure, acquire response data, and evaluate structural resonance. The developed device assists physicians in assessing and following up on the status of osseointegration stability after a prosthesis operation.

articleTitle: Implementation of Gamified Programming Learning Assistant System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Despite the rapid growth of the ICT sector, there is a gap between it and STEM education, resulting in high dropout rates in computer science and engineering programs. This has led to many vacancies in the ICT job market. A major challenge is that traditional teaching methods fail to engage students in difficult and abstract STEM subjects like programming.
