To overcome this, innovative technology-enhanced learning solutions are needed. In the past, we created a Programming Learning Assistant System (PLAS) to help novice students learn programming. PLAS provides various types of exercises to develop code reading and writing skills at different levels. In this paper, we implement the gamification into PLAS to enhance students' understanding of programming concepts, boost their confidence, spark their interest in STEM fields, and increase engagement in the course through interactive and stimulating scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhancing Sidewalk Maintenance through Accurate Joint Deflection Measurement
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this work, we propose a novel real-time method for precise measurement of sidewalk joint deflections utilizing stereo vision and deep learning. This method is designed to address key challenges in infrastructure management within the context of smart cities. Our approach leverages stereo vision to establish a highly accurate Pixel-to-Meter ratio, enabling the precise conversion of image data into real-world distances. This allows for precise measurement of joint deflections by capturing depth information between adjacent sidewalk slabs. We then integrate instance segmentation, which enables the precise identification of individual sidewalk slabs, facilitating the accurate detection of joint deflections between these sections. Together, these techniques provide a robust method for detecting and measuring sidewalk joint deflections with high precision. Our results demonstrate the potential of our method for large-scale deployment in smart cities, with future work focused on integrating the system into predictive maintenance frameworks and expanding its application across diverse urban settings.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Comparable Commitment Scheme for Secure System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A commitment scheme is a cryptographic scheme that can verify the authenticity of the sender's input value. The verifiability of the input value is a main feature of commitment schemes suitable for sealed-bid auctions. The sealed-bid auction is a scheme of finding who is the highest bidder with the bidding price hidden. On the other hand, since the bidding value depends on the amount one can pay oneself, publishing the bidding value is as same act as publishing the amount of the user bank account. Galal and Youssef constructed a verifiable sealed-bid auction based on the homomorphic commitment scheme in 2018. In their scheme, the bidding price of the user is converted to a commitment value, and they used an interactive zero-knowledge proof to hide all users' input values in their scheme. However, their scheme uses zero-knowledge proof to guarantee the privacy-preserving. It is simpler to construct a scheme without using zero-knowledge proofs, and it is more efficient since the verification time is smaller. To overcome this problem, we propose the Privacy-Preserving Comparable Commitment Scheme (PPCCS) to identify who has the highest input value without using zero-knowledge proof. Our PPCCS uses a special encoding scheme called 0/1-Encoding to construct a commitment value, which allows Receiver (verifier) to identify who has the largest input value during the commitment phase. Moreover, our PPCCS is even more privacy-preserving than general homomorphic commitment schemes, since no other sender except Receiver can compare each commitment value. We also prove our PPCCS satisfies binding and hiding properties.

articleTitle: An Experiment to Find Effective Conditions for Fast Walking Support
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Fast walking is an easy-to-practice exercise like run-ning. The authors focus on support for ideal (constant pitch and pace) fast walking. The authors utilized vibration and sound as ex-isting running support. The authors aim to find which conditions are efficient for ideal fast walking. As an experiment, three males fast-walked with different support conditions. As a result, the walking pitch was more constant when they walked with support. A combination of vibration and sound tended to be more effective than presenting one of them. And the pitch tended to be closer to the ideal pitch with support. The walking pace tended to be more constant with support. It will be necessary to select music appropriate for each person, as the effect of music seems to vary from person to person.

articleTitle: Empirical Evaluation of an FPGA-Based Vibration Extraction System for Stabilization of Surgical Instruments Under a Microscope
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper evaluates an image-based real-time vibration extraction FPGA system that aims to suppress involuntary tremors in microsurgery. Three empirical experiments are conducted to evaluate the vibration-extraction accuracy and suppression effect in the actual setup. First, vibration extraction experiments are conducted using synthesized endoscopic surgery video to evaluate vibration-extraction accuracy. Experiments are also conducted with various values of system parameters to evaluate their influence on the extraction accuracy. Next, the vibration extraction system is connected to an anti-phase vibration exciter to evaluate the basic performance as an active vibration suppression system. Finally, practical vibration suppression experiments are carried out using a vibration reproduction device that can generate vibrations based on recorded data of actual tremors. The results show that the system effectively reduces the target vibration components of tremors. On the other hand, an increase in the vibration components outside the target frequency band suggests that the accuracy of the vibration exciter significantly affects the quality of the system.

articleTitle: Prototyping of an MPEG-DASH Player for Verifying and Presenting Content Provenance Information
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Recently, with the development of generative AI technology, the spread of disinformation and misinformation on the web has become an issue, making it challenging for content viewers to judge the credibility of information. We focus on using “provenance information,” which indicates the source and production process of content, as one of the criteria for viewers to determine whether they can trust content. We developed a prototype system that attaches provenance information to video content for streaming distribution, and an MPEG-DASH video player that verifies the attached provenance information and presents the results to viewers on smart TV. Our system and player comply with the specifications set by C2PA, an international standard organization.

articleTitle: Environmental Control with In-Bed Airflow to Improve Sleep Quality
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: It is important to fluctuate core body temperature appropriately according to the circadian rhythm in order to improve sleep quality. In order to efficiently promote fluctuations in core body temperature, we focused on the soles of the feet, an important site for heat dissipation. We thought that controlling the temperature and humidity near the soles of the feet would create promote effective heat dissipation and a comfortable environment, so we blew air into the sleeping area as a way to control the temperature and humidity. As a result, we confirmed that the temperature and humidity inside the beds were lower than when there was no air blowing, and that this had a positive effect on subjective comfort. In this experiment, the main focus was on the airflow and the in-bed environment, but it is expected to have a positive effect on core body temperature and sleep structure.

articleTitle: 3D Cloud Position Estimation for Solar Radiation Forecasting Using Time-Series Stereo Vision Integrated with All-Sky and Satellite Images
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We propose a method to estimate the 3D position of clouds using time-series stereo vision from all-sky and satellite images, aimed at improving the accuracy of short-term solar radiation forecasting for photovoltaic power generation. Our method focuses on the temporal dynamics of cloud movement, eliminating the need for pattern matching across images from different viewpoints. By capturing a sequence of all-sky images and using optical flow, cloud motion on the celestial sphere can be tracked. Additionally, by utilizing the cloud motion speed on satellite images and assuming that the vertical movement of the cloud is much smaller compared to their horizontal movement, we estimate the 3D position. We evaluate the effectiveness of our approach using both simulated and real cloud videos. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method can estimate the 3D positions of various types of clouds, including thick and thin clouds, expanding the range of cloud types that can be effectively analyzed. Quantitative evaluations confirm the method's robustness.

articleTitle: Quantum-Enhanced Space Energy Monitoring: Quantum Sensors and Key Protocols for Precision and Secure Communication in Extreme Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The advancement of quantum technology holds significant promise for enhancing space-based applications, particularly in energy monitoring and data security. This paper investigates the integration of quantum sensors with advanced Quantum Key Protocols (QKP) to optimize and secure energy monitoring systems in space environments. Quantum sensors provide exceptional accuracy in measuring space-based energy sources, including solar radiation and cosmic energy, thereby enabling improved energy harvesting and utilization for space missions. QKP safeguards the integrity of the data collected by these sensors, employing quantum cryptography and entanglement to protect against potential threats such as data interception and tampering. This integrated approach addresses critical challenges such as signal attenuation, data integrity, and secure communication over long distances. This research will present a detailed analysis of the development and deployment of quantum sensors and QKP within space-based energy systems. The paper highlights advancements in sensor technology that enhance monitoring precision and examines the efficacy of QKP in maintaining data security under extreme space conditions. Results include prototype demonstrations, performance evaluations, and a comprehensive discussion of the benefits and limitations of this integrated technology. Findings in this paper indicate substantial improvements in both the accuracy of space-based energy monitoring and the security of data transmission, advancing the capability of space missions.

articleTitle: Lightweight Gaze Tracking Model Based on GhostNet
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In previous lightweight methods, most efforts focused on reducing the number of model parameters to lower computational requirements for terminal deployment. The aim of minimizing parameters is to achieve faster inference speeds. However, this often leads to a significant drop in accuracy. This paper seeks to accelerate model inference speed while maintaining accuracy with fewer parameters, facilitating easier deployment on terminal equipment. The proposed method employs the lightweight model GhostNet with a specialized-designed depthwise convolution. We further introduce a novel block to enhance the L2CS gaze tracking model. This approach allows the gaze tracking model to utilize a lightweight architecture from the training phase to inference one, achieving real-time performance while maintaining acceptable accuracy. Experiment results demonstrate that, compared to the original model, our improved model reduces computational parameters and inference time by nearly half, with only a 1.5% decrease in accuracy.

articleTitle: Binary Neural Networks for Real-Time Structural Health Monitoring on Edge Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) is critical to ensuring the safety of civil structures. SHM has been mostly addressed through cloud/workstation solutions, but new approaches are also considering edge devices, whose proximity to data sources allows minimizing latency and bandwidth. Typical SHM methods demand extensive data processing and high computational resources, that cannot be sustained by edge devices. In this paper, we investigate the application of binary neural networks (BNNs) to the SHM problem, exploiting their efficiency and reduced computational cost, without too much degrading classification performance, which makes them a very promising solution for edge computing. Using the Z24 Bridge dataset, our results show that BNNs can achieve state-of-the-art accuracy while reducing model size by approximately 90×, energy consumption by a factor 14, with a 12× latency cut, allowing real-time operation on a Raspberry Pi 4 device.

articleTitle: Perceptual Picture Quality Improvement and Power Saving Using the Helmholtz-Kohlrausch Effect
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper we propose a novel algorithm based on the Helmholtz-Kohlrausch (HK) Effect which simultaneously improves the perceptual picture quality of an image and saves power. We use simple and compute efficient pixel processing which is easy to implement on hardware and have achieved an average power saving of 3.03% on StEM2 video keyframes with 77” OLED TVs.

articleTitle: Human Avatar Generation Using 3D Gaussian Splatting With a Focus on Non-Rigid Deformations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for reconstructing clothed humans based on 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). Applying static 3DGS to the dynamic problem of human reconstruction is challenging due to the complexity of non-rigid deformations and detailed representation of clothing. To address these issues, we optimized 3DGS to align with non-rigid transformations based on the Splatting Avatar technique. As a result, our method enabled the generation of novel view images with better PSNR accuracy compared to the Splatting Avatar method.

articleTitle: Verification of Internal Memory Readout by Voltage Fault Attack on Automotive ECUs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, the spread of electric vehicles have led to the increasing use of IT devices in vehicle operation control. ECUs (Electronic Control Units) refer to the control devices that control automobiles' operations, and their security issues have emerged as a result of their rapid spread. In this paper, we propose a voltage fault attack execution environment targeting microcontrollers for ECUs. We applied the proposed environment to a microcontroller for ECUs and succeeded in reading out the contents of the read-protected memory in it by the fault attack.

articleTitle: Microstructures-Metastructures Integrated Hybrid Adhesives for Wearable Sensors
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Precise regulation of crack propagation at bonded interfaces is essential for the development of high-performance adhesives. However, prior research has largely focused on either microscale or macroscale crack behavior. In this study, we introduce a hybrid adhesive that combines microarchitectures with macroscopic nonlinear cut designs, offering unprecedented control over adhesion. This combination allows for conformal bonding and simultaneous crack trapping at multiple scales, resulting in a more than 70-fold increase in adhesion strength, while directing crack propagation at the macroscale for controlled detachment. The skin adhesive patches are breathable, gentle on the skin, and provide exceptional strength and security, yet they can be easily removed. When integrated with nanomaterials or electronics, these patches can adhere securely to the skin for accurate monitoring of various physiological signals.

articleTitle: A Multimedia Interactive Presentation System Based on AIoT and RAG-Enabled Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a multimedia interactive presentation system, Gen-Presenter, that leverages Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)-enabled Large Language Models (LLM). The Gen-Presenter system integrates an edge-AI computing device with peripherals such as a camera, microphone, speakers, and display screen, in combination with a natural language processing (NLP) server. The system detects visitor activity through the camera, infers their age group, and uses this information to select appropriate slides and generate corresponding voice narration for interactive presentations. Experimental results show that Gen-Presenter, when responding to queries from users of different age groups, can select appropriate presentation slides and generating corresponding explanations, with performance closely matching human decisions. In terms of slide selection, the overall precision, recall, and accuracy were 0.87, 0.67, and 0.76, respectively. Additionally, the suitability rates for the generated age-appropriate text content across the three age groups exceeded 0.7. This demonstrates the system's success in delivering human-like slide explanations and interactive Q&A sessions.

articleTitle: EMG-Based Anomaly Detection for Evaluating Exoskeleton Impact on Muscle Strain
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This research explores the potential of a passive occupational shoulder-supporting exoskeleton in reducing muscle strain by employing anomaly detection on electromyography (EMG) signals. We analyzed EMG data collected from sensors attached to various muscle groups of participants performing manual lifting tasks both with and without the exoskeleton support. Using feature engineering and machine learning, specifically the Isolation Forest algorithm, an anomaly detection model was developed. The results show that the model is able to distinguish between normal muscle activity and anomalies indicative of strain. Our results demonstrate a significant reduction in the anomalies detected when the exoskeleton was used, indicating a decrease in muscle strain, compared to tasks completed without them. This study contributes to the understanding of how wearable assistive technology can be used to enhance worker safety and ergonomics in industrial settings, offering a proactive approach to reducing work related musculoskeletal risks.

articleTitle: Loss Based Byzantine Resilience for Decentralized Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Decentralized learning has gained attention for over-coming the disadvantage of centralized learning such as single point of failure and scalability. However, when there are faulty nodes or attackers (Byzantine nodes) in the network, and these nodes perform Byzantine attacks by sending abnormal models, the model may fail to converge. Existing defense methods against Byzantine attacks have been pointed out to fail when facing sophisticated attacks or an increasing proportion of Byzantine nodes. To address these issues, we propose a novel defense method based on loss function values. Each node calculates the loss values of both its own model and the models of neighboring nodes using its local data. If the difference between the two loss values exceeds a certain threshold, the model is used for aggregation. This defense method ensures that only models with generalization performance above a certain level are included in the aggregation process, effectively filtering out Byzantine models as well as low-performing models from benign nodes. Experimental results using the CIFAR-10 dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves better convergence speed and accuracy compared to existing methods, and it remains robust even as the proportion of Byzantine nodes increases.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Behavior Observation Network System Using Multiple LiDARs for Indoor Digital-Twin
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, digital transformation (DX) systems leveraging various digital technologies become a key focus for many organizations. In particular, digital twin is gaining attention within DX. The digital twin is a technology that replicates physical spaces in virtual spaces by sensing various states within those physical spaces. This technology is utilized for applications across a wide range of fields. The applications involve an indoor monitoring system that utilizes sensors for understanding human movement and the structural layout of indoor spaces. Existing research proposes methods for identifying and tracking individuals using cameras. However, these camera-based methods have the potential to violate privacy. On the other hand, privacy-preserving sensing methods utilizing LiDAR, which captures the three-dimensional structure of physical spaces as point cloud data, is considered to construct the digital twin. However, the LiDAR generates a large amount of point cloud data, which is difficult to be analyzed for achieving both real-time performance and high accuracy. Therefore, in this study, we propose a new system that generates three-dimensional spatial data to recognize indoor environments and human behavior by analyzing point cloud data collected from multiple LiDARs. Furthermore, by adapting a system design of edge computing, our system can analyze data from multiple LiDARs to achieve real-time tracking and identification of individuals with high accuracy.

articleTitle: A Cycle-Accurate Simulation Platform for NPU-DRAM Integrated Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The ever-increasing accuracy of artificial neural networks facilitates various applications in consumer electronic devices. Furthermore, neural processing units (NPUs) enable the real-time processing of neural networks by leveraging domain-specific hardware structures along with considerable on-chip buffers. Unfortunately, the data movement between NPU and off-chip memory (e.g., DRAM) can no longer be ignored; hence, it is necessary to accurately take the performance effect of off-chip memory into consideration, particularly at the architectural-level simulation. In this paper, we propose a configurable, cycle-accurate NPU simulation infrastructure that considers not only the latency effect as in the analytical modeling but also the memory bandwidth utilization. Our simulator reveals that the accurate simulation of off-chip memory captures higher latency compared to analytical modeling. Specifically, it demonstrates the total execution time increases of 19.2%, 2.8%, and 16.2% in ResNet-50, YOLOv3, and BERT, respectively.

articleTitle: Using Transfer Learning on Deep Learning Networks to Predict Channel Operating Margin
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The increasing demand for data-intense applications such as artificial intelligence, Internet of things (IoT), wearables, augmented reality and virtual reality has led to the need for the constant upgrade of data channels everywhere including in-server infrastructures and consumer electronics. These upgrades require carefully checking the signal integrity of connected (wired or wireless) devices. However, signal integrity analyses can be time consuming processes. Anything from solving 3-D electromagnetic models to performing time-domain analysis of channels can take several hours to a day or even longer. The advancements in CPU and GPU technology have helped but those advancements have been countered by the increased complexity of the components and channels being analyzed which are essential for the ever-increasing need for faster data rates and higher bandwidths. One avenue to decrease complex multi-channel analysis is to incorporate deep learning networks. After training, these networks would allow design space exploration of pre-layout designs and post-layout verification to be completed faster. In this paper, several deep learning networks are trained to look at various PAM4 eye diagrams and determine whether the channel will pass or fail the Channel Operating Margin (COM) without having to run the COM script and therefore allowing the designer to eliminate failing channels early in the design process. Results show that significant time savings can be achieved by using a retrained deep learning network over COM. This time savings translates into reduced design cycle development times.

articleTitle: Radiation-Hardened Triple Modular Redundant Serial Communication System Using Triple Communication Lines
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: An earthquake occurred in Japan has caused a nuclear meltdown at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant in 2011. Currently, a decommissioning work is planned at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant. However, the radiation intensity of the melted reactors exceeds 1,000 Sv/h. Since the radiation intensity is too severe to human, robots must be used for the decommissioning work. In order to remotely monitor and control the decommissioning robots, a radiation-hardened communication system is necessary. However, currently available very large-scale integrations (VLSIs) are vulnerable to radiation. The total-ionizing-dose tolerance is not sufficient. Therefore, we have been developing a radiation-hardened serial communication system with a triple modular redundant structure on an DE1-SoC field programmable gate array (FPGA). This paper presents the radiation-hardened communication system and its experimental results.

articleTitle: Proposal for an Exercise Web Application with Gamification for Obese Students
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this study, a web application was developed for university students to promote exercise habits and prevent locomotive syndrome. The application provides a simple exercise menu (one-leg stand, squat, heel raise, front lunge) and analyzes correct exercise posture in real time using posture estimation AI. In addition, gamification elements (objectives, quests, and interactions) were incorporated to encourage competition and interaction among students. The results of the experiment showed that obese students lost weight and thin students increased muscle mass, confirming the effect of exercise on health.

articleTitle: An In-Memory Computing-based Efficient Transformer Accelerator Using Stateful Matrix Multiplier for Voice Assistant Consumer Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Processing-in-memory (PIM) is designed to overcome data transfer bottlenecks by performing repeated data-intensive operations on the same die as the memory. In this study, we propose a new variable systolic array with stateful matrix multiplication based on the input memory word count. It showed a high performance in transformers, the basis for natural language processing (NLP) models. The implemented Transformer encoder can be applied to mobile application processors (APs) to accelerate sentence classification in call recordings or voice memo content tasks.

articleTitle: A Fast Block Partitioning Decision Method Using Luminance Textures for VVC Encoders
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The latest international video coding standard, Ver-satile Video Coding (VVC), achieves approximately double the compression efficiency over the conventional standard, High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC). However, it also significantly requires more encoding time due to the block partitioning in VVC. This paper proposes a fast block partitioning decision method using luminance textures for VVC to reduce the encoding time. The proposed method accelerates the encoding speed with low-cost calculations. The proposed method reduces the encoding time by 59.45% for 2K and 66.44% for 4K, with only 1.56% and 1.25% losses in coding efficiency. This method is effective for encoding with a practical computational complexity.

articleTitle: An Ising Machine-Based Hybrid Optimization Method Using Constraint Conversion and Correction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes an Ising machine-based hy-brid optimization method to solve combinatorial optimization problems, which consists of an approximate formulation process, an annealing process with an Ising machine, and a correction process. The approximate formulation and correction aim to improve the performance of the Ising machine. Computational experiments were conducted on the multi-dimensional knapsack problem (MKP) using an Ising machine. We compare the results with those of the proposed method and the conventional method and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Hardware-Friendly Quantization via Outlier Scaling in Convolution-Attention-Based Hybrid Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Hybrid networks that combine convolution and attention have achieved state-of-the-art performance in computer vision tasks. Quantization is a promising compression method to efficiently utilize these hybrid networks in resource-constrained consumer electronics like IoT devices. However, although many hybrid networks have been proposed, research on quantization dedicated to hybrid networks has not yet been actively conducted. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel hardware-friendly post-training quantization method. Initially, we observe significant outliers in the bottleneck blocks of hybrid networks, which result in severe accuracy degradation due to quantization. To effectively address these outliers, we propose not only a novel outlier scaling method but also an objective function-based power-of-two approximation method that replaces conventional floating-point multiplication with hardware-friendly shift operations. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, experiments were conducted on the ImageNet-1k dataset using a representative hybrid network, MobileViT. Our proposed method significantly mitigated the accuracy drop with a small parameter increase at the same model size compared to existing quantization methods.

articleTitle: Low-Light Image Enhancement and Color Correction Using a Contrast-Driven Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to low-light image enhancement and color correction, utilizing a contrast-driven neural network. The proposed method employs a Contrast Encoder to identify and learn the low-light regions within images, followed by an Enhancement Decoder Network that enhances image quality specifically within these areas. To prevent issues like color distortion and over-correction, training is conducted using the Low-Light (LOL) Dataset and an Underwater Image Dataset, which provide a variety of challenging low-light conditions. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method effectively improves both illuminance and contrast when compared to existing approaches. Moreover, the generated images exhibit high quality, demonstrated by low scores on the Blind/Referenceless Image Spatial Quality Evaluator (BRISQUE), which indicate better-perceived image quality.

articleTitle: Random Number Generators and Sphere Sampling for High-Level Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Randomized algorithms are often utilized for applications such as path planning in autonomous mobile systems. FPGAs are considered a solution candidate for the computation to cope with the heavy load caused by the huge number of iterations. This paper presents our designs of Random Number Generators (RNGs) for FPGAs, including Mersenne Twister, Combined Tausworthe, and Sphere Sampling. We utilize High-Level Synthesis (HLS) design tools for productivity and tune the code considering the resultant architecture for performance.

articleTitle: Proposed Integrated Control Mechanisms Between Computing and Network Resources by Online Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In the IoT mature stage, a huge number of devices are deployed in various fields. Particularly, in consumer electronics fields, various purpose devices are deployed, e.g., for energy management, crime prevention, monitoring home electric appliances, etc. In this situation, these devices are associated with servers through heterogenous networks. Conventionally, the architectures for distribution processing have been discussed actively. e.g., Common Object Request Broker Architecture (CORBA). However, these architectures did not consider transfer network types and their resources. This paper proposes the architecture of resource management, considering networking and computing resources to connect massive number of devices and servers. It proposes a framework of the architecture and mechanisms for enabling architecture. Then, it describes a use case based on this architecture, and discusses its implementation.

articleTitle: Assessing Moral Decision Making in Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly permeate diverse industries, it has become crucial to comprehend the mechanisms underlying their moral decision-making processes. Existing studies on the moral decision-making processes of LLMs have been limited in their evaluation of ethical theories. The datasets utilized in these studies relies on human preferences, which introduces a set of inherent flaws. This paper utilizes different prompting styles to assess LLMs on moral ethical questions, addressing challenges associated with human preferences. The contributions include a dataset with human preferences and LLM preference on diverse ethical theories namely commonsense, virtue ethics, justice and deontology. We scrutinize these ethical decision-making on GPT-4 Bard, Mistral, and LLaMA2 to create a broad understanding of ethical reasoning capabilities across different platforms. We used baselines metrics such as accuracy, and F1-score for the evaluation purposes. GPT4 demonstrated a remarkable alignment with human ethical judgments, achieving an average accuracy of 81.5%. By including AI-generated justifications for ethical decisions, our study not only enhances the transparency of AI decision-making but also provides a foundational understanding of how LLMs conceptualize and apply ethical principles.

articleTitle: 3D Printed THz Demultiplexer Circuits Using Suspended-in-Air Grating Couplers
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Integrated photonic circuits are essential for advancing terahertz (THz) communications. This study leverages 3D printing to create high-quality integrated components with a high refractive index contrast, crucial for efficient demultiplexing of THz channels within Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) modality. We have developed compact, low-loss waveguides, bends, couplers, and fiber Bragg gratings using polypropylene filaments. The precision of our dual-nozzle printer allows for the seamless integration of these subcomponents into functional devices, such as single-channel drop filters that support data rates of up to 6 Gbps per channel at 140 GHz carrier. This research underscores the potential of suspended-in-air integrated circuits for efficient analog signal processing in THz communications.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Conical Spiral Sensor for Partial Discharge Detection in Oil-Filled Transformers
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This work proposed a low-profile conical spiral antenna for partial discharge detection in oil-filled transformers. The antenna consists of two spiral strips on the inclined surface of a conical dielectric. Compared with other wideband spiral antenna used for UHF partial discharge detection, the proposed antenna has a similar frequency response while improving pattern so that it has good reception ability in any direction. This improvement allows the detection system to collect more signals and increase the accuracy of predicting system health.

articleTitle: A Conversational Interaction Framework Using Large Language Models for Personalized Elderly Care
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As the aging population grows, worries regarding loneliness are increasingly prevalent, especially among senior adults living alone. This isolation can adversely affect both physical and emotional health. This study presents a large language model (LLM)-based voice interaction framework to alleviate loneliness and promote healthy living among older adults living independently. The system integrates speech recognition and synthesis technology with large language models to provide personalized, voice-driven interactions for senior users. Essential elements include medication reminders, fostering healthy dialogue, and preserving contextual discussions. In the future, we aim to improve consumer convenience via the integration of smart homes and mobile devices.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of a JPEG Encoder for Efficient Web Debugging of an Unmanned Mobile Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We are developing an SoC FPGA-based unmanned mobile vehicle for an FPGA design contest. A web server is running on the vehicle, and the input video from the camera and the white line extraction result video can be checked on the client PC. We have implemented a JPEG encoder on an FPGA to improve the processing performance and debugging efficiency of the operation control. The automated driving system was mounted on AMD's Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC and the performance of the software and hardware implementations of the JPEG encoder was compared, showing the effectiveness of the hardware implementation.

articleTitle: Real-Time Object Detection Using Low-Resolution Thermal Camera for Smart Ventilation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We propose an ultra-lightweight deep learning model for real-time object detection in smart ventilation systems using low-resolution thermal imaging sensors. The proposed FLARE (Fast and Lightweight Architecture for Real-time Estimation) model employs a Spatial Denoise Block, TOI (Thermal Object Insertion) data augmentation, and a composite loss function. Implemented on an STM32 MCU,FLARE showed an 84.28% performance improvement, 53.37% speed increase, and over 40% Flash and RAM reduction compared to existing lightweight methods. On Raspberry Pi 4B, it achieved higher mAP (0.72% improvement) than YOLOv8n, with 1/118 memory usage and 12.05 times faster execution speed.

articleTitle: Distraction-Free Functions for Facilitating Cognitive Mapping During Scroll Reading on a Tablet
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The incredible advancements in digital technology have revolutionized how we transmit and access information. This has made gathering knowledge from digital texts easily accessible and has become a widely embraced practice today. On the other hand, many studies said that the comprehension level of reading texts on a screen is inferior to that of reading paper texts. In this paper, we focus on reducing the difficulty of forming a cognitive map in scroll reading on a screen, which is considered one of the causes of this inferiority. To address this, we propose an e-book reader user interface that facilitates the formation of cognitive maps without distraction when scrolling texts on a tablet. We also describe the evaluation method of the proposed functions.

articleTitle: Robot Tele-Operations with 5G NR Sidelink
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: 5G New Radio (NR) sidelink, introduced in 3GPP Release 16, facilitates direct device-to-device communication, enabling robots to operate independently of traditional cellular networks. As industries increasingly adopt robotic solutions for remote operations, the need for reliable, low-latency communication has become paramount. This paper presents an experimental demonstration of robot tele-operations utilizing 5G NR sidelink technology. Our demonstration showcases the effectiveness of NR sidelink in enhancing robotic tele-operation by integrating real-time video streaming capabilities. We performed a series of experiments in dynamic environments to evaluate the responsiveness, video quality, and operational efficiency of robotic systems utilizing 5G NR sidelink. The results indicate that the low latency and high data rates provided by 5G NR sidelink significantly improve the operator's ability to control robotic systems, particularly in challenging scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on Acquisition and Validation of Unconscious Interest Based on Gaze Estimation Using a See-Through HMD
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Recently, many companies have been focusing on advertising as a part of their marketing activities, and there are many advertising media around us. This research aims to estimate interests that users are not yet aware of in a world where such advertisements are common, in real-time, using a see-through head mount display (HMD) that can be easily worn. We focused on the gaze estimation technology in the see-through HMD, and attempted to develop and demonstrate an interest acquisition system.

articleTitle: ioConnect: A Universal Embedded SDK for Connecting Smart Devices to Web3
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: An embedded software development kit (SDK) is an essential component in an IoT ecosystem. The existing embedded SDKs, while facilitating developers to build centralized, cloud-native IoT applications, are not able to meet the increasing requirements of connecting smart devices to Web3, in particular decentralized physical infrastructure networks (DePINs). To close this gap, we present a universal, open-source embedded SDK called ioConnect in this paper. Built upon the emerging technologies such as the platform security architecture (PSA) and self-sovereign identity (SSI), ioConnect is the first embedded SD K that allows developers to connect smart devices to a decentralized network and create rich and trustworthy device-to-device and device-to-person relationships. ioConnect is designed with a layered architecture coupled with a flexible configuration utility and is able to support a wide range of smart devices with different processing capabilities and memory footprints. Our extensive performance evaluations on two resource-constrained smart devices demonstrate viability and effectiveness of ioConnect when used in practice.

articleTitle: ID-Flow: Leveraging Voice Identity for Generalizing Audio Deepfake Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As deepfake generation models advance, significant research has focused on the deepfake detection task; however, challenges in model generalization persist. This paper introduces a novel audio deepfake detection method that achieves robust performance by leveraging voice identity information. Employing contrastive learning with voice identity features as additional data, the proposed approach demonstrates strong adaptability, effectively detecting data generated by unseen models during training. These findings demonstrate that effectively utilizing voice identity enables audio deepfake detection algorithms to be applied in real-world scenarios without the need for additional labeling efforts. Experimental results confirm the robustness of the proposed algorithm against variations in both audio deepfake generation models and domains.

articleTitle: Selective Error Correction for Activation in Large Language Model Training
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In Large Language Model (LLM) training, acti-vations constitute a significant portion of memory usage, and memory-side errors occurring in activations can lead to training failures. In this paper, we propose a lightweight but effective error correction method to mitigate the impact of such errors. The proposed approach leverages the inherent error tolerance of activations by selectively protecting only a subset of significant bits. Specifically, based on bit-flip error analysis, six sensitive bits are identified, and error-correcting codes (ECC) are applied exclusively to these bits. Compared to ECC implemented in HBM2, the proposed method exhibits 5.4 times lower parity overhead and 4 times higher area efficiency, while maintaining training performance in error-prone environments.

articleTitle: Programmable Power Management Integrated Circuit for IoT Devices Powered by Multiple Energy Harvesting Sources
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes the PPMIC-Iot, a power management system targeting the Internet of Things (IoT) capable of simultaneously using multiple energy sources. With the rapid growth of the IoT, especially in off-grid environments, efficient power management is crucial for reliable operation. The proposed framework supports battery charging, real-time parameters monitoring, and continuous switching between energy sources. Silicon validation of the primary sub-circuits demonstrates efficient voltage detection, stable biasing, reliable ADC performance, and effective data communication. The system's adaptability and performance make it suitable for a wide range of IoT applications, particularly those relying on energy harvesting.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Influence of Object Detection Models and Dataset Selection on Traffic Accident Prediction Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Traffic accidents pose significant social and economic challenges, making effective accident prediction systems essential. Traditional machine learning methods often struggle to capture the complex, nonlinear patterns in visual accident data. Recent advancements suggest that deep learning offers a promising solution to this challenge. These vision-based systems rely on object detection as a foundational step, identifying key entities in traffic scenes captured by cameras to improve prediction accuracy. Despite its importance, the impact of object detection accuracy on overall accident prediction effectiveness remains underexamined. This study investigates this relationship through cross-dataset analysis. Experimental results show that object detection accuracy directly impacts accident prediction performance, with training dataset choice playing a critical role. Enhancing model generalization is essential to stabilizing accident prediction systems.

articleTitle: DA-SAM: A Defect-Aware Segmentation Model for Industrial Product Inspection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The standard procedures for detecting industrial product defects typically involve collecting images, labeling defects, and training models through supervised learning. This process is often time-consuming and laborintensive. To address these challenges, we introduce the Defect-Aware Segment Anything Model (DA-SAM), a defect detection tool designed to simplify the conversion of box labels into segmentation annotations, thereby reducing labeling time and enabling efficient zero- or few-shot learning. First, we fine-tune the SAM model using LoRA and fine-grained bounding boxes to generate defect masks. The model is then trained on several public datasets. A two-stage training approach distinguishes defects from the background and addresses defect variations. Experimental results demonstrate that DA-SAM performs effectively on both the MVTecAD public dataset and the self-collected SPTD dataset.

articleTitle: Counting of Pear Flower Buds in Images by Judging Acquisition Conditions and Matching Keypoints
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We propose a method for accurately counting pear flower buds from worm's-eye view images acquired from a mobile ground-based camera system, using acquisition condition judgment and keypoint matching. To develop this method, we considered the following two issues. First, the appearance of flower buds acquired at each time point varies with the illumination and camera parameters. In this case, using a single detector of flower buds frequently reduces the count accuracy. Second, the extent of overlap in the camera field of view among acquisition time points varies with the camera system setting. In this case, the counting of identical flower buds is duplicated if only the detection process is performed at each time point. To accurately count flower buds, the proposed method detects the candidate flower buds in the worm's-eye view images acquired at each time point using a suitable detector selected by the acquisition condition judgment and identifies identical flower buds using keypoint matching in image pairs between time points. Experimental results demonstrated that our method counts flower buds more accurately than the comparative methods that use a single detector.

articleTitle: Product Recognition for Inventory Management Using Spatial Partitioning in a Multi-Camera System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Recent advancements in deep learning have significantly improved object detection capabilities. However, accurately recognizing objects in environments with complex occlusions remains a challenge. For instance, detecting densely packed items on shelves in unmanned stores presents difficulties even for the most cutting-edge deep-learning object detectors. To address this issue, we propose a deep learning-based inventory management system tailored for multi-camera unmanned stores. The proposed method utilizes a Voronoi diagram-based ground plane localization technique along with regions of interest (ROI) obtained by using image difference. A weighted voting algorithm is employed to ensure an accurate inventory check. This approach outperforms conventional ROI detection methods by 10.45% in terms of recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Consumer Electronics Security in Smart Homes with t-SNE Feature Selection and Seagull Optimized Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This work presents a t-SNE-based feature selection and Seagull Optimized Deep Learning Model to improve consumer electronics security in smart homes. Optimized using the Seagull Optimization Algorithm (SOA), the suggested Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model showed exceptional performance with an accuracy of 92% in identifying cyber risks. The model routinely exceeded in both accuracy and loss measures when tested against conventional machine learning and deep learning models. T-SNE helped to choose important criteria that provide strong identification of harmful activity. Our method presents a major development in smart home security and a dependable instrument for reducing cybersecurity threats in a linked world.

articleTitle: An Efficient Reconfigurable Parameterized Convolutional Neural Network Accelerator on FPGA Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient reconfigurable parameterized convolutional neural network (CNN) accelerator designed for FPGA platforms. The core of the accelerator allows flexible adjustments of input channel parallelism (Pc) and convolution filter parallelism (Pn) to meet the needs of various CNN models, optimizing both resource utilization and computational efficiency. The architecture is applied specifically to infrared (IR) and visible light (VI) image fusion, enabling real-time processing on an FPGA with significantly reduced latency. Experimental results demonstrate that the accelerator reduces latency to 192 ms while maintaining high image quality, achieving efficient image fusion on the FPGA platform.

articleTitle: A Point Cloud Downsampling Method Balancing Global and Local Shapes for 3D Object Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) spatial recognition using point cloud data imposes substantial communication and computational burdens due to the high-density data. Downsampling is commonly employed to reduce data volume but often struggles to balance the preservation of the overall structure and the retention of detailed areas, leading to accuracy degradation in tasks like object classification. Some methods consider downstream processing but prioritize overall geometry, which may result in the loss of local details. We propose a balanced downsampling method that preserves the overall shape while increasing point density in critical regions to maintain finer details. Based on the deep learning framework SampleNet, our method integrates Average Voxel Grid Sampling (AVG) and a modified Farthest Point Sampling (FPS') thereby creating balanced training point clouds. This approach reduces processing time while improving classification accuracy. Specifically, our method achieves a 1.23% improvement in classification accuracy at larger downsampling sizes (250–1000 points) compared to SampleNet, while maintaining similar processing times. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in addressing accuracy degradation in 3D point cloud classification tasks.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Sparse Matrix Vector Multiplication with Small-Scale Matrix Element Router
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Sparse Matrix Vector multiplication (SpMV) is a fundamental operation in various computational science applications, characterized by a significant degree of inherent parallelism. Recent FPGA-based SpMV accelerators employ routing architectures such as crossbar switch or 2D-mesh network-on-Chip (NoC) to efficiently map matrix non-zero elements to their corresponding vector elements. The scale of these routing archi-tectures, however, serves as a key constraint on the attainable parallelism in FPGA-based SpMV accelerators. In this paper, we describe two approaches aimed at reducing the size of NoCs to exploit greater parallelism while suppressing the increase of hardware resource usage. In a previous work, each node in NoCs equipped multiple elastic buffers to prevent routing stalls, which was the main factor to increased resource usage. Our first approach replaces the elastic buffers to simple data registers to minimize the circuit size, while the second approach introduces ping-pong buffering to improve routing performance. Experimental results show that our approaches achieve 1.3 × to 1.7 ×throughput improvement over the previous work with less increase of resource usage.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Approach for Vehicular Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Vehicular safety is essential to protect drivers, passengers, and pedestrians from accidents caused by human error, environmental factors, or mechanical failures. Identifying mechanical failures is more critical for autonomous vehicles and fleets due to the absence of a human that typically detects abnormal behavior. This paper proposes a reliability and safety evaluation system that monitors impending failure modes on critical mechanical components such as drivetrain, suspension, and steering assemblies, providing real-time health data to users and fleet operators. Such a system is crucial for advancing vehicular safety, building public trust, and promoting the adoption of autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Low-Power High-Accuracy Time Synchronization Using PPI for Bluetooth-Based IoT Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a low-power, high-accuracy time synchronization system for Bluetooth-based communication. Building upon our previous research on MicroSync, this system achieves high precision by utilizing the programmable peripheral interconnect (PPI) of nRF52840 for communication timing detection and hybrid timer synchronization. PPI is a hardware feature that enables peripherals to directly cooperate without involving the CPU, thereby eliminating unstable delays caused by interrupt-based implementations. Hence, the proposed method achieves a time synchronization accuracy of 107.6 ns with a standard deviation of 122.7 ns at a power consumption of 244.1 μW. This represents a 60.5% improvement in synchronization accuracy compared to MicroSync without increasing power consumption. By leveraging PPI, the proposed method demonstrates high synchronization accuracy while maintaining energy efficiency, making it suitable for Bluetooth-based IoT systems that require both low power and high precision.

articleTitle: Flexible Uber Fetch Shader Architecture for Fluid Gaming Experience
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: When running mobile games on RDNA-based GPUs, micro-stutters may occur due to late resource bindings. Vulkan's Graphics Pipeline Library (GPL) separates shading stages for separate compilation, enabling shader compilation during game loading and caching for subsequent use. To enable this, the shader compiler must insert a long instruction sequence, referred to as the Uber Fetch Shader for the Vertex Input Interface, to decouple the vertex buffer format from the vertex attribute fetch code. We propose a novel software/hardware hybrid Vertex Input Interface. This solution improves overall performance and gaming experience during gameplay by reducing compilation time overhead by 16.68% and reducing compilation count by 13.5%.

articleTitle: Log Parameter Anomaly Detection System: Evaluating Accuracy with Noisy Training Data
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In system development, frequent updates often result in daily issues, increasing the demand for automated error analysis. Our research focuses on anomaly detection based on parameter combinations within text logs. Previous studies have reported high accuracy under conditions where only relevant logs were included in the training data. However, in real-world operations, it is highly likely that irrelevant noise logs will be present in the training data. Therefore, we investigated the robustness of the parameter log anomaly detection model by introducing various noise ratios. As a result, we confirmed that even with 11.1% noise log contamination in the dataset, the accuracy remained unchanged. Additionally, in comparison to previous studies, we observed improved anomaly detection accuracy for Value parameters with overlapping ranges across different combinations, achieving an F1-Score of 1.0. This improvement can be attributed to the increased variety of logs in the training data, which enhanced the performance of both the tokenizer and the AI model.

articleTitle: Enhancing Thermal Infrared Object Detection Using SimAM-Integrated YOLOX for Improved Feature Representation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Object detection with thermal infrared images is vital for applications like autonomous driving in low-light and adverse environmental conditions. While TIRDet has improved thermal-only object detection through a Thermal-To-Visible (T2V) translation model, this module can suffer from information loss in certain scenarios. To address this, we propose enhancing the CSPDarknet53 backbone of YOLOX within TIRDet by incorporating SimAM, a parameter-free attention mechanism. SimAM enhances feature representation by inferring 3D attention weights based on an energy function inspired by neuroscience theories, without increasing model parameters. By strengthening feature extraction within the backbone, our approach compensates for the T2V module's information loss, thereby improving detection performance under challenging conditions. Experiments on the LLVIP and FLIR datasets demonstrate superior performance, underscoring the effectiveness of parameter-free attention mechanisms for advancing thermal object detection.

articleTitle: Inpainting the Degraded Area with Diffusion Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, diffusion models have gained prominence for their ability to generate high-quality images by reversing a stochastic diffusion process. Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs) have shown state-of-the-art performance in image synthesis, but their focus on removing Gaussian noise limits their application in cases where only partial image information is available. In this paper, we propose a novel adaptation to the DDPM framework that replaces the conventional denoising process with an inpainting process. Our approach progressively removes random pixels, setting them to zero at each timestep instead of adding noise. The reverse process reconstructs the original image by filling in the missing pixels. To demonstrate the feasibility of this method, we conducted a prototype experiment using a subset of the CelebA-HQ dataset, training the model on 128 images. Initial results indicate that our method is capable of reconstructing images effectively, even with limited data, suggesting potential for future work in image restoration and enhancement tasks. However, challenge such as low diversity during sampling process remains, which will be addressed in subsequent research.

articleTitle: ObjectBlend Data Augmentation Technique for Resolving Dataset Imbalance in Vision Inspection Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We propose ObjectBlend, a novel data augmentation technique that addresses the issue of class imbalance in the field of vision inspection. ObjectBlend analyzes the class ratio within the dataset and replaces objects of majority classes with those of minority classes to achieve the desired class ratio. The experiments were conducted by applying ObjectBlend to YOLO methods to detect micro-LED defects during vision inspection in the manufacturing process of micro-LED TV panels. As a result of the experiments, the proposed method significantly improved performance compared to other data augmentation techniques. Specifically, in terms of mAP50-95, the performance increased from 0.1988 to 0.9147 for YOLOv3-tiny, from 0.7211 to 0.9016 for YOLOv5n and from 0.7649 to 0.9081 for YOLOv8n.

articleTitle: Improving Inter-protocol Friendliness Through Revision of Copa Competitive Mode and Estimation of BBR Behaviors Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In the last decade, several influential congestion control algorithms (CCAs) have been devised for yielding high performance over the Internet. Among them, BBR, a CCA developed at Google in 2016, aims at attaining the optimum operating point reaching both the maximum throughput and minimum round-trip time simultaneously. Again, Copa, a delay-based congestion control assuming Markovian packet arrival has been developed at MIT and was first reported in 2018. Since BBR and Copa are likely to be among the major CCAs on the Internet in the coming days, it is important to ensure mutual friendliness between these two types of flows. However, that is often impossible due to the aggressive nature of BBR. To support scenarios where flows of different types share the same bottleneck link, Copa provides a specific operating mode, called competitive mode. However, even in competitive mode, while competing with BBR for network resources, Copa performance is adversely affected. In this paper, we therefore, propose a novel mechanism to improve the competitive mode of Copa. Also, using machine learning, we estimate the behavior of a BBR flow that competes for bandwidth with a Copa flow over the same path. Experiments using iPerf servers show that our proposed scheme improves the throughput of Copa by up to more than 700% when deployed together with BBR. This improvement leads our proposed scheme to achieve much higher friendliness with BBR than original Copa.

articleTitle: A Proposed Depth Camera-Based Gait Monitoring System for Stroke Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Stroke, a leading cause of death, is characterized by sudden brain function impairment. Early detection through continuous monitoring is crucial to reducing risks and complications. We propose a stroke detection system using depth-based cameras and deep learning to monitor gait and detect stroke onset. Gait data were collected from post-stroke patients and healthy individuals using Microsoft Azure Kinect DK. The preprocessing included outlier removal, interpolation, and smoothing to ensure data quality. Gait features such as joint angles were analyzed with a convolutional neural network, achieving 75% accuracy and an F1-score of 0.76. Despite privacy and data security challenges, positioning this technology as a public health measure may improve acceptance. Our findings demonstrate its potential for non-intrusive stroke detection in smart homes or healthcare settings.

articleTitle: Jitter Modeling for High-Speed Interconnects Using Segment-Based Statistical Analysis for PAM4 Signaling Scheme
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper highlights jitter modeling using a segment-based link analysis algorithm for PAM4. The statistically based approach examines the ISI data dependent jitter to predict the system performance. Signal integrity is essential in high-speed data transmission used in consumer electronics. In the link analysis technique, aggregate PDFs are obtained through a series of mean and convolve operations, for both pre- and post-cursor segments. The final voltages are grouped into bins using hashmaps to optimize the calculations and data sizes.

articleTitle: Autonomic Nervous System Indicators of Love: Evaluation of Matching of Marriage Partners Using Heart Rate Correlation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Japan's declining birth rate and reduced formation of couples has become a serious social issue. This study aims to identify factors contributing to successful couple matching by analyzing heart rate data from participants in a matchmaking event. 16 participants (8 men and 8 women) attended a 2-hour event where their heart rates were continuously measured during activities such as watching a short movie and participating in 1-on-1 and free talk sessions. After the event, participants selected up to three preferred partners. Pairs were categorized into “matching” (both selected each other as first or second choice), “non-matching” (one selected the other), and “others” (neither selected the other) groups. Correlation coefficients of heart rates were calculated for these groups. While heart rate synchronization during the movie viewing did not correlate with matching success, the “matching group” exhibited the highest heart rate synchronization when the analysis was conducted across all sections of the short movie viewing and 1-on-1 dialogue. This suggests that overall heart rate synchronization may indicate emotional compatibility and could serve as a new indicator in future matchmaking events.

articleTitle: Realization of Wafer-Scale VLSI Using Optical Configuration Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In situations where many very large scale integrations (VLSIs) are integrated together, communication between chips disturb performance improvement. In general, communication between two chips is very time and power consuming. Therefore, we are considering ways to improve performance by building a huge-size VLSI and replacing chip-to-chip communication with inside chip communication. However, realizing of the wafer-scale VLSI is difficult because wafer-scale VLSI must have defect regions. Therefore. we are considering to realize wafer-scale VLSI using optical configuration architecture which is programmable device. In this paper, we have evaluated the delay time when implemented avoiding defects, and discuss the realization of wafer-scale VLSI. Also, we report a new RHORGA-VLSI with four clock distributions.

articleTitle: Efficient QUBO Formulation for Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: To support the rapid proliferation of IoT devices, non-uniform multiple access (NOMA) admission control appears as a promising technology. Indeed, through spectrum reuse, it allows more devices to communicate than the traditional orthogonal frequency-division multiple access scheme of 4G. Previous research has shown that the NOMA allocation problem can be formulated into a maximum independent set problem, which is NP-hard. Recent advances in quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) solvers show promise in their capability to solve this kind of allocation problems efficiently. We explore various QUBO formulations to determine which is best-suited for the high-frequency requirements of the NOMA allocation problem.

articleTitle: Robot Path Planning for Monitoring Dynamic Environment by Predictive Uncertainty Minimization Using Gaussian Process Regression
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In environmental monitoring, traditional methods primarily focus on collecting as much spatial information as possible to construct a more accurate static model of the environment. However, these methods fail to account for the fact that environmental factors, such as temperature, can vary over time during monitoring, making it difficult for robots efficiently capture temporal dynamics of each region across the entire spatial area. This paper addresses these challenges by applying a spatiotemporal Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) model, which estimates not only the environmental conditions of unobserved regions but also their associated uncertainties based on observed data, considering time variations. Building upon this model, we propose a method called Predictive Uncertainty Minimization (PUM), which controls the robot's trajectory to minimize future uncertainties. Through simulation using the data set obtained in the real-world environment, we show that PUM consistently maintains lower uncertainty levels, reducing overall uncertainty by 7.91% and 9.25% compared to the method following a predefined path and the method continuously moving to the point with the highest uncertainty, respectively.

articleTitle: Research on Machine Learning-Based Curtailment Analysis for Optimal Operation of Wind Farm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Novel controllers have been introduced in energy systems to enhance efficiency and manage uncertainties in renewable sources. These controllers incorporate real-time meteorological and SCADA data for more accurate wind turbine output predictions. This paper presents a curtailment weighting control module using a CNN-BiLSTM model trained on data from the Dongbok wind farm. The objective is to minimize active power loss during curtailment using a sequential quadratic programming algorithm, focusing on improving prediction accuracy and operational efficiency. The system integrates a real-time simulation environment, including hardware-in-the-loop simulation. Communication between wind farm controllers, RTDS grid models, and the management system is via the Modbus TCP/IP protocol. Comparative analysis with traditional methods validates the proposed method's advantages. Real-time simulation results indicate that the curtailment weighting control module reduces power losses and improves operational efficiency. The proposed method achieved a power loss reduction of 2.5813 kWh compared to traditional PD control methods and demonstrated a 99.9% availability across all wind turbines during curtailment scenarios. This study highlights the importance of combining machine learning-based control with advanced strategies to address challenges in renewable energy integration and maintain a stable power supply.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Emotion Recognition Using Fusion of Multimodal Affective Data From Consumer-Grade Wearable ECG and Speech Sensors
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Emotion recognition has emerged as a significant interdisciplinary research topic across various fields, including physiology, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence. This work proposes a deep learning-based emotion recognition model to classify emotions using multimodal affective data, specifically electrocardiogram (ECG) signals and speech from consumer-grade wearable sensors. This system has the potential to monitor and detect anxiety, depression, and intervene in cases of harmful thoughts. Deep learning techniques are leveraged in this study to recognize emotions while individuals watch movies, utilizing data from consumer electronics-based wearable watches. A modified convolutional neural network (CNN) based YOLO (You Only Look Once) algorithm is employed to train the model on the fusion of multimodal affective data, combining ECG and speech. ECG and speech data are collected through a smart ECG measurement watch and a digital voice recorder watch. Our results show an accuracy of 81 % for recognizing emotions. The validation of different emotions classified is performed using spectral centroid (SC) and wavelet transform (WT) methods. The proposed model is compared with several state-of-the-art algorithms, including support vector machine (SVM), k-nearest neighbor (kNN), convolutional neural network (CNN), long short-term memory (LSTM), and YOLOv5 to analyze its performance. This paper investigates the potential of consumer electronics to support a real-time multimodal emotion recognition model, empowering individuals to easily monitor their mental well-being from the comfort of their homes for healthcare applications.

articleTitle: A Study on Joystick-Based Collision Avoidance Methods for Improving the Operational Convenience of Intelligent Wheelchairs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: As the global population ages, the application of advanced technology to assist the elderly in their daily lives is gaining significant attention. People with upper limb disabilities, especially those with tremors or muscle stiffness, often have difficulty operating traditional electric wheelchairs that use joystick-based controls. Therefore, there is a need for technology to assist the elderly and individuals with upper limb disabilities who have difficulty using these traditional control methods. In this study, we propose a joystick control system that combines a Low-Pass Filter (LPF), an eight-sector circular filter, and an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) to ensure stable movement at boundaries. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed joystick control system, experiments were conducted with users suffering from stroke and spinal disorders. The experimental results showed that collisions decreased by 43.18% and the target arrival time decreased by 14.23%. In addition, the Artificial Potential Field (APF) algorithm was applied to prevent subsequent collisions, allowing the wheelchair to safely navigate both static and dynamic obstacles. As a result, the system was found to be effective in reducing the risk of collision for users with upper limb disabilities and improving the operational convenience of wheelchair

articleTitle: Optimizing Customer Targeting Using Reinforcement Learning and Neural Networks for Adaptive Marketing Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Optimizing customer targeting in marketing is crucial for maximizing returns, yet traditional approaches often struggle to adapt to changing customer behaviors. This paper presents a reinforcement learning-based framework that models customers' spending inclinations as normal distributions to optimize targeting strategies. We introduce a novel mean-stat strategy, which leverages statistical confidence intervals to dynamically adjust exploration-exploitation trade-offs. Unlike traditional methods such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex>-greedy and decaying <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex>-greedy, which are used for comparison, the mean-stat strategy is mathematically proven to provide superior performance by efficiently identifying high-value customers. Additionally, a neural network-based approach using the cross-entropy method further enhances adaptability by learning complex patterns in customer behavior. Extensive simulations validate the effectiveness of these strategies, demonstrating the practical advantages of incorporating advanced learning techniques and mathematical rigor into marketing strategies.

articleTitle: Optimizing Construction Payment Systems Through Blockchain-Enabled Smart Contracts
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
